News.title: Wife ‘drugged by husband so other men could rape her’ in case branded Pelicot 2.0 dies ‘from injuries caused by abuse’
News.content:
A WOMAN who was allegedly drugged by her husband so that other men could rape her has reportedly died from injuries caused by the abuse.

The 39-year-old’s body was found on a waterbed covered in blood by her teenage daughter at their home in Marchtrenk, Austria.



The horrific case has been dubbed Pelicot 2.0 by prosecutors in reference to the Gisèle Pelicot case where a French woman was drugged and abused by her husband and dozens of other men.

Emergency services were called to the scene on June 25, where they found the husband intoxicated, according to 20 Minuten.



He reportedly told cops that his wife had died during rough sex, and cops did not initially suspect the 51-year-old of any wrongdoing.

But an autopsy revealed horrific, fatal injuries that suggested that her death was linked to something much more sinister.



When police searched the man’s mobile phone, they allegedly found a trove of incriminating evidence.

The day before his wife’s death, he is said to have looked up home remedies to incapacitate a person.

Investigators also believe he repeatedly let other men rape her over an extended period for €500 (£430) per time.

The man is also alleged to have referred to his wife as “dead meat” in text messages.



He was arrested along with a neighbour, who is accused of sexually assaulting the woman twice, including on the night of her death.

He is understood to have left the house before she died.

Disturbing texts between the men allegedly saw them discussing the abuse, as revealed by Austrian newspaper Krone.

The outlet said the husband sent his neighbour a photo of his unconscious wife on the night of her death.

In one text, he wrote: “I’ll get her properly drunk. Then you can have sex with her again. The way she was whining the other day was amazing.”



The neighbour responded: “She almost screamed. You cover her mouth again.”

He also thanked the man for “allowing me to use her”.

Another text confirmed that the wife did not consent to the act, with the husband writing: “She’s not participating willingly”.

He also wrote: “If it worked, if I had date rape drugs, I would regularly make her available for you to rape.”

Several more suspects are currently under investigation.



he allegations have drawn immediate parallels to the Gisèle Pelicot case.

The high-profile French trial saw Pelicot’s husband, Dominique, drug her for nearly a decade and invite dozens of men to rape her while she was unconscious.

Brave Gisèle, who waived her anonymity, became a symbol of resistance after revealing she had no memory of the assaults and had been abused by at least 72 men.

That landmark trial exposed a sprawling network of men recruited online, a vast archive of videos and photos documenting hundreds of assaults.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It also revealed a sick grooming pattern in which Pelicot’s husband mixed powerful sedatives into her food and drink.



That case, which concluded with sweeping convictions in December 2024, set a stark legal and cultural benchmark in France.

News.title: Man, 39, arrested over ‘assault’ after funeral of Middlesbrough A66 crash victim, 17, was ‘disrupted’
News.content:
FUNERAL ARREST Man, 39, arrested over ‘assault’ after funeral of Middlesbrough A66 crash victim, 17, was ‘disrupted’

A MAN has been arrested on suspicion of assault at a funeral held for one of the young men who died in the A66 crash.

A 39-year-old has been arrested after reports of a disturbance at the service for Cole Worthy.



He died in a head-on collision with police on the A66, which also killed two armed officers.

The Teesside Crematorium service for 17-year-old Cole was disrupted today and police responded to reports of a disturbance inside.



Superintendent John Wrintmore from Cleveland Police said: “At around 12.30pm on Wednesday September 9, police swiftly attended to Teesside Crematorium following reports of a disturbance during a service taking place inside.

“A 39-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of assault and has been taken to police custody.



“The service has since resumed. Officers will be in the area to provide reassurance.”

The family announcement for Mr Worthy’s memorial read: “In loving memory of Cole, our beautiful boy taken from us on 22nd August 2022.



“An adored son, brother, grandson, nephew, cousin. A loving boyfriend to Ruby and a cherished friend to many. Fly high Cole, forever 17.”

The funeral was on the same day as that of PC Matthew Blades, 37, which took place in Hartlepool.

He was an armed response officer in a marked police car which was hit head-on by a VW Passat in the early hours of August 22.

His colleague PC Tom Clough, 38, also died at the scene, and will be honoured in a separate service.

Hundreds of cops lined the streets in an emotional farewell to “superhero” PC Blades.



Heartbroken colleagues wiped tears from their eyes as his coffin – draped in the Union flag – was carried into a packed church.

Schools closed early for the previous funerals of some of the other young men who died, sparking a political row, but they remained open during the ceremony for Mr Worthy.

The five young men in the Passat were Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Jakub Matusiak, 23, and Makai Saddington, 18.

On Monday, teens were seen hanging from car windows as they gathered for the funeral of Theo Rae, a close friend of Mr Worthy.

Cleveland Police previously said the men in the Passat may have had links to organised crime.



An extra 200 specialist officers, including armed cops, were deployed to Middlesbrough from six other northern forces as the police tried to keep a lid on the escalating violence.

News.title: Met Police launches criminal probe into Reform party donations after undercover sting
News.content:
THE Metropolitan Police has launched a criminal investigation into Reform UK following allegations that the party breached donation rules.

A full inquiry has been launched after an undercover sting from Channel 4 appeared to show two senior figures arranging for a US firm to fund three polls earlier this year, costing £32,500.



James Orr, head of policy, and Dan Jukes, a senior aide to Mr Farage, both stepped back this morning amid an internal investigation.

Mr Farage insisted his party did not break any laws and denied that the party had taken cash from foreign donors.



He added that he “wasn’t even listening” when he met with the undercover reporters disguised as an American father and son looking to give money to the party.

The force has been assessing the allegations since the Channel 4 show was broadcast on Thursday.

A Met spokesman said: “Following a broadcast by Channel 4 News on Thursday, September 3, the Met received a number of reports relating to donations and polling involving a political party.

“Detectives have assessed the information provided and determined that there are potential offences requiring investigation.

“The potential offences are similar in nature to matters already under investigation by the Met’s Special Enquiry Team relating to donations made to the same political party. As a result, these matters will form part of that ongoing investigation.

“All allegations under investigation relate to potential offences under the Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000.



“As part of enquiries, detectives are seeking to obtain relevant footage relating to the broadcast on Thursday, September 3.

“Detectives continue to liaise closely with the Electoral Commission and Crown Prosecution Service as enquiries progress.”

Mr Farage dismissed the allegations as “a little local difficulty” and described the reports as “an exercise in entrapment”.

He told reporters: “The party has done nothing wrong, taken no illegal money. In fact no money was taken at all.

“What is more problematic is loose pub talk, including a couple of boasts that simply were not true.



“And whilst I’m aware that our people were pushed and pushed and pushed into saying these things, the comments were injudicious at best.

“Neither of these members authorised to act in that way.

“Accordingly, they’ve stepped down pending an investigation, and I emphasise again: Reform has broken no law.

“We take compliance around donations very, very seriously.”

Rival parties reported Reform to the police following the Channel 4 News investigation.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Party chair Lee Anderson told Sky News there was “no chance” the Reform UK officials would return.

A Reform UK Spokesman said: “Reform UK denies any wrongdoing and will fully cooperate with the investigation. We won’t be commenting further while a live investigation is underway.”

News.title: Richard Branson’s wife died from blood clot after ‘medics failed to give her medication’ – as doctor daughter speaks out
News.content:
TRAGIC DEATH Richard Branson’s wife died from blood clot after ‘medics failed to give her medication’ – as doctor daughter speaks out

SIR Richard Branson’s wife died from a blood clot after doctors failed to give her medication, an inquest heard.

Lady Joan Sarah Drummond Branson, 80, passed away in November last year at The Lister Hospital in Chelsea, West London.



She died following complications from a back injury she obtained as a result of a fall at the family home on Necker Island in the Caribbean.

Joan suffered a “massive” blood clot in one of her lungs, an inquest was told today.



The court heard Joan was admitted to the hospital on November 17 last year following a GP referral for “persistent” pain following the fall.

She had tripped over a pair of slippers by her bed and was “unable to get up” and was “in a lot of pain”.



Joan had a history of blood clots going back as far as at least 2010 and had previously taken blood clot jabs.

But while at the hospital, she was not offered Enoxaparin injections despite her medical issues, the court was told.

Dr Nevil Pavithran, who took over Lady Branson’s care, told the inquest she should have been given anti-coagulants within 12 hours of her admission to hospital.

Her daughter, Dr Holly Branson, expressed concern at her mother’s treatment but said she did not want to “attribute blame to any individual doctor”.



She questioned why Joan was not offered the medication after being admitted to hospital and said she “does not accept” her mum refused it.

Dr Branson said her mum was “accustomed to anti-coagulant (anti-blood clot) injections and never had difficulty with them”.

She explained Joan “used them extensively while flying and during previous hospital admissions” and always took the injections when advised.



Dr Branson added: “The suggestion she refused Enoxaparin due to prior pain or bleeding concerns is not consistent with her usual practice or attitude.”

She also said in a statement that while at her mother’s side during the first two days, Enoxaparin “was never offered”.

Dr Branson added: “Had I been aware she was not receiving Enoxaparin injections I would have been very concerned given her recent long haul travel and medical history.”



She also said Joan had not been given anti-clot stockings to wear for up to 48 hours after her admission to hospital and had to ask the nurses for some.

The consultant in charge of her care told the inquest he “deeply regretted” not having prescribed her clot-busting drugs.

Dr Inaki Bovill said a VTE assessment (Venous Thromboembolism assessment) “should have been carried out” and the medication should have been prescribed on her admission.

He said: “Yes it should have been done and should have been prescribed.

“It was a regret it wasn’t spotted by me that evening.”



Dr Basir Kunduzi, who was on duty at the Lister Hospital, was asked by the coroner whether he thought she should have been on anti-coagulant medication.

He accepted it was his responsibility to prescribe the drugs and told the court Joan should have been given the drugs.

When asked why she wasn’t, Dr Kunduzi said he wanted to organise a CT scan ensure there was no bleeding, which the medication could worsen.

He said he wrote on Joan’s records he had not given anti-clot drugs and believed any doctor who took over would review the decision.

Dr Kunduzi said he now realises “the importance of communication between team members” and has “changed” his team practice.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said the decision not to administer the anti-coagulants to would live with him for the rest of his life, adding: “I would like to express my deepest condolences to Lady Branson’s family”.

The inquest continues.

News.title: Travellers ordered to leave illegal site opposite UK’s top-secret nuclear weapons facility where 13 homes were built
News.content:
TIME TO GO Travellers ordered to leave illegal site opposite UK’s top-secret nuclear weapons facility where 13 homes were built

TRAVELLERS have been ordered to leave an illegal site opposite Britain’s top-secret nuclear weapons facility after building 13 static homes.

Dozens of families moved onto land opposite the Atomic Weapons Establishment (AWE) spot in Berkshire, despite a planning injunction.



The sprawling site is Britain’s largest of three locations where nuclear warheads are manufactured.

West Berkshire Council first ordered work to stop in November last year after a planning application was submitted.



But building work continued, with heavy machinery used to clear the land and create multiple additional plots.

A High Court injunction was then granted in December, banning further development and residential occupation.



Despite the order, the site continued to grow and by May this year there were at least 22 occupied pitches.

Multiple planning applications were later submitted but were described as invalid and incomplete.



Now High Court Judge Sylvia de Bertodano has rejected a bid by families to alter the injunction so they could remain while seeking planning permission.

The families had argued their rights under Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights should allow them to stay.

They also raised the welfare of children living on the site and offered to leave if a future appeal against planning enforcement failed.

But the judge said she could not allow the families to “ride roughshod” over the court’s previous order.

She said allowing them to remain would render the planning injunctions “entirely toothless”.



The judge said she was minded to order all families to leave by October 5.

One family will be exempt because they were living on their plot before the December injunction was served.

AWE had warned that the presence of people on the site was affecting its Off-Site Emergency Plan.



Judge de Bertodano said it was “clear” the situation could impact the safety of others.

A witness also warned caravans could not provide the same protection as brick-built homes during a nuclear emergency.

Locals had meanwhile been left “fearing for their safety” as the unauthorised development continued.

More than 600 people signed a petition demanding an immediate halt to construction and land development.

Residents claimed machinery was operating from 6am until almost midnight, causing noise, disruption and distress.



They also claimed there had been attempts to illegally access the residential park’s water and electricity supplies.

In a statement, residents said: “This situation has left our community feeling unsafe, anxious, and unprotected.”

They insisted the petition was not aimed at travellers because of their identity, but was about “legal compliance, safety, and environmental protection”.



West Berkshire Council said it understood how “distressing” the situation had been for nearby residents.

A spokesperson said the authority had gathered evidence and reports to support urgent escalation of the case.

The council also said planning enforcement was a civil process and it did not have powers to remove people from the land.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It had requested support from Thames Valley Police and Ministry of Defence Police over site activity and public safety.

Further rulings are expected by September 14, with the exact removal arrangements yet to be finalised.

News.title: Brits take five selfies before getting one they’re happy with
News.content:
SMILE AWAY Brits take five selfies before getting one they’re happy with

BRITS take an average of five selfies before landing on one they’re actually happy with, according to research.

The survey of 2,000 adults found while 18 per cent are generally satisfied with their very first shot, 32 per cent admitted they rarely get it right first time.



This leads to 35 per cent confirming their camera roll is packed with multiple versions of almost exactly the same picture.

When it comes to capturing the perfect memory, for 83 per cent, making sure everyone fits inside the frame is one of the biggest priorities.



The research was commissioned by Samsung to mark the launch of the Galaxy S26 FE with an enhanced 12MP front camera with a wider view and Photo Assist, giving users greater flexibility when capturing and editing photos and videos.

The research found other important ingredients for an ideal image, and potential reasons to retake, include getting everyone looking at the camera (77 per cent).

As well as capturing a natural moment (75 per cent), finding the most flattering angle (65 per cent), and getting the lighting right (63 per cent).

Whereas someone looking away from the camera (28 per cent) or blinking (29 per cent) are two of the biggest issues amateur photographers face when trying to get the perfect group shot.

A further 22 per cent have discovered only after taking the picture that someone has been partially cut out of the frame or completely hidden behind someone else.

This ratio changes depending on who is behind the camera, with Gen Z revealed as the biggest selfie perfectionists, taking an average of six shots before settling on one.



Dropping to five for Millennials, four for Gen X, and three for Boomers.

But the quest for the perfect group selfie can test everyone’s patience, as the average person is prepared to stand around for only three minutes while a friend repeatedly retakes a group shot.

But an impatient 26 per cent admitted they start getting irritated in under a minute, with the average irritation point being just four attempts.

There is usually one person in their friendship group or family who takes charge of the camera, according to 43 per cent.

TOP 10 REASONS BRITS RETAKE A SELFIE 1. They don’t like how they look

2. They don’t like their expression or smile

3. Someone is cut out, hidden, or they can’t fit everyone in

4. The angle isn’t flattering

5. The lighting isn’t right

6. Someone else’s expression or smile doesn’t look right

7. Someone else doesn’t like how they look

8. The background, framing, or composition isn’t right

9. Wanting a different pose or angle

10. Wanting more options to choose from

When not in control themselves, 19 per cent have insisted on seeing a picture before they’ll approve it.



Others (18 per cent) have at some point asked for another attempt because they didn’t like how they looked.

Gen Z are the fussiest generation, as 11 per cent admitted they have vetoed a picture altogether.

While the same number of all polled (11 per cent) have at some point kept everyone standing around while they tried to get a better shot.

And sometimes the maths simply doesn’t work, as 29 per cent have given up on taking a group selfie altogether because they couldn’t fit everyone into the frame.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Annika Bizon from Samsung said: “Our research shows that a top selfie frustration is missing people in the shot.



“Whether it’s a family gathering, holiday memory, or night out with friends, we’ve all taken endless versions of the same photo just to get everyone in frame.”

News.title: King Harald’s rapist grandson Marius Borg Høiby, 29, seen at funeral as shamed royal temporarily freed from house arrest
News.content:
CONVICTED rapist Marius Borg Høiby has been seen at his grandfather King Harald’s funeral after being temporarily freed from house arrest.

The disgraced 29-year-old arrived at Oslo Cathedral with his royal step-cousins alongside dozens of world leaders, including Prince William, at the funeral of Norway’s late leader.



Høiby was found guilty in June on two counts of rapes and assaulting his former girlfriend along with dozens of other offences.

He was sentenced to four years in prison but his lawyers filed for appeal leaving Hoiby on house arrest until a new trial next year.



Høiby is not directly related to the late Harald but is the son of new Queen Mette-Marit and stepson of King Haakon VIII.

He has been serving his detention at Skaugum, a royal residence in Norway.



As Harald’s health rapidly declined in recent weeks Høiby was allowed to temporarily ignore his house arrest on several occasions.

He was first seen in public visiting the National Hospital on Thursday, August 27, to be alongside Harald and relatives.

He also travelled to Bygdøy Royal Palace and the Royal Palace in Oslo on Friday, August 28, after Harald’s death.

On August 31, Høiby was a pallbearer and helped carry Harald’s coffin through the Royal Palace.

Høiby was only scheduled to remain on house arrest until September 7, but he was made to stay in detention as Oslo Police argued there was a “clear danger” Høiby could commit further offences.



The shamed royal was kept away from his parents – the new King and Queen of Norway – as he arrived at the funeral this morning.

He walked into the packed venue alongside his step-cousins, the daughters of Princess Märtha Louise before greeting Preses Olav Fykse Tveit and the Bishop of Oslo Sunniva Gylver.

Høiby’s defence attorney, Petar Sekulic, said ahead of the funeral: “He does not want any focus on [the rape convictions] in these days surrounding King Harald’s death.”



Harald died on August 28 at the age of 89.

He was Europe’s oldest living monarch and had been on the throne since 1991 but was put on royal “sick leave” after falling ill with a blood disorder.

The grand funeral procession started at the Royal Palace in the capital, before moving east towards Oslo Cathedral – where Harald married Queen Sonja in 1968.

The state service will be followed by a private burial in Norway’s royal mausoleum, beneath the castle church.

There are 30 royals, 17 non-royal heads of state and five prime ministers in the funeral procession.



The Prince of Wales is among those in attendance – in place of Charles – and Princess Anne who is the godmother of the new King of Norway.

Under royal precedent, the King doesn’t attend funerals of other heads of state.

Members of the royal families in Sweden, Monaco, the Netherlands, Belgium, Spain, Denmark, Luxembourg, Liechtenstein, Japan and Greece are also at the procession.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Before his death King Harald was still technically in the line of succession to the British Royal Family.

He was the great-grandson of Edward VII and his godparents included Queen Mary and her son George VI – who were the late Queen Elizabeth’s grandmother and father.

News.title: At least one dead & 20 passengers injured in horror train crash at level crossing after truck driver ‘blinded by sun’
News.content:
AT least one person has died and 20 passengers have been injured after a train smashed into a delivery truck at a level crossing and flew off the tracks in Poland.

Shocking images show the stricken train lying on its side as emergency workers scramble to tend to the wounded.



Deputy Infrastructure Minister Piotr Malepszak said that preliminary information suggested the crash happened after the truck driver was reportedly blinded by the sun.

A press officer for the Mazowian region police confirmed one person has died.



Among the injured were the drivers of the truck and the train, with the former getting trapped in his vehicle until firefighters managed to free him.

Four people were left seriously injured in the horror smash, which happened as the train travelled from the eastern city of Lublin to the northern port of Szczecin.

The collision occurred near the town of Przysucha, around 60 miles southeast of Warsaw at about 11.20am.

A fire service spokesman said: “The locomotive is on its side on the opposite track and some of the wagons are also on their side.”



The crippled train was made up of six carriages and was carrying around 120 passengers.

Two air ambulances were deployed to rush the injured to hospital.

All rail traffic on the line has been suspended until further notice.

A probe has been launched into the cause of the crash.



It comes just five days after another passenger train ploughed into a truck at a level crossing in Poland after the driver allegedly ignored a signal.

Footage shows the terrifying near-fatal crash between a 300-person passenger train and a lorry in the northern port city of Gdansk.

The large truck was caught between barriers on a level crossing after the driver reportedly ignored signals to wait on the road.

The driver attempted to move forwards and backwards to get off the tracks but failed to do so in time.



The fire service said it was alerted to the collision at about 12.30pm on September 3.

In June, three people were injured after two Polish passenger trains crashed and caused a carriage to derail.

Around 200 passengers were travelling on both trains when the horror impact occured.

News.title: Hero schoolboy, 11, saves baby sister, 1, in horror house fire after tumble dryer burst into flames
News.content:
Hero schoolboy, 11, saves baby sister, 1, in horror house fire after tumble dryer burst into flames

The Spruce family are fundraising for financial support after the horrific blaze, which is believed believed to have been the result of an electric fault with the family's four-year-old tumble dryer

View 3 Images Mum Samantha, 35, had told Harrison to get Isabelle while she helped the other children (Image: Reece Spruce / SWNS)

An 11-year-old boy carried his baby sister to safety after a tumble dryer burst into flames during his younger sister’s birthday celebrations.

‌



Harrison Spruce ran upstairs to get one-year-old Isabelle, after mum Samantha spotted smoke pouring from the utility room of their family home in Penkridge, Staffordshire. The family had been celebrating nine-year-old Pippa’s birthday when the blaze broke out on September 1, forcing Samantha and her four children to flee as flames tore through the property.

‌



Dad Reece Spruce, 35, said the family have now “lost pretty much everything”, with damage estimated at around £200,000.

‌



The self-employed carpenter said: “Thankfully, Sam and all four children got out safely. We’re incredibly proud of Harrison. He did what his mum asked, but it took a lot of courage for an 11-year-old to go upstairs during a house fire and bring his baby sister out.”

View 3 Images The kitchen and utility room was severely damaged (Image: Reece Spruce / SWNS)

Turkey wildfire: Residents evacuated as flames spread towards homes in Antalya READ MORE :

Samantha, 35, had told Harrison to get Isabelle while she helped the other children, including five-year-old Joey, out of the house.

‌



The blaze is believed to have started with an electrical fault involving the family’s Candy tumble dryer, bought from Argos for £280 around four years ago. The kitchen and utility room were badly damaged, while smoke and soot spread throughout the four-bedroom property.

The home is now uninhabitable and the family of six are staying with relatives, sharing one room while they wait for their insurance claim to progress and try to find temporary accommodation.

Reece said: “The family are OK, but my missus has cried a lot about it and I’m trying my hardest to just keep going. I’ve been working very hard as I’m self-employed and it’s the only income we’ve got coming in, so I’ve tried to stay normal, but it’s really hard and we still can’t believe what has happened.

‌



“The utility room and the kitchen have gone as they are all burnt out and while it was contained towards the back of the house, the whole house is full of soot and all the beds and the kids’ toys smell of smoke. We’ve lost pretty much everything.”

He believes the total cost of repairing the property and replacing damaged belongings could be a hefty cost. Reece said: “The fire damage itself was mainly in the kitchen and utility room, but the smoke damage has affected the entire house. If you add together the building work and the contents of the house, I think the damage could be around £200,000.

View 3 Images A GoFundMe page set up by Samantha’s sister has already raised more than £3,000 (Image: Reece Spruce / SWNS)

‌



“We believe the tumble dryer was the source because the washing machine is still largely intact, whereas the tumble dryer has completely disintegrated. We think perhaps a safety cut-off failed or something caused it to overheat but it wasn’t that old really.”

Reece said the family hopes what happened will encourage others to check electrical appliances and make sure their smoke alarms are working. He added: “You never imagine something like this happening to your family. One minute the children were colouring on Pippa’s birthday and the next they were getting out of a burning house.

“We want people to check their appliances and make sure their smoke alarms are working. If our experience makes another family think about fire safety, then something positive has come from it.”

‌



The family has contents insurance, but Reece fears their cover may fall short of the true cost of replacing everything damaged in the fire. He added: “You don’t think about the combined value of every bed, mattress, television, computer, games console, appliance, item of clothing, children’s toy and everything else you’ve accumulated over the years.

“A contents figure can sound like a huge amount of money until you’re suddenly faced with potentially replacing the contents of an entire family home."

"We’d urge people to actually go around their house and work out what everything would cost to replace. We thought we had enough cover, and we’ve now realised how easy it is to underestimate it.”

Article continues below

A GoFundMe page set up by Samantha’s sister has already raised more than £3,000 as the family tries to find somewhere suitable to live. Reece added: “When my sister-in-law suggested it, I wasn’t sure as we’ve always been a family who want to get on with our lives and don’t look for handouts and try to do things ourselves, so I was a little bit reluctant.

“However, my wife was saying how we need beds and other stuff, including clothing for the children as they’re going back to school, so we decided to go with it. We’re incredibly overwhelmed by what people have donated so far and by how many people have offered to help us.”

To donate, visit here.

News.title: PC Matthew Blades' family pay tribute to 'superhero' at funeral after police officer killed in A66 crash
News.content:
PC Matthew Blades' family pay tribute to 'superhero' at funeral after police officer killed in A66 crash

PC Matthew Blades, 37, made his final journey with the white floral tribute 'Dad' from his two young sons, as his widow, Sarah, stood alongside hundreds of officers and mourners at her husband's funeral

Funeral of PC Matthew Blades: cortège arrives at church

The family of a police officer killed in the A66 tragedy said a heartbreaking goodbye to their 'superhero' today.

PC Matthew Blades, 37, made his final journey with the white floral tribute 'Dad' from his two young sons at his funeral. His widow, Sarah, stood alongside hundreds of officers and mourners as her husband's Union Flag-covered coffin was carried into church.

In her moving tribute to her husband after his tragic death, she said: “Forever loved. Forever missed. Forever our superhero. Our Matt and Dad.” Standard bearers from every police force in the country raised and then lowered their flags.

The full police ceremonial cortege for PC Blades included four horses and Scottish pipers as it approached St Joseph's RC Church in his hometown of Hartlepool, Co Durham. The pipers played 'Amazing Grace' as former Cleveland Police colleagues, standing side by side, wiped away tears.

View 7 Images The tribute to PC Matthew Blades from his two young sons (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

About 1,000 officers lined the streets, many wearing the white ceremonial caps of the traffic patrols. Matthew was a much-loved member of the Matrix team of responders.

He tragically lost his life alongside his colleague PC Tom Clough, 38, when a VW Passat containing five youths struck their armed response vehicle head-on at high speed in the early hours of August 22, on the A66 near Middlesbrough. Many of their colleagues wore a special identity badge for the funeral displaying ''PC Blades 2443 PC Clough 3234'.

PC Blades, who had two sons aged six and eight, should have been coaching a youth team named in his honour this week, and enjoying the exploits of his beloved Manchester United.

View 7 Images Cleveland Police officers comfort each other outside the funeral of their colleague PC Matthew Blades (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Sarah and his family said he would be "loved beyond words, today, tomorrow, and always". Their two young sons were not seen among the mourners outside church today.

Lauren Somerville, chair of the Cleveland Police Federation, wiped away tears as colleagues carried the coffin inside. She praised the outpouring of grief and support for the two officers which showed '"how much they were loved".

View 7 Images Pall bearers carry the coffin of PC Matthew Blades into his funeral (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

She said: "Matty was described as a best friend, a father, a brother and a son by his family. There are no words powerful enough to describe exactly how the family feels. He was the heart of the family, and he will be loved beyond words, today, tomorrow and always.

"He would have been so incredibly proud and thankful for all the love and support given to the family. He is going to be missed more than words can ever say. His laughter and silly jokes made them smile even when they least expected it.

View 7 Images PC. Matthew Blades who gave his life in the line of duty (Image: North News & Pictures Ltd)

"He was a joker who brought light and laughter into every room. And now life feels unbearably quiet without him." She added that there was a "huge sense of pride, honour, and duty among Cleveland Police and officers across the country".

Ms Somerville, whose Federation set up a fund which raised £1.2m for the two A66 officers, added: "It is there especially for those who loved and worked with Matthew and Tom. They are standing shoulder to shoulder for Matthew and Tom and the rest of the country will be with them as well."

Ms Somerville said Cleveland Police received support from other forces following the crash and investigations into wider organised crime.

View 7 Images PC Blades died when a car going in the wrong direction hit a police car on the A66 near Middlesbrough (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

She said: “I knew they would come to help us, and that they would be honoured to do so at this time. Not just police officers, but the Federation; people have been desperate to come here and wrap their arms around us.”

Hundreds of mourners lined the streets for the service, which was attended by Cleveland Chief Constable Victoria Fuller, Tees Valley Mayor Ben Houchen, Cleveland Police and Crime Commissioner Matt Storey, and Policing Minister Sarah Jones.

‌



Prime Minister Andy Burnham also paid tribute. He told the Commons: "I also want to send our sympathies to the hundreds of people who will gather today at the funeral of Matthew Blades, including many serving police officers, and we send our thanks to them all for their service and their work to keep our communities safe."

View 7 Images The funeral cortege for PC Matthew Blades (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Outside church, Zara Lavender, 30, from Hartlepool, said: “I have come here to pay my respects to the officer, I thought it was important that people came out to show that.”

‌



James Masey, 20, a student, recalled the shock of hearing that PC Blades had lost his life. "I wanted to show my respects, it was such a horrific incident."

A former British Army soldier, who asked not to be named, explained why he came, saying: “You can see from the turn-out that people wanted to get together. These guys did not deserve what happened to them – the police have a hard enough job as it is.”

View 7 Images Police officers hug each other before the funeral of PC Matthew Blades at St Joseph's Roman Catholic Church in Hartlepool (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

‌



Family friend Ian 'Buster' Gallagher, a former footballer turned physiotherapist, wrote a touching tribute to PC Blades and his family in community newspaper Hartlepool Life.

He said: "I can’t describe how angry and frustrated I am for what happened but we all have to cherish and remember the times we spent with Matt. Sarah has been superhuman. I have seen her at close hand every day showing immense strength and I am sure Matt would be so proud of her. In fact, he couldn’t be any prouder."

Paying tribute to her husband the day after the tragedy claimed his life, Sarah said: "No words will ever feel like the right words to honour our Matt - my beloved husband, my best friend, and the most devoted father to our two young boys.

Article continues below

"He was an adored son and brother, a perfect son-in-law, and the most fun uncle. He was loved beyond words by all his family, his loss has left a space that can never be filled.

"He gave his life in the line of duty, protecting and serving others with courage, dedication and selflessness. The pain of losing him is beyond words, and our lives will never be the same. Neither will the love he gave us ever fade."

News.title: 'Disturbance' at funeral for teen killed in wrong-way A66 crash as arrest made
News.content:
'Disturbance' at funeral for teen killed in wrong-way A66 crash as arrest made

A man has been arrested following reports of a disturbance at the funeral of 17-year-old Cole Worthy, one of the seven people killed in a head-on collision on the A66

View 4 Images Cole Worthy, 17, was killed in a crash on the A66 at South Bank, near Middlesbrough, on August 22

A 39-year-old man has been arrested at the funeral of one of the five young males killed in a wrong-way crash on the A66, which also claimed the lives of two police officers.

The funeral service for 17-year-old Cole Worthy at Teesside Crematorium was disrupted shortly after midday on Wednesday amid reports of a disturbance inside the building, Cleveland Police said. A 39-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of assault and taken into custody.

In the early hours of August 22, a Volkswagen Passat travelling the wrong day down the A66 at South Bank, near Middlesbrough, collided head-on with a marked police car.

Both police officers inside the vehicle - PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38 - and all five occupants of the Passat - Worthy, Theo Rae, 17, Makai Saddington, 18, Michael Cahill and Jakub Matusiak, both 23 - were pronounced dead at the scene.

View 4 Images The funeral of PC Matthew Blades took place on Wednesday, with hundreds lining the streets to pay their respects (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

On Wednesday, Cleveland Police confirmed that an arrest had been made at Mr Worthy's funeral.

Superintendent John Wrintmore said: "At around 12.30pm on Wednesday September 9, police swiftly attended Teesside Crematorium following reports of a disturbance during a service taking place inside.

"A 39-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of assault and has been taken into police custody. The service has since resumed. Officers will be in the area to provide reassurance."

View 4 Images PC Tom Clough (left) and PC Matthew Blades (Image: Cleveland Police/PA Wire)

Following the crash, it emerged that a property in a quiet street in Acklam, Middlesbrough, linked to Mr Worthy had been rammed, causing extensive damage.

The funeral was held on the same day as that of PC Matthew Blades, 37, which took place in Hartlepool. Hundreds of officers from Cleveland and forces across the country lined the streets in a guard of honour.

View 4 Images (L-R) Makai Saddington, Theo Rae, Cole Worthy, Michael Cahill, Jakub Matusiak

Article continues below

The funeral for PC Clough will take place at a later date.

Schools had closed early for the previous funerals of some of the other young males in the Passat, sparking a political row, but remained open during the ceremony for Mr Worthy.

Cleveland Police previously said the young males in the Passat may have had links to organised crime.

News.title: 'I love my partner, but I don’t want to move in with him'
News.content:
Dear Coleen,

I’m a woman in my early 30s and have been seeing my partner for just over a year, and it’s going well. The issue is, he keeps dropping hints that he’d like us to move in together and that’s not something I want – at least not yet.

Currently, we live a few minutes’ walk away from each other and it works brilliantly. I live with a friend and he lives on his own. We spend nights at each other’s places and are always together at weekends.

I feel it’s still a bit early in the relationship to set up home together, but we’ve talked about marriage and possibly even kids in the future, and I suppose moving in together is the next step on that road.

I should say that I did live with my previous boyfriend and it was a big nightmare when we came to separate. We were living in a flat owned by his family, so I was the one who had to leave and start again. I feel settled where I am and it’s a nice feeling.

‌



View 2 Images The reader says: "I’m not ready to live with him just yet." (Image: Getty Images)

I suppose what I’m saying is, I’m not ready to live with him just yet, but I don’t want him to think it’s because I’m not sure about the relationship because I’ve never been surer of anything or anyone in my life. Can you advise?

Coleen says,

It sounds like deep down you’ve been very affected by what happened in your previous relationship, so you’re cautious and a bit fearful because last time it went horribly wrong and you don’t want to rock this perfect boat you’re on right now.

OK, here are a couple of scenarios. You move in with him tomorrow and realise a few months down the line that it’s not working, so you find out quickly that he’s not the one. Or you spend the next two years as you are and then move in, only to find out it doesn’t work. Or it could be brilliant!

‌



Living together is a whole new ball game – you see every side of each other and you have to be less selfish and compromise more. But if you can talk about your expectations of living together and how you’ll deal with challenges, then in my opinion it’s worth a try. Sometimes in life you have to take a leap of faith.

I don’t think a year is too soon and that’s obviously what your partner is thinking too. While it’s good to take time to consider it (I’m the opposite in these situations!), don’t overthink it. You can’t know how things will work out, but you might regret not trying.

Coleen’s words of wisdom

I love the phrase “be brave enough to be bad at something new”. It’s a reminder to take a punt on ourselves, to get excited about learning a different skill and that we’re all beginners at the start.

News.title: Andy Burnham hits out at 'appalling' abuse directed at RNLI volunteers by anti-migrant protesters
News.content:
Andy Burnham hits out at 'appalling' abuse directed at RNLI volunteers by anti-migrant protesters

Andy Burnham has hit out at 'appalling' abuse directed at RNLI volunteers by anti-migrant protesters

View 2 Images Andy Burnham's official spokesman criticised the abuse (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Andy Burnham has hit out at "appalling" abuse directed at RNLI volunteers by anti-migrant protesters.

‌



Footage online showed hero life-saving crews being labelled as traitors by far-right thugs for rescuing asylum seekers in the Channel.

‌



The charity, whose mandate is to save lives at sea, has been the target of abuse after masked-up protesters brought Dover to a standstill at the weekend. A separate protest in Portsmouth on Sunday saw thugs face off with police.

‌



The Prime Minister's official spokesman said: "Directing abuse at people who dedicate themselves to helping others is appalling.

"We won't tolerate social media being a haven for this kind of behaviour. We support the police in investigating any threatening or unlawful behaviour and taking action where appropriate."

RNLI lifeboats carrying 120 migrants denied access to land at two UK ports READ MORE :

View 2 Images Masked protesters blocked access to the Port of Dover on Saturday (Image: @Ay_audits/YouTube)

‌



His warning came as the boss of the lifesaving charity condemned far-right protesters for targeting heroic volunteers.

RNLI Chief Executive Peter Sparks said: "The RNLI's people represent the very best in our society, they selflessly give up their time to keep others safe. Yet they and their families are being threatened by those who would hide behind a balaclava or a keyboard.

"Their action, in contrast, is wholly unacceptable in a civilised society. We will take whatever steps we can, to care for and protect our people and their families."

‌



Digital Secretary Lisa Nandy said on Tuesday that she was “personally concerned” about social media doxxing, when a person’s private information is shared online without their consent.

She was responding to Vikki Slade, the Liberal Democrat MP for Mid Dorset and North Poole, who told the Commons that “some very disturbing posts” had emerged on social media, identifying “brave RNLI rescuers”.

Asked what more the Government could do to remove posts “that put children and adults’ safety at risk through doxxing”, Ms Nandy replied: “I have had an initial discussion with some of the tech companies about this.”

Article continues below

She later added: “It is something that the Government is concerned about (and) I’m personally concerned about.”

News.title: Alison Hammond fears she's 'wasted years' with son as she addresses 11st weight loss
News.content:
Alison Hammond fears she's 'wasted years' with son as she addresses 11st weight loss

Alison Hammond has given some more details about her weight loss journey and how she cut out one thing to help her fit into a go-kart to go racing with her son

View 3 Images Alison Hammond has opened up on the impact her weight loss has had on her son (Image: ITV)

Alison Hammond has lifted the lid on her huge weight loss, revealing a recent outing with her son showed just how far she had come. The Great British Bake Off host and This Morning host has inspired thousands with her weight loss journey, after losing around 11 stone (69.8kg).

‌



She says part of the process has been a change in her mindset, away from focusing on the raw numbers and turning pictures of progress into more relatable things such as clothing becoming easier to get into.

‌



These were things she addressed in an interview with her health coach Ellis Gatfield on his YouTube channel where he spoke about helping women as they made their way through the perimenopause.

‌



Alison has paid tribute to Ellis publicly on social media, writing in an Instagram post earlier this year: “Massive thank you to the incredible @ellisgatfield who started my whole fitness journey… You made my life so much easier by simple changes and kindness.”

View 3 Images Alison has stunned people with her weight loss (Image: Getty)

Speaking to Ellis about how she changed her mindset to celebrate small wins, Alison said: “Because I was quite a big girl, it was the fact that it took so long to even see a difference.

‌



“So, then you said, ‘Ok, but what’s the difference? How do you feel going up the stairs?’ It was like seeing those things that wasn’t to do with weight, seeing how I was progressing in that sense which was really really good. Seeing my trousers get a bit looser.

“That for me was so much better than just weighing myself because weighing myself, it didn’t actually make me feel good.”

One example of how far Alison had come was her ability to now fit into a go-kart.

‌



However, thanks to her weight loss she can now join her 21-year-old son Aidan, whom she had with her ex, Noureddine Boufaied, recounting how happy he was when she reached the milestone after years of trying.

View 3 Images Aidan Hammond and Alison Hammond (Image: Getty Images)

She said: “When Aidan was young he loved go karting. I could never get into the suits to go go-karting, would never go into the karts. Anyway, recently, we both went go-karting.

‌



“It was amazing [Aidan] lit up. I’ve never seen anyone so happy that I was getting in the car and driving against him and we were racing each other.

“Once I did that with him I thought, ‘Look at all the years I’ve kind of wasted when he was younger and he really wanted his mum to come and drive with him'.”

This isn’t the only personal story Alison has mentioned around her weight loss journey. Recently, she also appeared on ITV and discussed how a comment from her mother motived her.

Article continues below

Talking about the moment with her co-host Dermot O’Leary and guest Janet Street-Porter, she said: “I'll never forget when my mum was really ill in hospital.

“She looked at me – she's never commented on my weight my whole life – she said ‘Alison, don't end up like me; try and sort out your weight.’”

News.title: Man in 40s dies as tragic police-led incident forces M60 to close
News.content:
Man in 40s dies as tragic police-led incident forces M60 to close

A man has died following an incident on the M60 in Greater Manchester, which led to the motorway being closed for around an hour on Wednesday morning

View Image The M60 remained closed between junctions 10 and 11 for around an hour on Wednesday morning (Image: National Highways)

A man in his 40s has died following an incident on the M60 in Greater Manchester.

‌



Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said officers were called shortly before 7.30am on Wednesday to reports of concern for a person's welfare on the motorway near the Trafford Centre.

‌



All traffic was stopped on the clockwise carriageway between junction 10 at Urmston and junction 11 at Eccles. A large emergency services response was seen at the scene, including multiple ambulances.

‌



In an update issued this afternoon, GMP confirmed that a man in his 40s had sadly died. A report will be prepared for the coroner.

The M60 clockwise was closed between junctions 10 and 11 at around 8am and remained shut for around an hour while police carried out enquiries, the Manchester Evening News reports.

Article continues below

National Highways traffic officers were dispatched shortly before 7.30am to assist with traffic management while the road was closed during police investigations, a National Highways spokesperson said.

For mental health support, contact the Samaritans on 116 123, email them at jo@samaritans.org or visit samaritans.org to find your nearest branch.

News.title: Martin Lewis rising energy bills warning as he says 'it really isn't looking good'
News.content:
Martin Lewis rising energy bills warning as he says 'it really isn't looking good'

Martin Lewis has shared a new update for UK households about the outlook for energy bills

View 2 Images Martin Lewis is warning that UK household energy bills are heading higher (Image: ITV)

Martin Lewis is sounding the alarm that UK household energy bills are poised to climb - potentially by a considerable amount - as wholesale gas prices have surged dramatically. In an update posted on X on September 9, the MoneySavingExpert founder alerted the British public to the forecast.

‌



He warns that the situation for domestic energy bills "really isn't looking good". He highlights a chart of UK natural gas prices (in GBp/thm), which have climbed to around 196 — their highest point since the peak of the Ukraine-related energy crisis.

‌



He said: "The situation for domestic UK energy bills really isn't looking good. The chart below shows gas prices (which feed into elec bills too) spiking at the highest levels since the core of the Ukraine conflict energy crisis.

‌



"The immediate impact is the rate you can get a new fix at will get even more expensive. Then longer term, this feeds into the January price cap. It's currently on target to rise 10% to 15% over October's cap, and that remember is already confirmed to rise 3.6% rise, and was on top of the 12.6% rise in July."

Gas prices have a knock-on effect on both gas and electricity bills, given that a substantial proportion of UK power generation depends on gas. Martin Lewis warns that new fixed-rate energy tariffs are likely to become costlier as suppliers account for higher wholesale prices, reports the Liverpool Echo.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



This influences the upcoming Ofgem energy price cap (for the January period). At the time of the tweet, it was on track for a 10–15% increase over the October 2026 cap. As things stand, the October cap is already confirmed to climb to roughly 3.6%, although some sources put it closer to 4%.

And this followed a significant jump in July, which stood at approximately 12–13%. Reports suggest that wholesale gas prices have been pushed higher by ongoing tensions in the Middle East, primarily tied to the US-Iran conflict and associated disruptions to LNG/shipping routes. This has driven UK natural gas prices to multi-year highs, with predictions of additional strain on the price cap into early 2027.

The price cap only directly impacts people on standard variable/default tariffs. Those already locked into fixed-rate deals are shielded until their fixed period expires.

‌



View 2 Images The MoneySavingExpert founder shared the news on X (Image: ITV)

In essence, Martin Lewis highlighted that the recent gas-price surge is most likely unwelcome news for anyone hunting for a new energy deal now, and for the next price cap level kicking in during January. His typical guidance in these circumstances has been for people still on the price cap or standard variable rate to assess whether securing a fixed deal makes sense before rates climb further.

What are the confirmed and expected bill changes?

Current price cap (July 1 - September 30, 2026):

‌



Around £1,663 annually for a typical dual-fuel household paying by Direct Debit. This figure is calculated using Ofgem's revised typical consumption levels of approximately 2,500 kWh of electricity and 9,500 kWh of gas.

From October 1, 2026:

Article continues below

Confirmed increase of around 4% (approximately £60 annually / £5 monthly) to £1,723 for the same typical household. Gas is responsible for the bulk of the rise, while electricity is somewhat cushioned by the temporary scrapping of VAT on electricity bills.

January 2027 price cap (announced late November):

Anticipated to climb further - projections suggest roughly 10–15% on top of the October figure, as various supplier estimates ranged from the high single digits to mid-teens or beyond, depending on the source and precise wholesale fluctuations. The recent gas-price surge heightens the probability of a substantial increase.

News.title: National security can't come at expense of social security, Burnham says
News.content:
In the Commons session, Burnham repeated that the government would meet the Nato target of spending 3.5% of GDP on defence by 2035, with a target date for hitting the 3% figure set out in the spending review in the spring.

The PM said he had appointed John Healey, who resigned as Sir Keir Starmer's defence secretary over the government's failure to commit to a 3% increase by 2030, "because of his strong commitment to the defence of this nation".

However, Badenoch hit back that 2035 was "a decade away" and "the threats are now".

She questioned whether Burnham was "unable" or "just unwilling" to meet the 2030 target.

In response, Burnham insisted: "This chancellor of all chancellors will be willing to provide that funding to our armed forces."

However, he rejected a Conservative plan to partly fund increased defence spending by saving at least Â£4bn through reforms to housing benefit.

"I don't think, myself, that taking Â£4bn out of housing benefit is going to get the right consensus around this issue because that would create levels of homelessness in this country... that we wouldn't have seen before, hundreds of thousands of children in temporary accommodation," he said.

"Yes, we do everything to support our national security, but it can't come at the expense of social security."

He added: "This side of the House will not be forced to choose between the two and we will set out a plan to get to 3.5% by 2035 at the spending review."

Badenoch said Burnham's comments were "unbelievable", adding: "We need to fund our defence, not spend all of our money on welfare."

Burnham insisted he would "bring the welfare budget down" by tackling the number of young people not in education, employment or training.

"That's the Labour way to get the welfare bill down," he said.

"That is the right way to fund defence."

Badenoch accused Burnham of being "continuity Keir".

"He's pretending that he's the change candidate. But the fact is, he's still failing to cut welfare," she said.

As prime minister, Sir Keir attempted to cut disability benefits but was forced to row back on the plans in the face of opposition from Labour MPs.

Cutting the welfare bill is a key part of Tory proposals for funding increased defence spending.

Spending on benefits has ballooned in recent years and is forecast to rise to Â£408.6bn in 2030/31, according to figures from the Department for Work and Pensions.

There is particular concern about the nearly one million young people in the UK who are not in education, employment or training â known as "Neets".

The government has asked former minister Alan Milburn to look into the issue and he is expected to publish his final recommendations for how to tackle the problem shortly.

News.title: Police launch criminal investigation into Reform UK donations
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police is carrying out a criminal investigation into allegations Reform UK broke the law in relation to foreign funding, following a broadcast by Channel 4 News last week.

An undercover reporter recorded two senior Reform aides apparently suggesting a way around electoral law to secure foreign party donations, one of which would have totalled Â£500,000.

The police investigation by the Met's Special Enquiry Team is being folded into an inquiry that has been under way into other donations to the party.

A Reform UK spokesman said the party "denies any wrongdoing and will fully cooperate with the investigation".

"We won't be commenting further while a live investigation is under way."

A Met spokesperson said it had received "a number of reports relating to donations and polling involving a political party", after the film by Channel 4 News and Verbatim Investigations was shown on Thursday evening.

In its statement, the Met Police said: "All allegations under investigation relate to potential offences under the Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000."

"Detectives continue to liaise closely with the Electoral Commission and Crown Prosecution Service as enquiries progress."

The police spokesperson said detectives were seeking to obtain footage relating to the broadcast.

The film overshadowed the party's conference in Birmingham and led to the party losing two key figures - Dan Jukes, chief of staff to the leader Nigel Farage, and James Orr, head of policy.

News.title: Miliband rejects chief rabbi's claim British Jews in greater danger after sanctions move
News.content:
Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has rejected the chief rabbi's warning that British Jews are at greater risk after the UK announced sanctions on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

Miliband said that as a "proud British Jew" he disagreed with UK Chief Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis, who described the move as a "truly dark day" that would "succeed only in bolstering the very extremism they seek to target".

"We all need to do more to tackle antisemitism," Miliband said, "but I believe we can do that and stand up for British values".

The sanctions on trade with illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank come against a backdrop of rising antisemitic incidents across the UK.

The Community Security Trust (CST), an organisation that provides security support to the Jewish community, recorded 1,926 incidents of anti-Jewish hate across the UK in the first six months of 2026, a 21% increase on the same period in 2025.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham defended his government's decision, telling MPs that "Britain has to stand for fairness against injustice".

"Where people are being bullied out of their homes... we will always stand with the underdog," he said.

The Palestinian presidency welcomed the UK's decision, saying it was "an important step towards confronting Israel's colonial system and its violations against the Palestinian people".

But there has been mixed reaction within the UK Jewish community on the sanctions and possible implications for security.

The chief rabbi called the government's announcement "little more than political flag bearing for mendacious anti-Israel rhetoric".

Sir Ephraim said: "Gesture politics of this kind feeds into an increasingly hostile discourse about Israel, and the cumulative effect of such punitive policies is to further embolden those, at home and abroad, who use hatred as a weapon against Jews."

Asked about Mirvis's comments, Miliband said: "I don't agree with the chief rabbi, somebody... of whom I have great respect."

He told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that "anyone who holds British Jews - or indeed Jews around the world - responsible for the actions of the Israeli government, is engaging in antisemitism, pure and simple".

Meanwhile, the Jewish Leadership Council (JLC) warned the government's decision "risks becoming a de facto boycott of Israel" and accused Miliband of "yielding to pressure from the most extreme elements of British society".

The Board of Deputies of British Jews said the decision to make the announcement before Rosh Hashanah - the Jewish New Year festival which begins on Friday - brings "concerns for communal security at their highest levels... felt particularly acutely by British Jews".

It added that the deteriorating relationship between the UK and Israel has the potential to "further inflame community tensions here too", while also noting it had warned the Israeli government over the "intolerable settler violence" that harms Israel's reputation.

Greater Manchester Police (GMP) announced on Wednesday that extra resources would be allocated during the Jewish High Holy Days to provide "extra visibility and security" and "ensure everyone can celebrate this time safely".

Ch Supt Dave Meeney said: "Our officers will continue working with Jewish communities as we head into this important period for their faith, which we understand is a time which may bring heightened concern for the community."

News.title: 'We were raped and exploited by a drug gang as teenagers', women tell BBC of their ordeal
News.content:
Warning: Contains details of sexual exploitation

Christine is one of four women who have chosen to waive their anonymity and speak publicly to the BBC documentary, Britain's Forgotten Girls, about how they were targeted by criminals when they were children.

Their stories differ in detail, but reveal strikingly similar patterns of abuse.

All four describe being targeted by boys and older men connected to drugs gangs, manipulated into abusive relationships, then repeatedly sexually exploited.

All believe the authorities failed to protect them and did not take their allegations seriously.

The sexual and criminal exploitation of girls by drug gangs has long been overshadowed in public discussion by the focus on sexual grooming gangs, according to front-line social workers and experts in the field.

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support can be found at the BBC's Action Line.

News.title: Hundreds mourn police officer killed in wrong-way A66 crash
News.content:
Hundreds have turned out for the funeral of one of the police officers killed in a wrong-way crash.

PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, died when a Volkswagen Passat collided with their marked armed response car on the A66 at South Bank, near Middlesbrough, on 22 August. Five young men were also killed.

A full ceremonial police funeral took place for PC Blades in Hartlepool earlier, with hundreds of officers from Cleveland and forces across the country lining the street in a guard of honour.

Speaking on behalf of his family, Cleveland Police Federation chair Lauren Somerville said "life feels unbearably quiet" without the father-of-two's "silly jokes" and laughter.

Members of other emergency services were present at St Joseph's Roman Catholic Church, alongside community leaders and politicians.

Cleveland Police chief constable Victoria Fuller greeted mourners at the entrance to the church.

Policing minister Sarah Jones and Home Office minister Anna Turley also attended.

News.title: Watch: Sinkhole at Nicolas Cage's Malibu house swallows driveway
News.content:
Aerial footage shows a massive sinkhole in front of a house in Malibu, California, reportedly belonging to US actor Nicolas Cage.

The actor bought the home in 2024, according to a report in the New York Times.

The driveway of the beachfront house collapsed on Tuesday morning, according to local authorities.

In a written statement, the City of Malibu said it ordered the evacuation of the houses in the street and set up a temporary shelter for evacuees.

More on this story.

News.title: Actor Noel Clarke charged with sexual offences
News.content:
Actor Noel Clarke has been charged with sexual offences including sexual assault, voyeurism and exposure.

The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) authorised the Metropolitan Police to charge the Doctor Who and Kidulthood star on Wednesday.

Clarke, 50, from Kensington, west London, was charged with two counts of sexual assault, three charges of voyeurism and one charge of exposure. The offences are alleged to have taken place between 2007 and 2016 and relate to five women.

Clarke has not yet publicly responded to the charges.

In a statement released on Wednesday, the CPS said: "Our prosecutors have worked to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring this case to court and that it is in the public interest to do so."

The charges follow an investigation by detectives which began a year ago.

A man, then in his 40s, was first arrested in connection with the investigation on 25 September 2025.

A file of evidence was later given to the CPS who authorised charges.

Clarke will appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on 21 October at 10:00 BST.

Det Supt Mike Cagney, whose team is leading the investigation, said: "The women connected to these charges continue to receive support from specially trained officers.

"We urge anyone who has been a victim of sexual assault to contact police. The information you provide will be dealt with in the utmost sensitivity and we have trained investigators on hand to support you."

Clarke found fame playing Mickey Smith in Doctor Who between 2005 and 2010, and went on to become a successful actor, writer, producer and director.

News.title: Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'
News.content:
A top safety researcher at Anthropic has warned AI is advancing so quickly he believes there is a greater than 10% chance it "could kill all humans" within the next decade.

Evan Hubinger said in a post on X, external the risk from the models which currently exist was "low" but he was "worried" the technology might develop and improve itself soon to the point where it posed an existential risk to humanity.

He did not spell out how he thought AI systems could in future result in humans being wiped out.

But his comments are the latest in a series of increasingly stark warnings about AI, with the debate shifting from whether it truly poses a risk to how big that risk is.

Hubinger's intervention was in response to another post on X, external from Jacob Coxon, an AI researcher who has just quit Anthropic and previously worked at OpenAI.

"Neither company is acting responsibly," he wrote.

"These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionise any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources."

OpenAI has been approached for comment.

Dame Wendy Hall, a computer scientist who advises the UN on AI, told the BBC she was "shocked" by Hubinger and Coxon's social media posts.

She told the World at One on BBC Radio Four some of it could be "PR and marketing" however, as Anthropic and OpenAI raced towards highly anticipated stock market debuts.

But she added: "Why would someone want to say that? I would plead with investors not to invest in this company if that is their value system."

Separately, the Financial Times reported, external Anthropic withheld its latest model from the UK's AI Safety Institute (AISI), one of the leading bodies in the world for assessing AI risk.

Anthropic has declined to comment on the posts by its employees or the situation with the AISI.

A Cabinet Office spokesperson did not comment on whether the latest model had been withheld from the AISI - instead saying it "continues to collaborate closely with industry partners, including Anthropic, to make models safer".

News.title: Drug gangs exploited and raped us as teens, then police failed us, women tell BBC
News.content:
Warning: Contains details of sexual exploitation

"It was the thrill of being with a bad boy."

Christine was 13 when she began exchanging messages online with someone she believed was a teenage boy.

On their first meeting, she discovered he was a grown man 10 years older than herself. He also told her he was involved with gangs and drugs.

"I always knew, OK, he's probably hurt someone, but in terms of hurting me, I didn't think it would get to that point," she says.

Over the next few years, he would use Christine to courier drugs, subject her to extreme sexual exploitation, and assault her so violently she feared she might die.

Christine is one of four women who have chosen to waive their anonymity and speak publicly to the BBC documentary, Britain's Forgotten Girls, about how they were targeted by criminals when they were children.

Their stories, covering 2002 to last year, differ in detail - but reveal strikingly similar patterns of abuse. All four describe being targeted by boys and older men connected to drug gangs, manipulated into abusive relationships, then repeatedly sexually exploited.

All believe the authorities failed to protect them and did not take their allegations seriously.

The sexual and criminal exploitation of girls by drug gangs has long been overshadowed in public discussion by the focus on sexual grooming gangs, according to front-line social workers and experts in the field.

"For grooming gangs, the primary purpose is often the sexual exploitation of those girls, but the primary purpose of a drug gang is to make money off selling drugs and other criminal activity," says Connie Muttock from the children's charity, Centre for Young Lives.

Girls are brought in to generate money, says Muttock, but many are also sexually abused by gang members.

News.title: Channel 4 to cut 340 jobs by the end of the year in major shake-up
News.content:
Channel 4 has said it plans to cut 340 jobs before the end of the year, reducing its workforce by more than a quarter.

The network, which broadcasts Gogglebox and The Great British Bake Off, will lose around 28% of its current 1,270 staff following a strategic review of the organisation.

Priya Dogra, Channel 4's chief executive, said the announcement "marks the first phase of our transformation, ensuring Channel 4 is the right shape and size to deliver its future strategy and focus investment in the programmes audiences love".

Caroline Dinenage, chair of the culture, media and sport committee said the news would be "deeply worrying for the talented and dedicated people who work at Channel 4".

The network said it planned to focus on creating a simpler and more efficient operating model and enable greater investment in distinctive programming.

In her statement, Dogra said: "Channel 4 is a precious asset which plays a unique role in the UK.

"We need to secure and own our future so we can continue to make shows others won't, reach audiences others can't, and thrive as a distinctive and disruptive British voice for future generations.

"The challenges we face require a fundamental transformation in how we work. I know the proposals we are announcing today will be very difficult for many colleagues and will have a significant impact across the organisation."

She added: "These decisions have not been taken lightly, but I strongly believe they are necessary to create a simpler, more focused and more sustainable Channel 4."

News.title: Learner drivers still forced to wait months to book tests
News.content:
Learner drivers have to wait an average 20 weeks, or around five months, before booking a practical test, according to new figures, despite attempts to reduce delays.

The data from the Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency (DVSA) for August is only a marginal improvement from 20.2 weeks in July.

The average wait time between booking and sitting a test is unchanged at 11.1 weeks.

The DVSA initially had a target of reducing the average waiting time to seven weeks by the end of last year. Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander pushed the target back to summer 2026, but subsequently admitted even that would not be possible.

The DVSA made a number of changes to its practical driving test booking system earlier this year.

Only the learner driver themself is now able to book their driving test, blocking an instructor or third parties from booking using the learner's details.

There is also a geographical restriction which means a learner can only book a test at their three local test centres, rather than one at the other side of the country if they found a test available.

The number of times a would-be driver can swap a test date has also been restricted.

News.title: Divorcing abusive husband cost woman £105k
News.content:
A woman who endured years of abusive controlling behaviour by her ex-husband says it has cost her more than Â£105,000 to divorce him.

Annabelle Boucher, 48, from Somerset, wants the law changed after she paid Â£75,000 to David Rogers, 61, despite him admitting to coercive and controlling behaviour. She also had to pay her legal costs.

"I thought being stuck in this relationship I couldn't get out of would be highlighted within the divorce procedure," Boucher said. "But the divorce law doesn't take into account the fact that he was a criminal."

The Ministry of Justice (MoJ) said it had begun a consultation to reform the law so "family courts meet the needs of domestic abuse victims".

Boucher, a mother from Chiselborough, said Rogers had come into her life in "a whirlwind" in 2017 and the pair got married two years later.

It was once they were married that things started to "take a turn", she said, and "some very extreme behaviour started to happen".

"It creeps up on you and you're in it, and so you don't kind of notice what is happening."

Boucher said she had ended up "shutting down emotionally" and "cutting off from everyone" because she feared what would happen.

"You find that you're trapped within a situation that you can't get out of."

News.title: Man shot by police after woman stabbed at property
News.content:
A man has been shot by police after a woman was stabbed at a property in Luton.

Shots were fired by armed officers at an address in Cardigan Street at about 12:50 BST on Tuesday.

The man was struck in the arm and leg after a Bedfordshire Police officer discharged four shots, while another fired a baton round.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it was now investigating the police response.

"We have secured the police firearms for examination and CCTV and officers' body worn video have been viewed," a spokesman said.

The man's injuries were described as life-changing but not life-threatening.

Both he and the woman, whose injuries were also not life-threatening, were taken to hospital for treatment.

Bedfordshire Police said it was responding to reports that a man was threatening a woman with a knife at the address.

Det Ch Supt Zara Brown said officers "responded quickly" to the unfolding incident.

"As part of this response, shots were fired by police, and one man sustained serious injuries," she continued.

"Immediate first aid was provided, and he has been taken to hospital, where he remains under police watch."

The force pledged to provide further information about the IOPC investigation when possible.
