News.title: Shane Richie pleads not guilty to drink-driving
News.content:
EastEnders actor Shane Richie has pleaded not guilty to a single charge of drink-driving.

The 62-year-old, who has played Alfie Moon in the BBC soap since 2002, was arrested at a petrol station in Harlow, Essex, on 29 July where he was with his Hyundai IX35.

Richie, from Tadworth in Surrey, has appeared at Colchester Magistrates' Court via video link from a hotel room.

The actor - who appeared under his real name of Shane Roche - spoke only to confirm his name, address and plea. He is next due to appear for trial at the same court on 17 November 2027.

News.title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns
News.content:
There could be tens of thousands more teenagers who are not in education, employment or training (Neet) than official statistics suggest, the children's commissioner for England has warned.

A report by Dame Rachel de Souza said around 42,000 16- and 17-year-olds in England were officially classed as studying at college, but were not showing up at least half of the time.

She said they had gone "under the radar" and were "not getting the support that they need".

The Department for Education (DfE) said it planned to help colleges track attendance and ultimately to gather that data centrally.

Unlike schools, further education and sixth form colleges in England are not required to collect or report attendance data.

Dame Rachel's report is based on attendance data obtained from 262 college groups in England and says rates are "substantially lower" than in schools.

It suggests that more than half (52.2%) of 16- and 17-year-olds are estimated to be persistently absent by the standards used in schools, meaning they are missing 10% or more of college sessions.

And around 42,000 (5.9%) are severely absent, meaning they are missing at least half of college sessions.

The DfE estimates that 57,000 16- and 17-year-olds in England are Neet, and Dame Rachel's report argues that these persistently absent teenagers should be considered as "hidden" Neets alongside them.

Dame Rachel told the BBC a range of factors led to teenagers missing college, including part-time work and travel costs, and that some had been largely absent from education since the Covid pandemic.

She said while those juggling part-time employment were likely to miss college every so often, it was those who are "far more vulnerable" who were likely to be severely absent.

She added that it was "shocking" that the DfE did not collect the data as it meant the issue was "ignored".

"It's under the radar and these kids are not getting the support that they need," she said.

News.title: Man in court accused of killing two cyclists in crash
News.content:
A man has appeared in court accused of killing two cyclists and injuring another in a crash in Kent.

Aaron Turner, 22, from St Patrick's Gardens in Gravesend, was bailed after appearing by video link at Medway Magistrates' Court charged with causing death by dangerous driving.

Natasha Lewis, 51, and Stephen Anscomb, 60, died of "traumatic and catastrophic" injuries in the crash near Gravesend on Sunday, and the third cyclist was treated in hospital, the court heard.

Turner is accused of having "lost control" of his white Ford Focus while travelling south-west near the village of Sole Street at about 07:45 BST.

In addition to two counts of causing death by dangerous driving, Turner has been charged with failing to stop at the scene of a crash and possession of a class C drug.

A 21-year-old man who was arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving and a 19-year-old woman who was detained on suspicion of assisting an offender have been released on police bail.

Turner spoke to confirm his name, address and date of birth during Wednesday's court appearance.

He is next due to appear at Woolwich Crown Court on 7 October.

Prosecutor Dylan Bradshaw said the three cyclists had been on a "training cycle ride" prior to a "very long cycle ride" they were planning overseas.

He added that Anscombe left behind his wife and two daughters while Lewis was survived by her 23-year-old daughter, who also lost her father in 2019.

Investigators are asking anyone who saw the car or cyclists before the incident, or who witnessed the crash near the junction of Sole Street and Round Street, to contact them.

They also appealed for members of the public with CCTV or dashcam footage to get in touch.

Short-term home rental platforms, including Airbnb, are facing fresh limits after the European Commission proposed new rules on Wednesday to help local authorities address housing shortages in tourism hotspots.

The initiative by the EU executive aims to create unified regulations across the bloc, following a mix of local curbs in destinations such as Paris, Barcelona and Venice that led to legal challenges.

Surging numbers of holiday rentals have restricted the availability of affordable homes, driving residents, particularly younger citizens, to stage street protests.

"A year ago, I promised to tackle Europe's housing affordability," Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said in a statement.

open image in gallery Authorities in cities including Paris, Barcelona and Venice turned to a raft of diverse rules to crack down on Airbnb, which triggered legal challenges ( Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images )

"Today, we are taking one step in this direction. By providing more clarity and support to local authorities and communities, anchored in local realities," she said.

Subject to agreement by EU member states and the European Parliament over the coming months, the draft measures will establish a first common European framework for assessing residential housing policies.

According to the Commission, local officials can identify strained housing markets by monitoring high price-to-income levels or sustained upward trends over a 10-year period.

Any subsequent curbs on short-term rentals must be necessary, supported by evidence, limited strictly to the impacted areas, and not applied retroactively.

Airbnb aligned itself with the tech lobby group CCIA Europe in requesting independent review or redress mechanisms. The firm maintained that the main issue remains a shortage of available properties.

"That means focusing it (the regulation) where the shortage actually is: construction, renovation, and the homes standing empty across Europe today," George Mavros, Airbnb's head of government affairs for the European Union, said in a blogpost.

CCIA Europe's head of policy Alexandre Roure challenged the plan to let cities oversee their own enforcement.

"Without independent scrutiny or effective redress, this proposal will remain a paper tiger, leaving disproportionate restrictions in place and undermining the legal certainty the Affordable Housing Act is meant to provide," he said.

Individual authorities will determine whether to implement actions. The Commission also advised local councils to free up land for residential building and modernise construction and planning processes.

The board of the U.N. nuclear watchdog on Wednesday adopted a resolution ending its investigation into past secret nuclear activities in Syria that revealed a reactor configured to produce fissile material for possible use in nuclear weapons.

Under ousted former President Bashar Assad, Syria was believed to have operated an extensive undeclared nuclear program that included a reactor built by North Korea in eastern Deir el-Zour province.

The 35-member board of governors of the Vienna-based International Atomic Energy Agency adopted the resolution unanimously, according to diplomats who spoke on condition of anonymity to describe the outcome of the closed-doors vote.

Delegates could be heard applauding inside the board room as the resolution was adopted ending the investigation after almost two decades.

The resolution was put forward by Egypt, Jordan, Morocco and Saudi Arabia.

In June 2011, the IAEA Board of Governors found Syria in non-compliance with its nonproliferation obligations for secretly constructing a nuclear reactor in Deir el-Zour and reported the matter to the U.N. Security Council and the U.N. General Assembly to consider sanctions.

Under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and the safeguards agreement Syria has with the U.N. nuclear watchdog, Syria is legally bound to declare all nuclear material and activities to the agency and allow IAEA inspectors to verify that none of it is being diverted from peaceful uses.

Following Assad’s ouster in December 2024, the new authorities in Damascus agreed to give IAEA inspectors access to suspected former nuclear sites.

Wednesday’s draft resolution, which was seen by The Associated Press, therefore decided to “terminate” the provisions of the 2011 resolution, ending the IAEA investigation into Syria’s non-compliance.

The draft resolution, however, underlined that Syria “remains bound” by its obligations under the Nonproliferation Treaty and the safeguards agreement and encourages Syria “to continue its cooperation with the Agency, including the excavation work” at the site of the nuclear reactor.

It also requested the head of the IAEA, Rafael Grossi, to continue updating the board on the “outcomes of ongoing activities” in Syria.

The site in Deir el-Zour only became public knowledge after Israel launched airstrikes in 2007 that destroyed the facility. Syria later leveled the site and never responded fully to the IAEA’s questions about it.

The draft resolution welcomed “the transparency and cooperation” of Syria’s new authorities and commended them “for the actions taken in resolving its non-compliance.”

During a visit to Syria in August, Grossi and a team of senior inspectors observed the ongoing excavation work of the Deir el-Zour reactor.

They also inspected additional locations, including sites for fuel fabrication and fuel storage and for planned reprocessing activities.

The IAEA chief and a team of senior agency officials also inspected a previously undeclared site in Syria where they witnessed the unearthing of 73 tonnes of natural uranium metal, of which 55 tonnes were in the form of fuel rods.

All of this material has been placed under IAEA surveillance measures.

The Metropolitan Police has launched a criminal investigation into allegations that Reform UK breached donation rules with potential illegal foreign funding, the force has confirmed.

Allegations that the party arranged illegal donations not only overshadowed the party’s conference in Birmingham, but also led to the resignation on Friday of Nigel Farage’s chief of staff and longtime aide Dan Jukes, as well as policy director James Orr.

Over the weekend, the Metropolitan Police confirmed they were considering complaints from Labour and the Lib Dems over video footage obtained by Channel 4 and investigative group Verbatim which appeared to show senior Reform figures discussing how to disguise donations from foreign sources.

But Mr Farage has insisted he and his aides “had done nothing illegal” and that no money changed hands.

open image in gallery Party leader Nigel Farage was already facing intense scrutiny about donations Reform has received, as well as £5 million he was given by a wealthy backer ( Reuters )

On Tuesday, a spokesperson for the force said: “Following a broadcast by Channel 4 News on Thursday, September 3, the Met received a number of reports relating to donations and polling involving a political party.

“Detectives have assessed the information provided and determined that there are potential offences requiring investigation.

“The potential offences are similar in nature to matters already under investigation by the Met’s Special Enquiry Team relating to donations made to the same political party. As a result, these matters will form part of that ongoing investigation.

“All allegations under investigation relate to potential offences under the Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000.”

They added: “As part of enquiries, detectives are seeking to obtain relevant footage relating to the broadcast on Thursday, September 3.

“Detectives continue to liaise closely with the Electoral Commission and Crown Prosecution Service as enquiries progress.”

open image in gallery The Metropolitan Police have launched a criminal investigation into allegations that Reform breached donation rules ( Metropolitan Police )

It is understood that no arrests have been made and no one has been interviewed under caution in relation to the latest allegations.

Mr Farage was already facing intense scrutiny about donations Reform has received, as well as £5 million he was given by a wealthy backer.

But he claimed over the weekend that the allegations broadcast by Channel 4 have been made because “they’re scared of us” and he insisted that there will be further probes into Reform as a result.

He told the BBC on Saturday that he “frankly wasn’t listening” during a conversation with his former chief of staff and an undercover journalist featured in the Channel 4 broadcast.

In the footage, Mr Farage was present when it was suggested a US donor give £500,000 to Reform through his UK-based son - a proposal that could have been in breach of electoral law. The political donation was ultimately never made.

“I was in the middle of canvassing in the Clacton by-election. I turn up. I frankly wasn’t even listening”, he said.

The footage was part of an investigation by undercover group Verbatim, who posed as an American donor and his son who had paid for polling allegedly commissioned by Reform and were seeking to channel money to Reform.

Accepting donations from a foreign company, including donations in kind such as polling, could constitute a criminal offence.

The latest row continues a difficult period for Mr Farage, whose poll ratings have fallen amid scrutiny of Reform’s finances and a Clacton by-election that was boycotted by other parties.

After the news of the investigation broke, Mr Farage ignored it to post on X, formerly Twitter: “I will ban the burqa and balaclavas. This is Britain. We see each other's faces.”

Reform UK said it would co-operate fully with the police investigation.

In a statement, a spokesman for the party said: “Reform UK denies any wrongdoing and will fully co-operate with the investigation. We won’t be commenting further while a live investigation is under way.”

Prince Harry and Meghan Markle were disappointed by the King’s decision to brand them as private citizens and instead hoped to be known as “public figures”, it has been reported.

Buckingham Palace released an official memorandum on Monday clarifying that although the couple have returned to the UK, they should be treated strictly as private citizens and not as working royals.

Royal aides said that the directive aligns fully with the couple's previously stated wish to live as private citizens following the Sandringham agreement in 2020, when the pair formally ended their royal duties and moved to California.

open image in gallery Prince Harry and Meghan Markle reportedly wished to be referred to as ‘public figures’ ( PA Wire/PA Images )

But reports in the MailOnline on Wednesday suggest the couple were unhappy with the memorandum and would have preferred the King to refer to them as “public figures”.

Clarifying the couple’s status, the document reads: “In short, their position is akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests,” stating that their philanthropic work is conducted in a personal capacity, entirely separate from the royal household. But reports suggest the Sussexes feel this does not reflect their true status as part of the Royal family in a private capacity.

“The Sussexes prefer the term "public figures", and would have liked an acknowledgement that, on a personal level, they remained members of the Royal Family, despite no longer receiving public funding,” a briefing received by the paper reads.

The report also claims the pair were caught “off guard” by the document, and had not had a chance to “clarify one or two points” with the King.

A spokesperson for the Sussexes previously told the BBC that the pair “were a little surprised not to have been told about this in advance.” The broadcaster said that royal sources had told them the couple were made aware of the letter before it was made public.

open image in gallery Harry and Meghan moved back to the UK two weeks ago after six years in the US (Aaron Chown/PA) ( PA Archive )

It comes as the military chief of Uganda announced the country will pull out from Prince Harry’s Invictus Games as he said the country would not participate in any event "that does not have His Majesty’s approval".

General Muhoozi Kainerugaba wrote on X: “In order not to be construed as being opposed to His Majesty King Charles III of the United Kingdom, whom we deeply revere, Uganda hereby withdraws from the invictus games. We shall not participate in anything that does not have His Majesty's approval.”

He later told The Times: “I have factions in the Ministry of Defence that support that Harry-Meghan nonsense. I had to quash it straight away. I support the monarch. Period.”

The Sussexes returned to the UK on 26 August after it was revealed earlier that month that they were enrolling their children, Archie and Lillibet, into British schools. In the run up to their return, the King was said to be glad to be able to spend more time with the family, but remained adamant they would not be working royals and there was no half-in, half-out option.

The letter said: “Following the decision by the Duke and Duchess of Sussex to relocate to the UK, we have received a number of requests for guidance. To help avoid doubt or confusion, The King has directed that the following information be shared.

“It is well known that in January 2020 the Duke and Duchess stepped down from undertaking representative duties on behalf of The Sovereign, and are no longer working Members of The Royal Family.

“This position, distinct from the State and Royal duties undertaken by the working Royal Family, and with the personal latitude it brings the couple in respect of financial independence and protection of their privacy as they would wish, will continue to be fully respected.”

The Independent has contacted the Sussexes’ representative for comment.

British police said Wednesday that they have opened a criminal investigation into allegations that anti-immigration party Reform UK broke rules against foreign donations.

Last week, Channel 4 broadcast an undercover investigation in which two senior Reform UK officials appeared to discuss ways money from an American financier could be channeled through his U.K.-based son.

U.K. electoral law says parties can only accept donations from British voters or U.K.-registered businesses.

The Metropolitan Police said that after the broadcast, the force "received a number of reports relating to donations and polling involving a political party.

“Detectives have assessed the information provided and determined that there are potential offenses requiring investigation," it said.

The party suspended Dan Jukes, a longtime adviser to Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, and chief James Orr, after the documentary was aired. But Farage denied that there was any breach of electoral law.

The program showed two men purporting to be a U.S. financier and his U.K.-based son discussing with Jukes, in the presence of Farage, how 500,000 pounds ($675,000) could be donated to the party through the son. The “son” was actually a reporter from investigative group Verbatim, and the “father” an actor.

In separate footage, Orr, a Cambridge University theologian, appeared to discuss getting the U.S. donor to pay for opinion polls commissioned by Reform UK.

Reform UK said Wednesday that it “denies any wrongdoing and will fully cooperate with the investigation.”

Current and former employees of Anthropic, an American AI company founded by former OpenAI leaders, say they believe AI could potentially kill all humans within the next 10 years.

“We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade. I believe Anthropic is trying its best, but we do not yet have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence and are not clearly on track to,” Anthropic alignment-science lead Evan Hubinger wrote Tuesday night on X.

His comments came after Anthropic AI researcher Jacob Coxon resigned from the company and took to X to detail his departure.

“The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Coxon stated. “This is not a marketing stunt. If anything, many executives and senior researchers will couch their phrasing in the press to sound sensible - but I hear the same people express fear privately. No other human activity poses this level of danger.”

His comments come as AI becomes an increasingly routine part of daily life for millions of Americans, while concerns over its potential risks grow. Industry leaders have warned that increasingly powerful AI systems could eventually become difficult or impossible to control.

Anthropic employees, including ex-researcher Jacob Coxon, who resigned Tuesday, say AI could potentially kill all humans within the next decade ( Reuters )

Around 2 a.m. Wednesday, Anthropic scalable-oversight lead Samuel Marks also responded to Coxon’s post, claiming that he was “[Writing this in a personal capacity, not on behalf of my employer (Anthropic).”

"AI developers believe their technology could cause human extinction (or similarly bad outcomes). This could happen in the next few years. In general, the more senior the employee, the more concerned they are,” Marks wrote.

The Independent has contacted Anthropic for comment.

OpenAI, a separate but leading AI company, declined to comment on Coxon’s post when contacted by The Independent. However, a spokesperson pointed to several updates the company has published in recent weeks outlining its efforts to improve AI safety and alignment.

Hundreds of police officers gathered to line the street for the funeral of a colleague killed in a collision on the A66.

Standard bearers from every UK force attended the service for 37-year-old Pc Matthew Blades at St Joseph’s Roman Catholic Church in his home town of Hartlepool.

Pc Blades died alongside his colleague, Pc Tom Clough, 38, in a horrific crash near Middlesbrough at South Bank, which also claimed the lives of five young men.

Lining the length of Hutton Avenue outside the red-brick church, a number of officers displayed identity patches on their uniforms marked "Pc 2443 BLADES" and "Pc 3234 CLOUGH".

The hearse had a white and red floral tribute which read “Dad” on the roof for the married father-of-two.

open image in gallery A floral tribute which says 'Dad' on top of the hearse at the funeral of PC Matthew Blades. ( PA )

The standard bearers lowered their flags as the hearse, led by a police motorbike outrider, approached the church.

Four officers on horse-back stood guard beside a cordon where hundreds of members of the public were also paying tribute.

Before the service, traffic officers in white caps hugged each other as they remembered Pc Blades, who was an armed response officer.

Four pipers and a drummer processed in front of the funeral car and they played Amazing Grace as the coffin, covered by a Union Flag, was brought in.

Emergency services representatives from the North East Ambulance Service and Great North Air Ambulance were also there.

open image in gallery Bagpipers lead the funeral cortege through the streets lined with police colleagues at the ceremonial parade to the funeral of PC Matthew Blades ( PA )

Cleveland Police Chief Constable Victoria Fuller greeted mourners at the entrance to the church.

Policing minister Sarah Jones and Home Office minister Anna Turley also attended.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham paid tribute in the Commons, saying: “I also want to send our sympathies to the hundreds of people who will gather today at the funeral of Pc Matthew Blades, including many serving police officers, and we send our thanks to them all for their service and their work to keep our communities safe.”

Ahead of the service, a spokesperson for the Diocese of Hexham and Newcastle said: “Today we remember in prayer Pc Matthew Blades, who gave his life in service to others.

“We pray for his family, colleagues and all those affected by these tragic events, and ask for the Lord’s comfort, strength and guidance at this time.”

open image in gallery Pall bearers carry the coffin of PC Matthew Blades. ( PA )

Outside church, Zara Lavender, 30, from Hartlepool, said: “I have come here to pay my respects to the officer, I thought it was important that people came out to show that.”

A former British Army soldier, who asked not to be named, explained why he came, saying: “You can see from the turnout that people wanted to get together.

“These guys did not deserve what happened to them – the police have a hard enough job as it is.”

Ahead of the service, Cleveland Police Federation chairwoman Lauren Somerville thanked the public for their support.

She said: “There’s been over £1.2 million raised for Matt and Tom’s families, which is overwhelming, and a great show of support.

“There have been comments on Facebook, we’ve had flowers delivered to our stations.

open image in gallery A police officer wears a black armband embroidered with the names of two colleagues who were killed - Pc Blades and Pc Clough. ( PA )

“People have been in touch from Australia, France, America – the support has been overwhelming, and it’s been comforting.”

Describing Pc Blades, she said: “Matthew was a best friend, husband, father, a brother and a son, and his family have said the words are not powerful enough to describe how they feel right now.

“He has been described as the heart of the family, and he will be remembered beyond words today, tomorrow, and always.

“He would be so proud of all of the support that’s been shown from the public and from his colleagues, to his family.

“His family have said they’re going to miss everything about him more than words can say, and his laughter and silly jokes made them smile even when they least expected it.

open image in gallery Police officers hug each other before the funeral of PC Matthew Blades. ( PA )

“He’s been described as bringing light and laughter into every room and now life feels unbearably quiet without him.”

The armed response officers were in a marked vehicle heading the right way down the A66 in the early hours of August 22 when they were hit by a Passat which had been involved in a police pursuit before it was aborted.

Ms Fuller has previously said Pc Blades and Pc Clough were “brave, committed, professional people who put the public before themselves”.

Manchester United fan Pc Blades was a dedicated football coach in his spare time.

President Donald Trump is set to kick off the Republican Party’s first-ever midterm convention with a pair of speeches spanning both nights of the Texas confab, even as GOP candidates in close races avoid the entire spectacle.

Trump is scheduled to depart the White House this afternoon for the two-day event in Dallas, where he will first participate in a fundraiser for his MAGA Inc. Super PAC before heading to the convention itself.

He will then deliver what has been billed as a keynote address at 9:15 pm ET.

Trump will return to the convention on Thursday, where he will also deliver closing remarks after a planned speech by Vice President JD Vance.

The president’s appearance at the highly unusual off-year convention contrasts with the 45 or so Republican elected officials and candidates in close races who are snubbing the gathering and focusing on their own campaigns instead.

Rubber ducks in the image of President Donald Trump are seen at a store outside of the American Airlines Center ahead of the 2026 Republican National Committee Midterm Convention ( Getty )

Republicans are hoping to generate enthusiasm among potential voters and bring in money for the GOP – in part by charging donors $88,600 for a photo with Trump.

One House Republican told Politico the midterm convention was a “waste of time” and said planning had been “a mess.”

The event is also meant to raise money for Republicans fighting tough races, such as Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who is trying to defeat Democratic candidate James Talerico in the Senate race.

The RNC reportedly asked sitting House members to spend $25,000 for themselves and a guest to attend the two-day event or $100,000 for a higher tier.

The list of speakers is largely taken up by members of Trump's Cabinet like Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

Also set to address the crowd are Attorney General Todd Blanche, the president's son Donald Trump Jr. and former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt, as well as Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton and Mike Rogers, the party's Senate nominee in Michigan.

House Speaker Mike Johnson and Texas Sen. Ted Cruz are also giving speeches.

News.title: Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double
News.content:
Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Team news from Portugal to follow shortly.

News.title: Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start
News.content:
Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he said.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

News.title: Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off
News.content:
Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

News.title: Bird flu threatens French foie gras amid new duck cull
News.content:
The latest cull - like previous ones - was undertaken to protect both animal and human health.

Ducks are killed to stop the spread of the disease between farms, as well as to protect the health of farmers and minimise the risk of the virus mutating.

It is thought foie gras itself does not pose a risk to human health, even if it came from a bird-flu-infected duck, because it is almost always heat-treated before it is sold, which effectively destroys the virus, according to Public Health France.

“The consumption of meat, foie gras and eggs – and more generally of any food product based on poultry – presents no risk to humans,” said a spokesman for the Maine-et-Loire prefecture.

Veterinary experts say ducks are especially problematic regarding H5N1 because they can carry the virus without showing symptoms and have been described as the Chevaux de Troie or “Trojan horses” of bird flu.

It is unclear how the birds in the latest outbreak, located on a farm in Longué-Jumelles, contracted the virus, although it is typically spread by wild birds which shed the virus through their droppings.

It is for this reason that British poultry were forced into lockdown or “flockdown” from late October to April of this year.

This included so-called “free-range” birds, which, as the Telegraph reported in November continued to be described as free-range despite never seeing the light of day under a dispensation given by the Department for Environment, Food, and Rural Affairs (DEFRA).

Ducks reared for foie gras typically spend the first 90 days of their lives being reared in their tens of thousands in barns with very little access to natural light.

Animal rights campaigners say most never see water.

They then are put through a rigorous 12-16 day “fattening up” period where they are force-fed through a tube to significantly enlarge their livers, before being slaughtered.

While France introduced a vaccination programme to protect its duck population from bird flu in 2023, the jabs do not entirely stop the virus from getting into a flock.

Data collected by the French Agency for Food, Environmental and Occupational Health & Safety suggested that between 50 and 55 per cent of the country’s ducks are unvaccinated at any given time, due to a 20-day gap between the first and second dose of the vaccine and waning immunity over time.

The ducks subject to the latest bird-flu cull in Western France had received their first dose of the H5N1 vaccine, but not the second, meaning they were not fully protected, according to the disease monitoring firm Airfinity.

The threat to France’s £2 billion foie gras industry comes amid increasing global competition.

Once the dominant producer, it is now being challenged by China, which has rapidly scaled up its output of the delicacy and now accounts for 45 per cent of global production.

A tin of Chinese foie gras costs roughly £3.70, while a typical tin of French foie gras made from duck liver costs between £10 and £15. French foie gras produced from Geese costs anywhere between £70 and £150.

China is also said to operate a more rigorous poultry vaccination programme, according to an analysis by DEFRA.

It applies to all farmed birds in the country, which has managed to keep outbreaks of bird flu on farms relatively low compared with European levels.

The H5N1 avian flu pandemic has now been running for six years and has decimated flocks of farmed chickens and turkeys across the globe.

In the UK alone, more than five million farmed birds have been culled since 2021, costing an estimated £48 million in farmers’ compensation alone.

Last week, the virus was detected on a mink farm in the US state of Utah.

Minks in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of fur farms – where thousands of the animals are crammed together in tight proximity – give invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate.

The virus has also done huge damage to wild birds and other animals. In South America alone, more than 600,000 wild seabirds have died since 2022.

Dozens of other mammals have been infected and died across the globe, including foxes, otters, sea lions, bears, and seals.

In June, the virus was found in Australia for the first time – the last continent on earth to record a case – and the government has since launched a vaccination programme to protect the country’s rare species, including birds like orange-bellied parrots and black cockatoos.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 gains the mutations necessary to spread between people, it could trigger a human-pandemic, something that would be of “enormous concern”, according to the World Health Organization (WHO), given the virus’s 50 per cent case fatality rate.

News.title: The Chancellor’s speech, as it happened
News.content:
John Healey failed to rule out tax rises at next month’s Budget in his first major speech as Chancellor.

Mr Healey also sought to blame Liz Truss and her mini-Budget in 2022 for the high borrowing costs being paid by the Treasury.

During a speech in Coventry, the Chancellor said he would be “honest” about the need to control public spending during his time in Number 11.

He was speaking days after the cost of government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007.

It was also overshadowed by Jaguar Land Rover announcing plans to cut 4,000 jobs in the face of “intense competition and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty”.

Read our report on the Chancellor’s speech.

News.title: Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week
News.content:
At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

Sports.title: How Barcelona have turned their back on famed academy and are raiding Premier League to fuel Champions League dream
Sports.content:
BARCELONA are turning to the Premier League to try to win their first Champions League title since 2015.

The Spanish giants have struggled in Europe for over a decade and failed to add to their five UCL titles for the past 11 years.



They are now changing their approach, and relying less on their famed academy La Masia, and instead turning to the Premier League.

This summer has seen an unprecedented number of La Masia graduates leave the club.



The likes of Jofre Torrens, Toni Fernandez, Alvaro Cortes, Guille Fernandez and Tommy Marques have all made permanent transfers elsewhere.

It has been a deliberate change in approach from sporting director Deco, and Barca have made sure to include buy-back clauses and sell-on fees to the deals.

READ MORE IN FOOTBALL FEEL THE BERN Arsenal sign 40-goal striker, 16, from Prem rival days after window shut



The Catalan side have been raiding the Premier League over the last two years.

Last summer Marcus Rashford joined on loan, and had a successful season, scoring 14 goals and getting 11 assists in all competitions.



But Barca only reached the quarter-finals of the UCL before being knocked out by Atletico Madrid.

This summer they have made three PL signings. Anthony Gordon, Rodri and Gabriel Jesus.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Gordon and Rodri in particular have been signed as two of the key players in the squad.

Rodri is of course a Ballon d’Or winner and won the Player of the Tournament as Spain won this year’s World Cup, while Gordon was signed for £69million.



The former Newcastle winger has had a fantastic start to the new season, registering five assists in his first four La Liga games.

Incredibly, the last player to achieve those number was a certain academy product called Lionel Messi…

After the 2-0 home win over Athletic Club a couple of weeks ago, the home fans chanted his name. He is already a certified fan favourite.

There is real belief around the club that their Premier League reinforcements can push them to European glory.



Barcelona kick off their UCL campaign against Feyenoord, and will be hoping this is the season they finally lift the UCL trophy again.

Sports.title: Ryan Giggs reveals Man Utd REJECTED chance to sign Kylian Mbappe in one of Red Devils’ most costly mistakes ever
Sports.content:
RYAN Giggs has revealed that Manchester United turned down the opportunity to sign Kylian Mbappe – after he got a tip-off on the beach.

Giggs, speaking on the Rio Ferdinand Presents podcast, said that he was made aware of Mbappe when he was United’s assistant manager between 2014-2016.



He said: “So, I’m in the south of France. I was coaching United, so it’d be 2015. I’ve been for a walk in the local village and I’m walking back to the hotel.

“I’m walking on the beach back to the hotel. And I can feel someone following me. I get to the hotel and then all of a sudden I can feel someone coming up to me. Anyway, this guy is called Lionel, French guy.



“So he comes up to me and says ‘hi, I’m Lionel. I just wanted to just say hello. I’m a big United fan and big fan of yours. But I watch a lot of youth football in France, and you have to look at this player.

‘He’s called Kylian Mbappé. He’s at Monaco and I think he’s a player for Man United.’



“A few weeks later, he emailed me all the details. So me and Albert [Stuivenberg] again, who’s the coach with Arsenal, he was another assistant at United at the time.

“We used to in the afternoons just go and watch games or go and watch players at the training ground. So anyway, I’ve told him about this thing. He says ‘come on, let’s look him up.’

“And we watch a few Monaco youth games and we saw him and just went, ‘wow, what is this?’ You know, you can see players and they can be special, but he did look exceptional.

“So anyway, we told the scouting team. They went to watch him. Someone in France went to watch him and he was actually playing PSG. Monaco were playing PSG.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“So they went to Paris to watch him. Anyway, I think a few weeks later, I said to the guy ‘how did it go?’ and he went ‘yeah, they weren’t too sure about him, so we just left it, and that was it.'”

Mbappé actually went on to join PSG on loan in 2017 before joining permanently the next year for around £170m.

Sports.title: Premier League referees got THREE calls wrong including Arsenal penalty incident and controversial red card decision
Sports.content:
PREM officials got THREE calls wrong in the second round of matches.

But only ONE of them should have been overturned by VAR.



And that should have led to a penalty for Arsenal – and a red card for Aston Villa’s Ian Maatsen.

This season the League is publishing the verdicts of the Key Match Incident panel of former refs, players and coaches.



The panel assesses every major call on goals, penalties and red cards made over the Prem season.

And while the majority of decisions made in week two were backed, the panel felt that Arsenal were wrongly denied a stoppage time penalty in their 1-0 win at Villa Park.



Bruno Guimaraes went down under a scissors-style split leg tackle from Dutch defender Maatsen, who had been previously booked.

Ref Jared Gillett waved play on but that was a mistake which should have been rectified by the VAR, James Bell.

The panel said: “A penalty should have been awarded on-field for Maatsen’s reckless challenge on Guimaraes.

“Clear contact was made on the attacker’s standing leg and Maatsen made no contact with the ball.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“They also felt that VAR should have intervened as the non-penalty award was a clear and obvious error.”

That would also have brought a second yellow and therefore a red card for Maatsen.

But while the panel assessed two other major mistakes, they were NOT found to have met the threshold for an intervention.

The first was Nottingham Forest’s controversial penalty in their 2-2 draw at Anfield.



Sam Barrott gave a spot kick, converted by Morgan Gibbs-White, after he was sent flying by Allison after his shot was sent wide of the goal.

While the call was confirmed by VAR the panel ruled: “The referee’s call of a penalty was incorrect on-field.

“The contact from Alisson was inevitable as a consequence of his momentum in attempting to save the ball – the contact made was not reckless and below the threshold for a penalty.

“However, the nonintervention by the VAR was unanimously supported on the basis that it was not a clear and obvious error.”



And the other was in Brentford’s draw at Leeds, when the Bees felt they should have had a spot kick for a foul by Jayden Bogle on Kevin Schade.

The verdict was: “The panel felt that a penalty should have been awarded.

“There was foot on foot contact instigated by Bogle with enough contact for a penalty kick.

“However, given the high threshold for VAR intervention, the panel felt the referee’s call should remain on-field as it wasn’t a clear and obvious error.”



The other controversial calls, including the decision not to award Spurs a penalty when new signing Omar Marmoush went down under a challenge from Newcastle’s Malick Thiaw, were backed.

While one panel member felt it WAS a penalty, the other four disagreed and the panel said: “There was a genuine challenge for the ball by Thiaw with some contact made with Marmoush, but this was below the threshold for a penalty kick.”

And Manchester United’s second goal in the 5-2 win over Ipswich, after Harry Maguire handled outside the box before his shot led to an own goal by Jacob Greaves, was also confirmed as the correct call.

The panel decision was: “Maguire’s arms are within his bodyline meaning that the contact with his right arm was accidental and not a punishable handball offence given that Maguire was not the goal scorer.

“The shot was clearly off target and then deflected in via the defender for a clear own goal. The panel supported the referee’s call to award the goal, 4:1, with one panellist considering the handball to be deliberate.”

Sports.title: Major Chelsea team news hint as rarely-seen summer transfer signing looks set to start vs Leeds in Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
CHELSEA have dropped a major team news hint ahead of tonight’s Carabao Cup clash with Leeds.

Blockbuster summer signing Danny Welbeck looks set to start after being splashed across the front of the club’s matchday programme.



The former Manchester United and Arsenal striker joined Xabi Alonso’s squad in the summer but has only featured twice so far.

Welbeck started in the last round against Luton and even marked his Blues debut with a goal.



Now, his place on the front of tonight’s programme is another big clue he could lead the line again.

The 35-year-old headed home Chelsea’s opener in their 2-0 win over Luton at Stamford Bridge.

Welbeck admitted getting off the mark on his debut made the night even sweeter.

He said: “It was really nice (to score).

“I mean, it makes for a good start and it’s something that I’m looking to continue to build upon.

“Obviously, it was my debut at Stamford Bridge for Chelsea and it’s an honourable moment for me.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“So to kick it off with a goal was very pleasing.

“I feel very privileged to make the switch to Chelsea. It’s such a big club.

“At this stage of my career, it’s massive. I’m very honoured to receive the chance to come here and to be a part of this project.

“It’s exciting and one where I feel we can build something special.”

Welbeck was on the bench for both of Chelsea’s first two Prem games, when they overcame Fulham and Brighton.



And the Englishman only came on in the dying minutes of Chelsea’s 2-1 defeat to Arsenal.

In the programme’s exclusive, Welbeck also brushed off any talk about his age following his summer switch.

He said: “A little bit of talk is about my age, but it’s just talk. I’m here to push on, to improve.



“I feel really good – fit, strong, and obviously last season I had my best goalscoring season. I’m ready to push on.”

Chelsea do still have other options up front, with Emanuel Emegha in the first-team squad and Joao Pedro also available.

But after Welbeck started the last round, his spot on tonight’s cover feels like a pretty big hint he could get the nod again.

Leeds have already gone further than last time around when they exited in the second round following a penalty shootout defeat to Sheffield Wednesday.

Chelsea, on the other hand, made it to the semi-finals before they were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal.

Sports.title: Man Utd boss Michael Carrick’s brother confirmed as coach within Tuchel’s England set-up ahead of next fixtures
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK’S younger brother has landed a job in England’s coaching set-up.

Graeme Carrick, 41, has been named in the FA‘s official coaching line-up which was published on Wednesday.



He will be an assistant to England Under-17s head coach Barry Lewtas as they bid for Euro glory.

Qualifiers are set to kick off in November ahead of the UEFA U17 Euro Finals in Latvia next year.



Carrick is joined in the Under-17s camp by fellow assistant Matt Thorpe and goalkeeping coach Matt Doyle.

They will be jointly responsible for developing some of the most promising talents in the country who could eventually feed into Thomas Tuchel‘s senior side.

The most recent Under-17s squad featured the likes of Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel and Chelsea starlet Ryan Kavuma-McQueen.

Graeme’s football career was cut short by injuries as a youngster while Man Utd boss Michael went on to enjoy great success with the likes of Tottenham, the Red Devils and England.

The younger of the siblings dove straight into coaching and took on roles with Newcastle’s youth teams and the FA’s elite youth development sides.

Sports.content:
ANTHONY MARTIAL is wanted by THREE European clubs after Everton baulked at bringing in the former Manchester United striker.

The Frenchman, 30, is looking for a fresh start since leaving Mexican side Monterrey as a free agent.



Two Ligue 1 clubs are said to have already put firm contract offers on the table, while Spanish side Malaga are also weighing up a move.

According to Foot Mercato, the identities of the two French sides have not been revealed.



But Nice and Lens have reportedly been ruled out of the running.

One is fighting near the top of the table, while the other is battling relegation.

Neither were prepared to guarantee Martial a starting spot, instead both are hoping his experience could help their younger players.

Martial turned down BOTH offers as he waits for the right move.

Malaga have since emerged as another possible destination for the former United forward, according to Marca’s Matteo Moretto.

The Spanish side are considering adding Martial to their attack after being offered the chance to sign him.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Everton have also been given the chance to bring him back to the Premier League on a free.

Martial spent nine years at Old Trafford after joining from Monaco in 2015 and famously scored against Liverpool on his debut.

He went on to score 90 goals in 317 appearances for the Red Devils before leaving in 2024.

Martial peaked in the 2019/20 season when he became Ole Gunnar Solskjaer‘s talisman in attack.

And while spells at AEK Athens and Monterrey followed, neither stint really got his career going again.



Martial has not played a competitive match since March but can still join a new club as a free agent.

Sports.title: Tottenham’s ‘next Harry Kane’ finally fulfilling potential as he lights up Spain after shunning Premier League return
Sports.content:
TROY PARROTT is finally living up to his Harry Kane comparisons – if his match-winning finish in the Champions League is anything to go by.

The former Spurs wonderkid blasted home a strike Kane would have been proud of to help Real Betis beat Lille 3-2 in Europe’s premier club competition on Tuesday night.



It came four days after Parrott fired a late winner to inflict Real Madrid’s first La Liga defeat of the season and get one over his old boss Jose Mourinho.

Safe to say it has been some week for Parrott, who at 24 is threatening to develop into the centre-forward he was tipped to be in North London nearly a decade ago.



Spurs picked up the Dubliner from Belvedere in the Republic of Ireland capital in 2017 and it was not long before fans started calling for him to be given a chance in the first team.

Being a striker with an eye for goal, comparisons to Kane quickly followed, with many feeling Parrott to be the best thing to come through the Spurs academy since the England star.

Mauricio Pochettino awarded the youngster his debut in a memorable game – albeit not for good reasons for Spurs – as the Premier League giants lost on penalties to League Two Colchester in the Carabao Cup.

It was the biggest upset of Poch’s career and seven weeks later he was sacked.

In came Mourinho, who gave Parrott his Premier League debut as a late sub in a 5-0 win over Burnley in December 2019 – a game famous for Son Heung-min’s Puskas Award-winning wondergoal.

Despite that stunning strike, it was Parrott whom Mourinho was photographed giving the matchball to at the final whistle, to mark his bow.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But the Portuguese also took a tough love approach with Parrott, criticising the starlet’s attitude when he played for the Under-23s in a similar way to how he dealt with a young Scott McTominay at Manchester United.

Explaining in March 2020 why Parrott was “not ready” for regular first-team football, Mourinho said: “Every time he was playing with the kids, he was playing with the mentality of, ‘I shouldn’t be here’ or, ‘I am too good to be here.’

“I had exactly the same words with Scott McTominay. He was not loved in his age group because he was not there with the right frame of mind. The moment we started changing that lots of things started changing for him.

“Troy cannot go there [the under‑age teams] with discontent, contempt. It is a process.”

When Parrott missed a penalty in an FA Cup shootout defeat to Norwich that month, Mourinho excused the spot-kick but not the forward’s extra-time cameo.



The Special One added: “Now people can see that he has to work a lot, so don’t think that Parrott is the second Harry Kane because he’s just a young kid that needs to work.”

Like Kane did as a youngster, Parrott then underwent a series of lower-league loans to Millwall, Ipswich, MK Dons and Preston.

But it was when he was farmed out to the Netherlands that his career began to kick on.

A temporary and prolific spell with Excelsior led to a £6.7million switch to AZ Alkmaar, where Parrott smashed in 51 goals in 97 games.



He gave Spurs a rough time when facing his old side on their way to the Europa League title two seasons ago.

The day before giving Ange Postecoglou’s side the runaround, Parrot was asked about his Spurs exit and said: “I definitely have no regrets. For me it just didn’t happen. I’m OK with that.



“I was ready to move on and I think the club were also ready to move on. I thought it was the perfect time to do so.

“I look back (at my time with Spurs) with a smile. It’s a place where I grew up.”

There was talk of a return to England this summer but SunSport understands Parrott was never that keen on coming back as he enjoys playing in Europe and away from the intense spotlight of the Premier League.

Instead, his continental adventure continued as he was sold for £17.7m to Betis, a club boasting nine ex-Prem players including Hector Bellerin, Giovani Lo Celso and Antony and bossed by ex-Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini.

Then Parrott came to the world’s attention by firing home on the rebound to see off Mourinho’s Real 1-0 on Friday night.



His post-match interview had the hallmarks of Irish legend Roy Keane’s famous “That’s his job” comment as he said: “That’s a striker’s job, to go in after the ball and hope it will fall in front of me.”

But it was Parrott’s winner over Lille that showed his Kane-like lethal finishing, racing away from a defender via step-over before a belting, left-footed finish into the far corner.

It had Joe Cole waxing lyrical on punditry, with the former England star branding Parrott’s goal “almost Harry Kane like” and predicting that the “big guns will be circling” around the forward soon enough.

Parrott admitted in 2022 to stealing technique tips from Kane when the pair were at Spurs together, commenting: “Obviously, I want to be my own player.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But Kane is so good in terms of his finishing, his passing – why wouldn’t I try and take little bits from there?”



Over the course of a mouthwatering week in January, Parrott will get the chance to see how far he has come when he takes on Kane’s Bayern Munich in the Champions League, just days after playing Arsenal and a Mourinho re-match at the Bernabeu.

Sports.title: Premier League panel's Liverpool verdict is laughable and makes mockery of VAR
Sports.content:
Premier League panel's Liverpool verdict is laughable and makes mockery of VAR

A Premier League panel has ruled that Nottingham Forest's penalty against Liverpool last month shouldn't have been awarded - but nor should it have been overturned

View 2 Images Liverpool were furious with Samuel Barrott's decision (Image: Dan Mullan/Getty Images)

Making a mockery of VAR is not that difficult these days. Even in these so-called modern times which continue to embrace ancient but now traditional mistakes.

But this hasn't stopped the Premier League panel from rubbing the nose of a VAR system it continues to tolerate right in the dirt. The latest ruling has decreed Nottingham Forest should not have been awarded a penalty at Liverpool following Alisson's challenge on Neco Williams.

Yet the League's 'Key Match Incidents' (KMI) panel insisted the decision did not reach the threshold for a VAR intervention. So, Michael Oliver was correct not to send referee Sam Barrott to the pitch-side monitor.

The decision helped Forest go 2-1 ahead before a late equaliser saw Liverpool salvage a point. The KMI Panel voted that Barrott should not have given the penalty, but supported the VAR outcome.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

It said: "The contact from Alisson was inevitable as a consequence of his momentum in attempting to save the ball. The contact made was not reckless and below the threshold for a penalty.

"However, the non intervention by the VAR was unanimously supported, on the basis that it was not a clear and obvious error."

Confused yet? Well, here might be a simple explanation to the umpteenth incident in top-flight football to leave a farcical and lasting stain on its current reputation.

The verdict is laughable, because it is essentially admitting not one mistake has been made but two - yet those making them continue to be right. Go figure.

Barrott got it wrong in awarding a penalty in the first place. Then Oliver compounded the mistake by making one of his own, having decided not to send Barrott to the monitor to correct his original blunder.

Should the Premier League scrap VAR? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Alisson was deemed to have fouled Neco Williams (Image: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

Which begs the question - if VAR cannot be used to review or correct potential mistakes, what is the point of it in the first place? The simple answer is, there isn't one.

The introduction of the 'clear and obvious' threshold, which appears ironic in itself, has become the biggest cancer of the VAR era. VAR is supposed to exist to enable officials to make correct decisions.

But according to all of the above, cannot be used when referees make mistakes which are deemed to be too minor. Like costing Liverpool three points at Anfield, right?

The incident involving Alisson and Williams is the kind of scenario VAR was invented for to resolve. Instead, it has made itself, those officials involved, and the English game, look laughable.

Arsenal sign Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge in the summer and, after making such an immediate impact, those from the Premier League club were keen to compliment the Belgian side when they crossed paths

Arsenal officials have been so impressed with Christos Tzolis that they've been telling Club Brugge president Bart Verhaeghe about his exploits.

The Greek winger made a £34million move to the Emirates this summer following two hugely impressive seasons with the Belgian club, where he scored 43 times. Tzolis has gone straight into the Arsenal starting XI and immediately made an impression.

‌

Arsenal executives came across their Club Brugge counterparts when they headed to the Champions League draw and it was there that they made it known how much of an impact Tzolis has already has.

Sports.title: Ethan Nwaneri suffers ultimate humiliation as Dortmund boss moves to set record straight
Sports.content:
Ethan Nwaneri suffers ultimate humiliation as Dortmund boss moves to set record straight

Ethan Nwaneri was substituted in Borussia Dortmund's Champions League clash with Villarreal, but manager Niko Kovac insisted the decision was not performance-related

View 2 Images Ethan Nwaneri was subbed on and off by Borussia Dortmund (Image: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Ethan Nwaneri was faced with being substituted by Borussia Dortmund after coming off the bench earlier in the match in their victory over Villarreal in the Champions League. However, Niko Kovac has insisted the decision was no cause for concern, with the teenager delivering a 'really good' display.

‌



Nwaneri, on loan at BVB from Arsenal, was introduced after just 27 minutes when Konstantinos Karetsas required medical attention for what was subsequently described as a circulation issue. The 18-year-old was carried from the field on a stretcher before being taken immediately to the hospital in distressing scenes at the Westfalenstadion.

‌



Karetsas, who joined Dortmund from Genk in the summer, was making his fifth appearance for the club. The German side said: "Konstantinos Karetsas had to leave the pitch in the game against Villarreal due to circulation problems. Kosta is doing as well as can be expected given the circumstances, and he is on his way to the hospital for further examinations."

‌



The unfortunate issue provided Nwaneri with an opportunity to impress, and he looked to take it as Dortmund secured a 3-2 victory. The youngster registered the joint-most shots, joint-most dribbles and joint-most tackles for the Bundesliga side during his spell on the field.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Despite that influence, Nwaneri was withdrawn after Serhou Guirassy fired Dortmund 2-1 in front. Former Chelsea and Aston Villa ace Carney Chukwuemeka came on for the 19-year-old in the 82nd minute, after Nwaneri had been on the pitch less than 60 minutes.

‌



It is normally a source of embarrassment for players to be subbed on and off in the same match, but the Dortmund boss insisted that Nwaneri clocked up a comparable amount of playing time as he would have done had he been in the starting XI. "He gave everything. If he had started the game, he probably would have come off around the 60th minute," Kovac said.

When questioned whether the decision was linked to Nwaneri's performance, he added: "Quite the opposite, he was really good," Kovac emphasised.

‌

"It was great that he was able to have an impact on the team in such a short time."

After the final whistle, Nwaneri appeared far from downbeat, taking to Instagram to reflect on the victory, writing: "Great team spirit, onto Saturday."

‌



His post was met with a wave of backing from fellow players, with Jobe Bellingham and Waldemar Anton both responding with a string of smiling face with heart-eyes emojis.

Chukwuemeka chimed in with: "My boyy," accompanied by a red heart, while forward Fabio Silva kept it simple, posting: "So good."

Former Arsenal player and Ajax chief Marc Overmars has announced he's stepping away from his role at Royal Antwerp due to a serious health condition

Marc Overmars has confirmed he will leave his role as sporting director of Royal Antwerp FC with immediate effect citing major health issues as he claimed he "must listen to his body".

The former Arsenal star, who won the Premier League in 1998 before moving to Barcelona, has forged an impressive reputation off the pitch. He was key in assembling the Ajax side of 2019 that reached the semi-finals of the Champions League with Frenkie de Jong and Matthijs de Ligt in their ranks.

‌



But Overmars' health will force him to leave the game, at least for now, as he opened up on his struggles and his decision in an open letter.

Sports.title: Premier League panel admit Arsenal referee error with unanimous verdict reached
Sports.content:
Premier League panel admit Arsenal referee error with unanimous verdict reached

The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel has ruled on a controversial Arsenal decision in the Premier League and have decided the referee made an error

View 2 Images Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty, according to the Premier League (Image: James Fearn/Getty Images)

Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty in their Premier League clash against Aston Villa. The top-flight Key Match Incidents Panel came to a unanimous verdict in establishing that Ian Maatsen fouled Bruno Guimaraes.

‌



The Gunners' Brazilian summer signing was brought down inside the area in the 98th minute of Arsenal's victory, but a penalty was not awarded by Jarred Gillett, and VAR did not choose to refer the decision to review. The Arsenal midfielder screamed to be awarded a spot-kick but to no avail.

‌



The moment proved not to be too controversial as Arsenal came away 1-0 victors thanks to Bukayo Saka's strike. However, it appears the north London side were denied an opportunity to extend their lead.

‌



The Key Match Incident Panel is an independent group of five members: three former players or coaches, one Premier League representative, and one from ProRef. They offer an independent assessment of key decisions in every Premier League match.

The KMI Panel said: "The panel felt that a penalty should have been awarded on-field for Maatsen’s reckless challenge on Guimaraes. Clear contact was made on the attacker’s standing leg and Maatsen made no contact with the ball."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



They also believe the failure to award the penalty was a clear and obvious error. The Premier League added: "They (KMI panel) also felt that VAR should have intervened as the non-penalty awarded was a clear and obvious error. The panel felt that the challenge was reckless and therefore a second caution should have been awarded.

Speaking earlier this week, former Select Group referee Andy Davies given an insight into VAR James Bell's likely process to ESPN. "VAR James Bell clearly applied the new "high bar" for intervention when he cleared this decision, taking the view that the referee's on-field decision not to award a penalty to Arsenal was not a clear and obvious error," he said.

Davies came to the same conclusion as the KMI Panel, however. "The decision by Villa's Maatsen to challenge in the nature he did, from behind with a scissor action and no opportunity to play the ball was a poor one," he explained.

‌



"By making contact only with Guimarães and none on the ball, there can be little doubt that it met the threshold for a foul -- and it took place inside the penalty box.

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes was challenged by Ian Maatsen (Image: Naomi Baker/Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"The surprising non-intervention by VAR is a result of the Premier League's desire this season to have less involvement and only very clear errors to be corrected, with a new "higher bar" for interventions to be applied.

"It's a positive principle that should result in less time spent re-litigating decisions, yes. However, this was clearly a mistake from the on-field referee not to award a penalty and, in my opinion, this was an intervention that has been missed by the VAR team.

"Arsenal winning the game will cover the narrative to some degree, however, if this was a deciding moment that cost Arsenal all three points, the profile of the incident would've been significant."

‌



The Premier League revealed that in the second week of action there were 21 referee key match incidents. Of those 76 per cent were deemed to be correct decisions on the field, with the value rising to 90 per cent following VAR reviews.

The panel established that two VAR reviews resulting in overturns were proven to be correct, while the challenge on Guimaraes was the only missed VAR intervention.

Sports.content:
Seven players could miss Napoli vs Arsenal through injury as surgery confirmed in statement

Arsenal and Napoli are both missing multiple players for their first match in the league phase of this season's Champions League, as injuries are already biting

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta's Arsenal are dealing with multiple injury issues in defence ahead of ther clash with Napoli (Image: James Fearn, Getty Images)

Several players may miss Arsenal's Champions League match against Napoli due to injury. The Gunners continue to deal with multiple absences in their squad, while the Serie A side also have a similar number of setbacks to contend with.

‌



Mikel Arteta was sent off the last time Arsenal played a Champions League match in Naples, with Gonzalo Higuain and Jose Callejon firing Rafael Benítez's team to a 2-0 win in December 2013. However, they have won in Campania since.

‌



Unai Emery guided them to a 1-0 win during the Europa League semi-finals in 2019. Arteta will hope to right the wrongs of nearly 13 years ago tonight.

‌



Arsenal escape UEFA fine after being forced to cancel Champions League press conference READ MORE :

Scott McTominay health update as Napoli issue statement following heart surgery READ MORE :

However, the Gunners remain without William Saliba. He is still recovering from a back injury sustained while on international duty with France during the summer's World Cup.

Cristhian Mosquera has, meanwhile, been nursing a muscle problem over the past week, which forced the centre-back to sit out Arsenal's Premier League victory over Chelsea at the weekend. Arteta, however, hinted that the decision to leave Mosquera out of the matchday squad at Emirates Stadium was largely precautionary.

Arteta said: "He had a muscular issue. We think it is not too much, but we need to wait and see in the next few days how it evolves."

‌



View 2 Images Defender Jurrien Timber is training with his Arsenal team-mates again (Image: David Price, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Jurrien Timber is yet to pull on an Arsenal shirt this season following minor surgery during the summer. However, he has been putting in the hard yards on the training pitch ahead of this week's fixture.

Arteta offered an encouraging update on Timber's fitness last week when quizzed about the Netherlands international's rehabilitation. The Arsenal boss said: "He's in really good condition at the moment, he's been a few weeks on the pitch and has been training with us, so he's in a really good place."

‌



Napoli will also be missing several key figures when they host Arsenal. Scott McTominay, notably, is ruled out.

‌



"On Tuesday morning, Scott McTominay underwent an ablation procedure at Spire Manchester Hospital. The operation was a complete success," Napoli confirmed in a statement on Tuesday. "McTominay will rest for two weeks and then resume training."

Napoli will further be deprived of Luca Marianucci, who sustained a knee injury during pre-season and is set for a stint on the treatment table. Giovane underwent a hernia operation earlier in the summer and remains sidelined, while Alessandro Buongiorno is also unavailable owing to a knee injury.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher leaves Micah Richards in stitches with bankruptcy joke on live TV
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher leaves Micah Richards in stitches with bankruptcy joke on live TV

Jamie Carragher faces being declared bankrupt but was able to make light of the situation whilst being a pundit on CBS - with Micah Richards seeing the funny side

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher mocked his own financial struggles whilst on CBS (Image: CBS Sports)

Jamie Carragher was able to make fun of his own financial problems live on air - which had Micah Richards laughing as they dissected the night's Champions League talking points.

‌



Carragher was back fulfilling his usual role with CBS, where he covers Europe's biggest club competition. He's also a regular on Sky Sports having forged an impressive punditry career for himself since retiring.

‌



However the ex-Liverpool defender has found himself in hot water with the tax man and it was recently revealed that he faces being declared bankrupt over an unpaid tax bill, thought to be in the region of £700,000 and £800,000.

‌



Carragher made reference to his personal situation when discussing Barcelona. The La Liga champions made the last eight of the Champions League last season but haven't lifted the trophy since 2015 - and Carragher wants to see them back after a period of financial difficulty.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



He said on CBS: "I think it's about time we saw Barcelona back in terms of competing where they should be, one of the best teams in the world, one of the biggest teams in the world. They've had their financial problems haven't they?"

After a slight pause he then goes: "Haven't we all.." which promoted laughter from Richards and a smile from host Kate Abdo.

View 2 Images A bankruptcy case has been filed against Jamie Carragher (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

‌



A case has been filed against James Lee Duncan Carragher, reports the BBC, and a spokesperson for the former footballer said: "This is a private tax matter that should have been resolved sooner, and the appropriate steps are being taken today to settle it. It is understood that the matter will not proceed any further and will be resolved imminently."

Last September, it was revealed that up to 200 footballers may have lost tens of millions of pounds, with some losing their homes and being made bankrupt.

Carragher went on to say that, if it isn't Liverpool, he would love to see Barcelona claim Europe's top honour. They begin their campaign at home to Feyenoord on Wednesday evening ahead of playing two English sides in Aston Villa and Manchester City later in the competition.
