Thank you for your feedback.

In the end, it was a blend of old and new faces that got Villa over the line. Zion Suzuki made a couple of fine saves, João Gomes put in a typically tigerish performance and Jackson got the goal an encouraging all-round display deserved. The 19-year-old George Hemmings did not look out of place on his Champions League debut. “The old players need to keep our standards high, to show everybody this is the only way we can achieve the process in our objectives and targets,” Emery said. “I am so happy.”

Pau Torres was the unlikely catalyst for two of Villa’s three first-half goals. McGinn’s opener was a product of the centre-back roaming unchallenged to the edge of the box. Presumably it crossed Torres’s mind to shoot, though just as he was getting giddy, he spread play to McGinn, who guided a superb first-time, left-foot strike into the far corner of Yann Sommer’s goal. In starting on Tuesday night, the Swiss became just the second goalkeeper to represent five clubs in the Champions League, but it was a night to forget for the 37-year-old.

View image in fullscreen John McGinn punches the air after giving Aston Villa an 11th-minute lead. Photograph: PA Wire/PA

Club Brugge replied when the lively Jan Virgili found a way past Wan-Bissaka – who was making his full Villa debut – and located Hugo Vetlesen in the box, the Norway midfielder sending a crisp finish beyond Suzuki. The hosts were level for less than three minutes, a slick Villa move culminating in Buendía wheeling away in celebration. Jackson’s deft backheel supplied Gomes, who twisted inside the box and then picked out Buendía who did the rest.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Villa’s third arrived a few minutes before the interval. Emery punched the air, his delight at establishing a two-goal advantage plain to see. Torres collected the ball on the edge of the Villa 18-yard box and, after shifting the ball out of his feet, he sent a lofted pass spinning into the opposition half, where Jackson got in between the opposition centre-backs, Lee Han-beom and Brandon Mechele. Enter Sommer, who raced about 40 yards from goal. Jackson swiped the ball cleanly and then was too strong for Lee before passing into an empty net.

Things appeared rosy, but Villa had to withstand heavy pressure after a video assistant referee review led the Swiss referee, Sandro Schärer, to penalise Wan-Bissaka for handball in the box. Nicolò Tresoldi sent Suzuki the wrong way from the penalty spot and a few minutes later Suzuki pushed another shot on to the post.

Victor Lindelöf tested the nerves of Emery, slicing a routine clearance when attempting to relieve the pressure. Villa, too, had chances, Jackson getting a shot away after latching on to a McGinn pass and Bogarde had a shot cleared off the line by the home full-back Joaquin Seys.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi is set to buy Spanish second-division club Eldense - as Argentina icon continues to grow his footballing empire while still playing
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi is set to buy Spanish second-division club Eldense - as Argentina icon continues to grow his footballing empire while still playing

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Lionel Messi has reached an agreement in principle to become the owner of second-division Spanish side Eldense, Daily Mail Sport can confirm.

Messi is set to acquire the shares currently held by Colombian investment group Grupo TH, making him the club's majority shareholder.

The deal is expected to be finalised in the coming days once the final legal and contractual procedures are completed and it has received approval from Spain's High Council for Sport (CSD). The financial terms of the transaction have not been disclosed.

The Valencia-based outfit were promoted to the second division at the end of last season and have faced a difficult start to their campaign, picking up two points in the opening four games. Their coach Claudio Barragan was sacked earlier this week, leaving the club without a manager.

Messi's acquisition of Eldense marks the latest venture in the 39-year-old Argentinian star's growing football empire.

A few months ago Messi purchased a 100 per cent stake in another Spanish side, UE Cornella, a semi-professional outfit located on the outskirts of Barcelona.

UE Cornella, founded in 1951, play in Spain's fifth tier, and the club said Messi's arrival marked the beginning of a new chapter in its history, aimed at driving both sporting and institutional growth, strengthening its foundations and continuing to invest in talent.

Lionel Messi has reached an agreement in principle to become the owner of second-division Spanish side Eldense, Daily Mail Sport can confirm

View this post on Instagram

They added: 'The project is guided by a long-term vision and a strategic plan that combines ambition, sustainability, and a strong connection to its local roots.'

Messi, who recently announced his international retirement following Argentina's defeat in the World Cup final, has further investments elsewhere, although neither matches the scale of his two Spanish investments.

He co-owns Uruguay side Deportivo LSM alongside Inter Miami team-mate Luis Suarez. He also holds a direct equity option in his MLS team, Inter Miami, which allows him to buy a partial ownership stake in the club after his playing career ends.

As his empire grows, however, he could face a potential stumbling block.

Eldense and Cornella are currently separated by three divisions, but it is unlikely the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) would allow both teams to compete in the same division if the two clubs were ever to reach that point.

Eldense, founded in 1921, have spent most of their history outside the top two divisions of Spanish football.

They were promoted to the second tier for the first time since 1964 in 2023, suffered relegation in 2025 and secured an immediate return this past summer.

They play their home games at the Nuevo Pepico Amat, a 5,776-capacity stadium in the city of Elda.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes hints at World Cup fallout between England duo Declan Rice and Morgan Rogers as possible reason pair were involved in furious incident during Arsenal's win vs Chelsea
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes hints at World Cup fallout between England duo Declan Rice and Morgan Rogers as possible reason pair were involved in furious incident during Arsenal's win vs Chelsea

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Paul Scholes has suggested there may be some history between Declan Rice and Morgan Rogers after the England team-mates clashed at the Emirates on Sunday.

Arsenal's Rice infuriated the Chelsea man during the closing stages of Sunday's pulsating London derby, which Arsenal won 2-1.

Rogers, a £117million summer signing from Aston Villa, was looking to get up to support Cole Palmer as Chelsea pushed to get back into the game. But a cynical trip from Rice put an end to that, with Rogers tumbling to the ground.

The 24-year-old was incandescent with rage and confronted Rice, jabbing his finger at him before the players were separated by referee Chris Kavanagh.

It left onlookers shocked given the two midfielders were key components in England's run to the semi-finals of the World Cup over the summer.

'Do you think there's a little bit of something between Morgan Rogers and Declan Rice?' Scholes asked his former Manchester United team-mate Nicky Butt on their The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast, sponsored by Midnite.

Morgan Rogers was trying to get up in support of Cole Palmer when Declan Rice tripped him

A melee ensued after Rogers had reacted and attempted to confront the Arsenal man

Rogers jabbed his finger in the face of his opponent before referee Chris Kavanagh intervened

'Do you think there might have been a little bit of something during the summer? What Declan Rice did to him was the most annoying thing in the world.

'When people just leg you up when you're running. He snapped, Morgan Rogers, and rightly so.'

Rogers had opened the scoring against the champions in the second minute with a volley after the Gunners failed to clear Reece James' free-kick. That was cancelled out by Kai Havertz midway through the first half, before Martin Odegaard netted the winner for the Gunners.

So annoyed was playmaker Rogers that he refused Rice's olive branch after the final whistle and also showed little interest in former Villa team-mate Ezri Konsa's offer of a handshake.

Rogers had been linked with a move to Arsenal before Chelsea moved in to make him the most expensive-ever British player, just surpassing the fee Manchester City paid for another England midfielder, Elliot Anderson, earlier in the window.

Konsa said afterwards: 'I love duels. As a defender, I think these are things you have to cherish.

'For me personally, I love a challenge. I love being in duels. I had a few today and I'm glad I came out on top.

'Rogers is a good friend of mine, but on the pitch, it's a different story. I saw the opportunity to go in and make the tackle and it came off.'

Sports.title: Thanks, Dad! Man City star Erling Haaland credits his father, Alfie, for helping to improve his headers - after practising with him in the garden over the summer
Sports.content:
Thanks, Dad! Man City star Erling Haaland credits his father, Alfie, for helping to improve his headers - after practising with him in the garden over the summer

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Erling Haaland’s recent flurry of headed goals have come from perfecting the art with his father in the garden.

The Manchester City striker managed to score six headers last season but now has three in his last three matches – including the first of a brace in Porto as Enzo Maresca’s side opened their Champions League campaign with a victory on Tuesday.

Haaland pinpointed his aerial ability as something to improve after sealing a move to the Etihad Stadium in 2022 and believes it has now added another string to his bow.

And the dedication has extended to impromptu sessions with Alfie Haaland at home in Cheshire, seemingly recreating scenes of his childhood.

‘Over the years, I’ve worked a lot on my heading,’ Haaland said. ‘I’ve improved it massively and it’s become a strength of my game. I think a lot of it comes down to experience.'

The first goal of Erling Haaland's brace against Porto was an excellent header

Erling's father, Alfie, played 47 times for City during his career

Haaland has 37 career headed goals in club football, just over 10 per cent of his overall haul and added: ‘Actually, two days ago I was practising headers with my dad in the garden.’

The 26-year-old, who is now City’s third highest scorer of all time, could have left Portugal with a hat-trick and became embroiled in the heated scenes at Estadio do Dragao.

HAALAND BY NUMBERS His incredible goalscoring record in club football: Left foot - 221 goals Right foot - 43 goals Head - 37 goals Other - 1 goal TOTAL: 302 goals

Haaland was cautioned after tussling with Pablo Rosario late in the game and claims that the midfielder wanted to stop him by any means necessary.

‘I was really keen on a hat-trick and it seemed like he [Rosario] was very eager to stop me from getting it,’ Haaland told TV 2. ‘It was a little interesting, that. You'll be seeing a picture where he's grabbing my bottom... it’ll be interesting to see that picture.’

Both sets of players had to be dragged away from each other in the tunnel at half time, with Marcus Bettinelli understood to have been pushed by Porto officials after the home team were incensed by refereeing decisions.

UEFA’s disciplinary committee are assessing reports by the match delegate and referee Szymon Marciniak to ascertain whether any action is necessary. The punishment for any guilty party is likely to amount to a fine.

Sports.title: Carlos Alcaraz's vomit-stained 3.33am nightmare in New York! Defending champion throws up into a towel as he's knocked out of US Open by Ben Shelton in latest ever finish to a match
Sports.content:
Behind the baseline inside Arthur Ashe Stadium, the clocks ticked beyond 2:50am. It was Wednesday morning. A school day. Sunrise was only a few hours away. And yet? With the help of several thousand New Yorkers - some drunk, some asleep, the rest simply delirious - Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton dragged the US Open into uncharted waters.

Never in history had a match here finished this late. Never before had these two put on such a spectacle. But after four and a half sets and nearly four hours, the curtain refused to fall on this quarterfinal.

It was exhausting. It was intoxicating. And for Alcaraz, it was sickening. Before the start of the deciding set, the defending champion appeared to vomit into his towel. But still it went on. All the way until road's end: a fifth-set tiebreak.

All the way until 3:33am, when after four hours and 28 minutes, Ben Shelton fired down an 146mph ace, stuck out his tongue, pulled Alcaraz into a long embrace and then - at long, long last - soaked up the biggest moment of his young career.

The scoreline - 6-7 6-1 6-3 1-6 7-6 - spoke to the undulating chaos of the occasion: as night gave way to morning, this match swung back and forth between two of the most electrifying talents in tennis. In the end, it was Shelton and his hammer serve that won out.

What a player. What a night. What a shame someone had to lose. And what a travesty most of the world slept through it. Forget, for a moment, the incredible theater on this long night in New York. What are we doing? Who wins from starting a game after 11pm - beyond a few insomniacs, TV viewers on the other side of the world, and Shelton's semifinal opponent Frances Tiafoe?

Carlos Alcaraz was seen throwing up into a towel as he was knocked out of the US Open

Alcaraz was clearly struggling during the match - which ended in defeat at 3.30am local time

An ecstatic Ben Shelton celebrates beating Alcaraz in the latest ever finish at the US Open

'I am just hoping that my best friend and my sister over there don’t have to be at work at 6am – in three hours,' Shelton said. 'It would be huge for their employers to let them have the day off today.'

The American added: 'I am so grateful, so blessed. God has blessed in so many ways... sharing the court with Carlos is an absolute honor and I cherish every moment I have out here.'

Alcaraz has now played in the two latest finishes in US Open history. Back in 2022, en route to his first title in New York, the Spaniard beat Jannik Sinner at 2:50am. How we missed him over those four months when his wrist betrayed him.

With this defeat, Alcaraz's title defense is over. With this win, Shelton ended a run of 17 matches without victory over a top-three player. He has ensured an American will be in the final and a new name will be on the trophy.

It was at 11:05pm local time – after more than 13 hours of action and a final plea to influencers not to use Arthur Ashe Stadium for a personal photoshoot - Shelton and Alcaraz were finally ready to bring the curtain down on Day 11.

They had just over three and half hours to wrap this up or risk breaking new ground. They failed. Of course they failed. This showdown with Shelton had all the ingredients to be a blockbuster, another marathon tug of war.

But the 23,000 fans who forked out for this night session – including Seal, Simone Biles and Kevin Hart – knew the risk they ran. Unlike at Wimbledon, there is no 11pm curfew here. Only last week, Venus Williams’ first-round match kicked off at 12:13am – a US Open record – and on his way to the quarterfinals, No 1 seed Alexander Zverev has already clocked off at 1:55am and 2:15am.

Shelton had played beyond 2am in the second round and there was nothing sleepy about the way he began this match.

For 12 games and most of a breathless first-set tiebreak, the American went toe-to-toe with Alcaraz. Time and again, this contest delivered on its promise of swagger and vicious shot-making.

And yet it felt so predictable, so ominous, when – at 5-5 – Shelton was broken to love. How often do we see the very best find a way just when a set teeters on a knife edge? This time, though, Shelton did not yield. At least not immediately. He broke back before taking control of the tiebreak.

Shelton's girlfriend Trinity Rodman stayed until the bitter end as her partner beat Alcaraz

But some members of the crowd were less engaged with the late finish in the quarter-final

One astonishing rally, in which the American pulled Alcaraz from back to a front like a yo-yo, sent Arthur Ashe into a frenzy. Only one member of the crowd was not lost in rapture: Shelton’s father, Bryan, who gestured for his son to calm down.

The 23-year-old heeded his advice and looked set to steal the set when he led 5-3 in the tiebreak. But then, Alcaraz found something from somewhere. Four points later, he had drawn first blood.

That was the trigger for many inside Arthur Ashe to call it a night. Who could blame them for thinking the dye was cast? Thankfully Shelton didn’t see it that way – even after squandering four break points in the opening game of the second set.

The American’s pressure finally told two games later and, this time, Alcaraz had no immediate answer. So Shelton turned the screw, breaking three times in succession to take the set 6-1. It was 12:56am, we had a game on our hands and the stadium speakers blasted out Jay Z’s reminder that this ‘city never sleeps.’

You’d do well to doze off in earshot of ‘DJ Mode’ at the best of times. Let alone with this quarterfinal so finely poised.

And yet, by the time Alcaraz and Shelton climbed out of their chairs, more and more fans were on their way home. At this point, nowhere was more sparsely filled than courtside where a single seat can cost up to $5,000.

Those who remained in the posh seats were treated to more majesty at either end of the third set: first, a remarkable rally that saw Shelton stretch and contort every fiber of his 6ft 4in frame.

After 18 shots, Alcaraz eventually claimed the point before cupping his hand behind his ear. And then, half an hour later, the Spaniard won a battle of touch around the net. Even Shelton’s girlfriend – soccer star Trinity Rodman – rose to her feet to applaud.

With this win, Shelton ended a run of 17 matches without victory over a top-three player

Alcaraz recovered from two sets to one down to force a decider, only to lose on a tiebreak

Unfortunately for Alcaraz, neither made a difference as Shelton held firm to take the third set. This time, his father was his biggest hype man. At the other end, Alcaraz bent at the waist. It was 1:43am and those four-and-half months off appeared to be catching up with the No 2 seed. He was grimacing and chuntering and soon Alcaraz faced more break points.

This time, though, he saved them and then, out of nowhere, he put dent after dent in Shelton’s serve. Alcaraz won five of the next six games to send this to a decider. It was 2:20am and we were headed toward more history on Arthur Ashe.

How much had that taken out of the defending champion? As thousands of fans – many of whom had migrated from the nosebleeds to the lower bowl – bayed for more, Alcaraz appeared to vomit into his towel.

And yet, as this match ticked towards a fifth hour, the Spaniard seemed to find a second - third? fourth? - wind. He opened up a break-point opportunity and repelled Shelton as the American banged at the door. By the time Alcaraz sent this to a tiebreak, it was 3:21am. At long, long last. Something had to give. In the end, it was Alcaraz who broke and Shelton who marched into a second US Open semifinal. After this, who would bet on him stopping there?

Sports.title: Luke Shaw misses Manchester United training ahead of Champions League opener - sparking fears of left back headache for boss Michael Carrick
Sports.content:
Luke Shaw was missing from Manchester United’s training session ahead of their Champions League opener against Sabah on Thursday night, raising concerns that the club’s left-gamble has already backfired.

It’s unclear if the England defender is injured but club sources insist that Wednesday was designated as a rest day for Shaw, suggesting he may be held back for Sunday’s Manchester derby at Old Trafford. Head coach Michael Carrick is expected to address the issue at his pre-match press conference this lunchtime.

United decided against signing cover for Shaw in the transfer window despite showing interest in Newcastle’s Lewis Hall and rejecting an opportunity to sign Rayan Ait-Nouri on loan from Manchester City on deadline day.

The 31-year-old veteran defender started every Premier League game for United last season, but it was widely accepted that he could not go another season without injury. Shaw was replaced by Noussair Mazraoui in added time during Sunday’s 2-2 draw at Everton after setting up a goal for Benjamin Sesko, but it was assumed the change was tactical.

United are relying on a number of back-up options if Shaw is unavailable, with Patrick Dorgu able to play at left back after being used in a more advanced role under Carrick.

Luke Shaw was replaced by Noussair Mazraoui in added time during Sunday’s 2-2 draw at Everton

Both right-backs, Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot, are capable of playing on the opposite flank, and academy product Harry Amass has stayed at the club when it was anticipated he would leave. New £70million midfield Carlos Baleba – currently out until October – could also be used as an auxiliary left-back.

Carrick spoke about the flexibility of the squad, and Dorgu in particular, at his last press conference on Friday. ‘We obviously had certain things that we needed to fill and try and improve the group. Largely, I think we're in a good place,’ said the United boss.

‘We've got pretty good balance within the whole squad; dynamics, strengths, what we might need in certain games. So, we've got players that are flexible as well throughout the whole team that can play in different positions as and when and if we need it. As you go through a season, you always need that.

‘Patrick can certainly play left-back. It's something he can, we just haven't had to explore that. It's just the way we've been since I've been here. He actually has been injured unfortunately for some time, played three or four times for us last season. So, you could almost argue he's almost like a new player, you know, to have, and it's almost like a new signing in some ways because he's added so much to the group.’

Sports.title: Revealed: The staggering sums of money LIV golfers - including Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau - are owed following collapse of Saudi-backed rebel league
Sports.content:
Revealed: The staggering sums of money LIV golfers - including Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau - are owed following collapse of Saudi-backed rebel league

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

LIV Golf's high-profile stars are waiting to collect more than £30million in unpaid money from the Saudi-backed rebel league after it filed for bankruptcy on Tuesday.

A 'Chapter 11' petition was lodged in New Jersey last night, with the breakaway league locked in a battle for survival ever since its Saudi Arabian backers announced in April that they were pulling the plug.

Although the latest development had been widely expected, it marks a significant milestone in LIV's dramatic downfall, coming four years after its arrival triggered an ugly civil war in the sport.

The 'Chapter 11' petition also revealed the staggering sums owed to LIV's golfers, who are listed among the league's unsecured creditors.

Jon Rahm tops the list with a huge $7.5million (£5.5m) outstanding, followed by Bryson DeChambeau, who is owed $5.8m (£4.3m).

Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith and Adrian Meronk are owed $5.5m (£4.1m), $4.8m (£3.5m) and $4.4m (£3.2m) respectively, while English golfer Tyrrell Hatton has $3.4m (£2.5m) in unsecured claims.

LIV Golf's high-profile stars are waiting to collect more than £30million in unpaid money - Jon Rahm, pictured, tops the list with a huge $7.5million (£5.5m) outstanding in unsecured claims

The sums detailed in the petition refer to money already owed to the golfers as of the date of the filing, rather than the full value of their respective LIV contracts.

Rahm's mammoth LIV contract was agreed at a reported $350m (£258m), which means the £5.5m currently outstanding represents only a fraction of the enormous deal he signed to join the breakaway league.

While bankruptcy might allow the circuit to realise its stated ambition of a LIV 2.0, it remains to be seen if their forthcoming union with BC Partners, a private equity group, will be sufficient for the league to extend into a 2027 season.

The greatest unknown at this stage is which of their marquee players will stay with the project in a vastly diminished and less lucrative form, as it is understood that bankruptcy will allow the golfers to exit their contracts, even if they have time still to run.

Any LIV golfers looking to return to the PGA Tour could face a fresh battle for reinstatement, with the American circuit having already imposed significant financial penalties on players who defected to its Saudi-backed rival.

Earlier this year, Rahm appeared to hedge his bets by making peace with the PGA Tour, agreeing to return for occasional appearances and pay the fines he had accrued since joining LIV in 2024.

Bryson DeChambeau, whose LIV deal expired at the end of the 2026 season, is owed £4.3m

Yasir Al Rumayyan (Governor of PIF, Chairman of Aramco) congratulates winning player, Elvis Smylie (Ripper GC) on day 4 of LIV Golf in Riyadh LIV Golf Riyad back in February

'The DP World Tour (PGA European Tour) and Jon Rahm have come to an agreement on conditional releases to play in conflicting tournaments on LIV Golf during the remainder of its 2026 season,' a spokesperson from the league said. Meanwhile, Rahm revealed there was 'no longer a standoff' and that concessions were made by both parties.

DeChambeau's deal expired at the end of the 2026 season but he is expected to recommit in return for equity in the league. The picture around Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton is far more concerning to LIV insiders - both men are contracted through 2028 and Daily Mail Sport sources had indicated prior to bankruptcy that both men were likely to leave in the event of the petition being filed.

Rahm, for one, hinted at the possibility earlier on Tuesday, when asked at the DP World Tour's Irish Open if he would like to see a pathway back to the PGA Tour. He said: 'I still have a contract with LIV 1.0 that I am more than willing to fulfil, so like I said time will tell.'

The choice of phrase - 'LIV 1.0' – would suggest his loyalty was contingent on his existing terms being honoured in order to continue with LIV.

Sports.title: Hilarious moment sees Micah Richards run out of the CBS studio when Kylian Mbappe names him his favourite pundit - after he wrote him a poem and they shared bizarre virtual hug
Sports.content:
Micah Richards struggled to contain his excitement and ran out of the CBS Sports studio after being named Kylian Mbappe's favourite pundit on Tuesday night.

Mbappe joined US network CBS for a post-match interview after scoring in Real Madrid's 2-1 victory over Inter Milan in the Champions League, and Richards was so excited to speak to the striker that he even wrote him a poem.

As host Kate Abdo revealed Mbappe was joining the show for the first time in six years, Richards cheered in excitement and bellowed: 'Kylian! Finally we meet my friend.'

Overjoyed, the ex-England international danced over to the big screen to give a hug to Mbappe, who laughed and joined him in the bizarre virtual embrace, before returning to his seat to read a short poem to the Frenchman.

'Speed like lightning, a finish so clean,' he began. 'Kylian Mbappe, the football machine.

'From Paris to Madrid, he's chasing his dream. A star of the pitch, the king of the scene. My man!'

Who's @KMbappe's favorite on the #UCLToday show?



Not sure @micahrichards is ever going to recover from this 😂 pic.twitter.com/bnFBwuXAp9 — CBS Sports Golazo ⚽️ (@CBSSportsGolazo) September 8, 2026

Micah Richards ran out the CBS studio after Kylian Mbappe called him his favourite pundit

The former Man City defender was overjoyed after Mbappe joined the network for an interview

After buttering up the striker, Richards asked at the end of the interview: 'Who's your favourite on the show, baby?'

To the pundit's delight, Mbappe replied: 'I would have to say you.'

Richards immediately jumped to his feet in celebration and pulled out Alan Shearer's iconic celebration, raising his arm aloft as he charged out of the studio saying: 'See you later, I'm retiring now!'

His reaction has since gone viral, with more than 10,000 fans liking CBS Sports' clip of the moment after it was posted to social media platform X on Tuesday night.

During the interview, Mbappe spoke highly of his new Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho, praising the legendary manager after his side made a positive start in the Champions League.

'Jose Mourinho makes you feel alive,' the Ballon d'Or nominee said. 'He makes you feel special. He is a guy who puts a lot of pressure and high intensity in training.

'He talks a lot with the players, and we know what he wants from us, what he expects from us.

The France international saw the funny side after Richards wrote him a flattering poem

It's been six years in the making for @MicahRichards 🫂@KMbappe gets the warmest of welcomes on UCL Today 😂 pic.twitter.com/ht8YcJn6r6 — CBS Sports Golazo ⚽️ (@CBSSportsGolazo) September 8, 2026

Just when you think you’ve seen it all… @MicahRichards has written a poem for @KMbappe ✍️😭 pic.twitter.com/g4VPZoB9rt — CBS Sports Golazo ⚽️ (@CBSSportsGolazo) September 8, 2026

'When a coach gives you that confidence and that hunger, you do not want to disappoint him, and you want to give your best.'

After the match, which saw Mbappe and Federico Valverde strike for Los Blancos in the 2-1 win, Mourinho returned the compliment to his superstar forward.

'I rank him right up there among the players I've coached,' Mourinho admitted.

'I don't like comparisons... I've had players like Ronaldo Nazario. But Kylian is right up there! Kylian is incredible.'

Sports.content:
Rodri rings Valencia player to apologise after chat with Barcelona star gets leaked

Rodri is reported to have apologised after the former Manchester City star appeared to make comments about Valencia

Former Manchester City star Rodri is reported to have contacted Valencia defender Jose Gaya to apologise after comments he made about the club were leaked. Rodri is currently in the early weeks of his first season with Barcelona after completing a permanent move away from City in the summer.

‌



The Spain international left the Etihad Stadium to move to the Camp Nou in a deal believed to be worth around £65million, and has already established himself as a key player in the Barcelona midfield.

‌



Rodri was part of the Barca team that claimed a 5-0 win over Valencia at the weekend in La Liga, a victory that saw them maintain their 100 percent start to the campaign.

‌



Footage later emerged on Spanish TV that appeared to show Rodri talking about Valencia with his Barcelona and Spain teammate, Pau Cubarsi.

‌



"They're really bad, man, they're terrible,” Rodri was also quoted as having said about Valencia.

Rodri then appeared to ask Cubarsi how Valencia finished last season, to which the defender replied: “Just shy of Europe,” which left the former City star open-mouthed in surprise.

The BBC has secured the rights to a groundbreaking new athletics event, where a huge prize fund will be up for grabs. The inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship begins in Budapest on Friday and concludes on Sunday.

‌



It will feature the biggest stars in the sport, including British heroes Keely Hodgkinson, Georgia Hunter Bell, Amy Hunt and Josh Kerr. The extravaganza is designed to provide a fast-paced, high-stakes finale to the outdoor season.

‌



Individual track events are limited 16 athletes, field events to eight and relays to eight teams. Entrants include reigning Olympic champions, world champions, Diamond League winners and other leading athletes.

‌



With younger audiences in mind, each session will last less than three hours. It will focus on 28 core disciplines, with longer-distance events such as the 10,000m and the steeplechase left off the schedule.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

The total prize fund is a whopping £7.4million, making it the most lucrative event in track and field history. The winner of each individual event will take home £110,000, with the runners-up and third-place finishers netting £55,000 and £30,000. In the relay events, the winning team will share £60,000.

‌



Georgia Hunter Bell makes Keely Hodgkinson admission as she lets slip return plan READ MORE :

BBC Diamond League interrupted as host issues apology live on air READ MORE :

There will be no medals up for grabs, with all competing athletes receiving tokens. The champion of each event will lift a trophy that connects to their token, forming a complete piece. Other innovations include a pre-event red-carpet event, live music acts during the session warm-up and centre-court-style interviews shown in the stadium and on the broadcast.

In a move that should delight British fans, the event will be available to watch on terrestrial television after the BBC secured the rights, with coverage getting underway on BBC Two on 6pm on Friday.

View 3 Images Amy Hunt will be looking to end her incredible year on a high (Image: Julian Finney/Getty Images)

‌



While the broadcaster showed the European Championships, it lost its long-held rights to the Commonwealth Games, which were shown on the subscription channel TNT Sports, with highlights on Channel 5.

The field for each event has been confirmed, with Olympic champion Hodgkinson going up against European champion Audrey Werro and Femke Broeders-Bol in the women's 800m.

View 3 Images Josh Kerr will aiming for the £110,000 prize in the 1500m (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

European champion Hunter Bell will be one of the favourites in the women's 1500m, while sprint star Hunt, fresh from her four gold medals at the European Championships, will go for individual glory in the 100m and 200m.

In the men's 1500m, Kerr renews his rivalry with Jakob Ingebrigtsen, with the pair facing competition from Olympic champion Cole Hocker and world champion Isaac Nader.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca is playing a risky game with Man City stars after Gianluigi Donnarumma verdict
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca is playing a risky game with Man City stars after Gianluigi Donnarumma verdict

Enzo Maresca criticised his Manchester City stars for passing the ball back to Gianluigi Donnarumma too many times - in a public display of doubt in his goalkeeper

View 3 Images Gianluigi Donnarumma had another shaky performance as Man City beat FC Porto

There is said to have been some surprise amongst senior figures at Manchester City that Gianluigi Donnarumma didn't make the shortlist for world goalkeeper of the year.

‌



Not least when those same people discovered Vozinha had done - on the back of just two impressive performances for Cape Verde at the World Cup.

‌



But imagine the surprise at Enzo Maresca's comments about Donnarumma, following his side's opening Champions League win in Porto?

‌



Despite insisting he was "happy" with the Italian international, in the same breath Maresca ordered his players to reduce the number of back passes to Donnarumma.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Donnarumma endured a nervous performance in Portugal. He almost conceded an embarrassing goal when his clearance rebounded off William Gomes, before bouncing wide of the post.

While during last weekend's tense win over Coventry City, Donnarumma almost conceded when letting the ball run under his feet.

"I think a few times it's not a Gigio mistake, it's more for me the wrong decision to go back to Gigio," said Maresca. "We can go back to the keeper when we don't have another option, but the players need to find the other option."

‌



A show of Italian solidarity is understandable.

Maresca has been at the Etihad two minutes, so criticising a keeper Pep Guardiola made a big deal of signing from Paris Saint Germain in 2025, would be tantamount to claiming the Spanish genius got that one wrong.

View 3 Images Pep Guardiola was desperate to land the Italian keeper - his successor doesn't appear as keen

‌



But blaming the rest of the team for giving Donnarumma the ball too often is not a good look. What the rest of the dressing room make of Maresca's comments is anyone's guess.

Donnarumma cost almost £30m, and was handed a five-year-deal which made him one of the highest paid stars in the squad. So it feels a bit rich Maresca is now suggesting he doesn't want his keeper having the ball too often.

Donnarumma was also handed instructions to make sure the bloke he'd replaced wouldn't be missed. But the difference between Ederson and Donnarumma in their respective ability and confidence when having the ball, is like chalk and cheese.

‌



The distribution of goalkeepers at the highest level has become crucial to a team's success. Manuel Neuer became the first 'sweeper keeper'. Countless others have followed, having worked hard to improve this part of their game.

View 3 Images Enzo Maresca made some eye-opening comments after City's win over Porto

It cost Joe Hart his job at the Etihad when Guardiola took charge in 2016. Guardiola didn't believe Hart suited the style of play he wanted to implement.

‌



The same thing happened to Andre Onana across town at Manchester United.

When it became clear PSG were willing to sell Donnarumma, United were interested in signing him, but changed their minds when they discovered what wages he was on. They're probably glad they did now.

Because all Maresca's comments have done is undermine Donnarumma's all-round game. While at the same time, putting doubts in the minds of his team-mates that they might just have a keeper they cannot trust.

Sports.title: Exhausted Carlos Alcaraz vomits into towel as he loses US Open epic finishing at 3.33am
Sports.content:
Exhausted Carlos Alcaraz vomits into towel as he loses US Open epic finishing at 3.33am

Carlos Alcaraz was throwing up into his towel during his US Open marathon against Ben Shelton, which wasn't decided until gone 3am following a five-set classic in New York

View 2 Images Carlos Alcaraz was seen vomiting into his towel (Image: ESPN)

Carlos Alcaraz was seen vomiting into his towel before the deciding set of his US Open epic against Ben Shelton - which finished at 3.33am in New York.

The defending champion was undone by the home favourite, who claimed a 6-7 6-1 6-3 1-6 7-6 victory in a match that lasted four hours and 28 minutes. And after the Spaniard won the fourth set, taking it to a decider, he was seen being sick into his towel.

Alcaraz cut an exhausted figure in the early hours of the morning and covered his face as he vomited. It didn't impact on his performance as he produced some stunning tennis, before eventually coming up short in a fifth set tiebreak.

‌



Alcaraz's main rival, Jannik Sinner, is missing at Flushing Meadows and the Spaniard was tipped by many to defend his crown in New York, but left the court to huge applause in the early hours of the morning.

Serena and Venus Williams beaten on US Open return as insider reveals future plans READ MORE :

US Open champ Aryna Sabalenka angrily hits back at reporter during press conference READ MORE :

The match marked Shelton's first career win over a top-three player, against which he had been 0-17 coming into the match, but he will now be among the favourites to win the US Open. He will play Frances Tiafoe in the semi-final, meaning America will have a men's Grand Slam finalist for the first time since 2002.

Shelton hailed the home crowd for getting him through the contest - before joking that he hopes those in his corner won't have to prepare for their working day in a matter of hours.

He said: "For me it's always about the people in the crowd, whether it's my coaches, team or friends and family, or the city of New York that showed up tonight until 3am with the USA chants, that's what kept me going and what got me this win.

View 2 Images The Spaniard and defending champion was beaten in the latest ever finish at the US Open (Image: Getty Images)

"It's incredible. This is the greatest sports city and greatest stadium in the world. I'm hoping my best friend and sister don't have to be at work at 6am. I'm so grateful, so blessed to be in front of you guys and share the court with Carlos is an absolute honour."

Alcaraz has now played in the two latest finishes in US Open history. Four years ago in 2022 he beat Jannik Sinner with their contest eventually finishing at 2:50am en route to him winning his first Grand Slam.

Finishes of this type owe to games starting late at night. Shelton and Alcaraz began at 11pm, but such scenarios are impossible at Wimbledon with Merton council imposing an 11pm curfew for matches played under the lights on the main courts. An Andy Murray win in 2012 finished at 11.02pm and remains the latest game ever at SW19.

Conor Benn and Ryan Garcia will meet in the ring on Saturday night for the WBC welterweight title, and the American champion is already ramping up the mind games

Sports.title: Konstantinos Karetsas health latest as Borussia Dortmund chief speaks out on winger
Sports.content:
Konstantinos Karetsas health latest as Borussia Dortmund chief speaks out on winger

Borussia Dortmund issued an update on Konstantinos Karetsas at half-time of their Champions League match against Villarreal - and club officials have now spoken

View 2 Images Konstantinos Karetsas covered his face while lying supine on the pitch (Image: Borussia Dortmund via Getty Images)

Borussia Dortmund sporting director Nils-Ole Book says Konstantinos Karetsas was unable to speak after being stretchered off the pitch during their Champions League match against Villarreal. The summer signing from Genk signalled to the sideline that he could not continue midway through the first half, sitting down on the pitch and covering his face with both hands before lying supine.

‌



Karetsas, 18, was making his Champions League debut. The crowd applauded him as he was carried off on a stretcher.

‌



Dortmund described the issue as 'circulatory problems'. The club confirmed that he was going to the hospital for further examinations.

‌



Seven players could miss Napoli vs Arsenal through injury as surgery confirmed in statement READ MORE :

A statement shared on X at half-time of the match reads: "Konstantinos Karetsas had to leave the field due to circulatory problems. Kosta is doing well under the circumstances and is on his way to the hospital for further tests."

The former Dortmund captain, Mats Hummels, was working as a pundit at Westfalenstadion. He said of Karetsas on Amazon Prime Video: "When the doctors didn't even look at the legs, but only at the upper body, it sent shivers down my spine.

"We don't wish such a story on anyone. These are really nasty pictures that we had to see."

‌



View 2 Images Konstantinos Karetsas was carried off the pitch on a stretcher (Image: Alex Gottschalk/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

The club's sporting director Book then said of Karetsas on Sky after the match: "He was substituted due to circulatory problems. It came very suddenly, he sat down and was taken to the hospital for further examinations, where he is now.

"And of course we'll wait and see. Of course, that clouds the mood significantly."

‌



He continued: "I went out with him, but he wasn't able to speak directly at that moment. Of course, we hope that it will get better very, very quickly and that it's nothing serious. But now, especially after the game, we don't have any new information yet."

"At first, I assumed that he might have some muscular problems. But then he didn't touch his thigh at all and was even carried down on a stretcher."

Ricken explained that the reasons Karetsas was having tests is "to rule out everything in the end." The former player continued: "We have to wait and see what the next few days will bring."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off
