World.title: 159 pupils sleep in one-room hostel at Nasarawa nomadic school – Director
World.content:
An underserved nomadic school in Nasarawa State has cried out, saying about 159 pupils sleep in a single-room hostel.

The director of the Gudindi, Sabon Gida Nomadic Boarding Primary School in Kokona Local Government Area, Isah Turajo, spoke with our reporter during a visit to the school on Saturday.

Mr Turajo said the school needs to provide alternative accommodation for the pupils to avert a disease outbreak.

According to him, the 159 male pupils sleep on the floor and share about 100 mattresses.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the mattresses were donated by Nasarawa state Governor Abdullahi Sule last year.

Mr Turajo explained that inadequate hostel accommodation forced the management to convert the only school hall into a one-room hostel for the male pupils.

He said that the concern is heightened by an outbreak-like incident last term, when about 20 pupils were treated for rashes suspected to be chickenpox.

“We have 229 pupils in the school, out of which 159 are boys and 70 are girls. The boys sleep in a one-room hostel, while 34 girls out of the 70 sleep in the staff quarters with our female staff.”

According to him, 36 of the 70 females are day students from neighbouring communities.

Mr Turajo further stated that overcrowding becomes more challenging during periods of intense heat, as some pupils are forced to carry mats into classrooms at night in search of more comfortable sleeping conditions.

The director appealed to the Nasarawa State Government, individuals, philanthropists, and other well-meaning Nigerians to come to the aid of the school by providing hostels and other essential facilities for the pupils.

World.title: Malian women resist renewed support for female genital mutilation
World.content:
A coordinated social media campaign defending female genital mutilation (FGM) emerged in Mali this August, reigniting societal debates not just about women’s bodily integrity, but also about tradition and national sovereignty.

Days after a national non-governmental organisation displayed posters in Bamako denouncing the practice, anonymous online accounts began posting images that reversed the ‘no more’ campaign’s message. Men of various backgrounds are portrayed smiling or with thumbs up, surrounded by the national colours and the message: ‘In Mali, yes to excision! Let’s protect girls and build their future.’

The slogan turns the protection argument on its head in a country where cutting out parts of young girls’ genitals, often without anaesthesia and at the risk of deadly complications, remains commonplace. A 2023 study estimated that FGM caused roughly 44,000 excess deaths a year across 15 African countries, including Mali. This makes it a leading cause of death for girls and young women where it is practised.

For those who survive, the consequences are dire and both immediate and long-term. They include severe pain and bleeding, infection and emotional shock at the time of cutting. Throughout life, they manifest through chronic pain, urinary and menstrual complications, a greater risk of difficult childbirth, and lasting psychological trauma.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Local women’s rights advocates have opposed the practice for decades. Soon after Mali’s 1960 independence, midwife and lawmaker Aoua Kéita and fellow activists pushed for reforms to advance women’s rights in the 1962 Marriage Code. They achieved a ban on forced marriage and a minimum age for matrimony. But they failed to secure a prohibition on excision and polygamy.

Powerful conservatives went on to defeat draft laws in 2009 on advancing women’s rights in the household, and in 2019 on violence against women. Mali’s 2024 Penal Code condemns violence generally, but stops short of naming FGM.

This legal gap has been costly for Malian women and girls. Mali’s latest Demographic and Health Survey reveals that 89 per cent of those aged 15 to 49 have been cut – one of the highest rates globally. Among girls aged 0 to 14 – the age range when cutting usually occurs – the prevalence is lower, at 70 per cent, and down from 74 per cent in 2018. This suggests the practice may be slowly receding.

But the decline is modest, and potentially reversible. Many in Mali, both women and men, still support FGM, believing it is a religious obligation or a tradition worth keeping. Both claims are disputed, but the lack of consensus threatens thousands of infant girls every year.

FGM supporters minimise its physical harms, presenting it as necessary to control women’s sexuality – a long-standing feature of patriarchal control. Societal norms across much of Mali’s southern and central regions have long glorified suffering as a badge of honour for women, essentially normalising women’s pain. The stigma of bad morality that community expectations could attach to an uncut woman is presented as the greater harm she needs protection from.

‘Yes’ campaigners also try to portray opposition to FGM as a foreign agenda. This erases Mali’s long history of home-grown opposition, from Kéita to today’s human rights defenders. But it resonates with broader sovereignty narratives that recast women’s rights as a foreign import and traditional gender norms as a societal strength.

But this logic replaces one domination with another. It allows men, families and communities to police women’s bodies and maim girls too young to consent and call it resisting imperialism. It denies half the population sovereignty over their own bodies in the name of national sovereignty.

It is hard to determine who is behind the ‘yes’ campaign supporting FGM. Journalists and Malian feminist organisations have traced much of it to accounts sharing artificial intelligence-generated posters, apparently designed to manufacture the appearance of a mass movement. This makes it difficult to assess the campaign’s true scope.

While most men whose portraits are used in the campaign have defended it, some have cited unauthorised use of their image or retracted their support under public pressure.

By mirroring the communication style of the ‘no’ advocacy, FGM supporters have sought to normalise their position, creating a false equivalence between ‘yes’ and ‘no’. Once the two are placed on an equal footing, inaction can be presented as a balance rather than a choice to condone violence. Apparent neutrality works in favour of the status quo.

But in the course of Mali’s ‘refoundation’ – a process aimed at resetting societal norms and values, and the basis for political governance – women will not accept a more rigidly gendered social contract without a fight. The pro-excision campaign has met a strong response from women’s rights advocates, health professionals and other public voices challenging the notion that defending FGM equals defending Malian values.

Women – and some men – have also been mobilised beyond national borders. In Côte d’Ivoire and Togo, the ‘yes’ campaign triggered its own swift backlash. Malian and West African diaspora have organised anti-FGM protests in Paris, Montreal and beyond, indicating that FGM can no longer count on silence.

On 26 August, Mali’s National Human Rights Commission called on the authorities to criminalise FGM. Other countries where the practice is entrenched – including Burkina Faso, Senegal, Guinea, Niger, Egypt and Sudan – have passed such laws. It has not ended the practice, but it has made it riskier for perpetrators and handed women’s rights groups a legal basis to challenge it.

But legislating may not be the end of the story. In 2024, traditional and religious leaders attempted to have The Gambia’s Parliament repeal the 2015 Women’s (Amendment) Act criminalising FGM. The case is still pending before the Supreme Court.

Beyond parliaments and courtrooms, significant shifts in community norms are needed to protect women’s bodily integrity. Religious leaders should clarify that FGM is neither required nor consensually accepted in Islam. They should work with women’s rights organisations, who have long been committed to ending the practice, and health professionals who can best explain its consequences.

International partners should support that effort without becoming its face, a move that risks feeding the campaign’s own claim that reform is foreign-imposed.

Ornella Moderan is the Regional Director for West Africa, the Sahel, the Lake Chad Basin and Central Africa at the Institute for Security Studies (ISS).

World.title: Gridlock worsens as Kara Bridge repairs begin
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

Two-week repair works on the Kara Bridge have triggered heavy gridlock on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, leaving motorists stranded for several hours.

The Federal Government began the replacement of damaged expansion joints on the bridge on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, after the project was earlier suspended to allow for traffic management planning.

The repairs have caused severe congestion along the corridor, with the gridlock stretching from the Kara Bridge in Ogun State to the 7Up Junction in Lagos State and beyond.

As of Tuesday afternoon, the traffic had extended beyond the Secretariat Bus Stop, while motorists coming from Ikeja and Agege and heading towards the Otedola underpass were also caught in the congestion stretching beyond Otunba Jobi Fele Way.

Many commuters also took to social media to share videos and images of the gridlock, saying they spent several hours travelling from their workplaces to their homes.

By Wednesday morning, motorists were seen using one-way traffic routes to get passengers to their destinations as the congestion persisted.

Traffic and security officials, including the police, military, Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, Federal Road Safety Corps and Ogun State Traffic Compliance and Enforcement Agency, were deployed to manage the situation.

However, the repair works at the entry and exit points of the bridge towards OPIC further compounded the congestion around Kara.

The spokesperson for the Ogun State Traffic Compliance and Enforcement Agency, Babatunde Akinbiyi, urged motorists to exercise patience and cooperate with traffic officials during the repair period.

He said, “We anticipated that there would be traffic, and that was why we issued a traffic advisory earlier.

“We can only appeal to motorists to bear with us for the time being because the repair works are necessary to ensure smooth movement and the safety of road users along the corridor.

“Anyone who does not have an important business along the axis should stay away, and those who cannot avoid using that route should cooperate with traffic officials.”

The two-week rehabilitation, directed by the Minister of Works, David Umahi, involves replacing deteriorating expansion joints to improve road safety and the structural integrity of the bridge.

The project is expected to run until September 22, 2026.

The Lagos State Government has advised motorists using the corridor to plan their journeys ahead, adding that one half of the affected section would be closed at a time while traffic uses the other half interchangeably.

The government also urged motorists to cooperate with traffic managers to ensure the rehabilitation is completed as scheduled.

World.title: Obi demonstrated power of restraint in Benue – NDC’s Moses Paul
World.content:
Sekinat Osundiji

One of the youth leaders of the Obidient Movement, Dr. Paul Moses, has said the controversy surrounding Peter Obi’s recent visit to Benue State should not be reduced to a political disagreement, insisting that the focus should be on the lives of Nigerians affected by violence in the state.

Moses made the remarks during an interview on ARISE News on Wednesday while speaking about the incident that prevented Obi from reaching Yelwata, where he had planned to meet victims of the killings.

According to Moses, Obi’s decision to pull back in the face of opposition demonstrated restraint and should form a major part of the conversation surrounding the incident.

“Leadership isn’t about showing who has the bigger crowd or the bigger force. It’s about the power of restraint,” Moses said.

He argued that attempts to frame the incident as a disagreement between political parties or personalities would distract from the more important issue of Nigerians who have lost their lives and those still living in affected communities.

“What they want the conversation to become is a banter between political parties, between personalities, but we’re not going to allow that to happen,” Moses said.

“We need to get down to the crux of the matter, which has to do with the value of the human lives that are involved.”

Moses, who said he was physically present during the visit, said the larger concern was Obi’s inability to freely reach people affected by violence despite his intention to engage with them.

He questioned how Nigeria could strengthen its democracy if access to communities affected by killings depended on the approval or goodwill of incumbent authorities.

“How do we build democracy where access to citizens, particularly those who have been slaughtered, killed, you know, without any roadblock, is now dependent upon the goodwill of incumbent authorities?” he asked.

Moses maintained that Obi’s visit should instead have sparked a broader conversation about political leaders visiting victims of violence, arguing that other presidential candidates should be equally challenged to undertake similar visits.

“The question or the debate should be challenging other presidential candidates to do the same, even if for politics,” he said.

“This is the kind of debate that we should be having.”

He questioned how political leaders could properly understand the situation in affected communities if they couldn’t physically visit and engage with victims.

“How do you understand the sovereignty of Nigeria when you can’t even visit with them and see what’s going on?” Moses asked.

The Obidient leader also rejected the suggestion that the incident should be viewed primarily through the lens of internal political disputes.

He said while disagreements within political parties were inevitable, the circumstances surrounding Obi’s visits to communities affected by violence went beyond party politics.

“Internal political parties’ issues will always be there. But this has nothing to do with that,” Moses said.

“I mean, in all cases, it has to do with the fact that Mr. Peter Obi wants to visit with victims or people or relate with people, and then deliberate attempts are being made to ensure that that doesn’t happen, and it’s a big concern.”

Moses also defended Obi’s previous humanitarian visits to Benue, explaining that the former Anambra governor had engaged directly with victims, traditional rulers and community officials.

He said the latest visit differed because political actors and Labour Party supporters were involved, making it necessary for the team to formally notify the police.

According to him, however, the fundamental right of Nigerians to move around the country should not be confused with the requirement to notify security agencies about political rallies or organised events.

“As a Nigerian citizen, the laws, the Constitution is there — you can visit, you can move, the right,” Moses said.

He added that Obi’s response to the confrontation showed the kind of leadership he believed should be encouraged.

Moses said the focus should ultimately remain on the victims and the need for Nigerians to have access to their fellow citizens during moments of crisis, rather than turning the incident into another political contest.

World.title: Colombia lifts decade-long gun-carrying restrictions
World.content:
BOGOTA — Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella has signed a decree lifting a decade-long restriction on the public carrying of legally owned firearms, fulfilling a campaign promise to adopt a tougher approach to crime.

According to the BBC on Wednesday, the new decree allows Colombians who hold valid permits to carry registered firearms to take their weapons outside their homes without obtaining additional authorisation.

Defending the measure, De la Espriella said law-abiding citizens should not be prevented from defending themselves while criminals continued to carry illegal weapons.

“It is not right that criminals are armed to the teeth while decent people can’t defend themselves,” the president said.

He, however, stressed that the decree did not amount to unrestricted access to firearms, noting that existing regulations governing the legal ownership of guns would remain in force.

While signing the decree, De la Espriella said the decision fulfilled a pledge he made during his presidential campaign.

“A man’s word is his honour, and I have honour, that’s why I keep my word,” he said.

The restriction was introduced in December 2015 by then-President Juan Manuel Santos as a temporary security measure during the Christmas and New Year period.

It was subsequently renewed annually by Santos and his successors, Iván Duque and Gustavo Petro, despite their differing political orientations.

Under the previous arrangement, even firearm owners with valid carry permits were barred from taking their weapons outside their homes unless they secured additional government authorisation.

Reports cited by Spanish newspaper El País indicated that the policy change could affect nearly 700,000 Colombians who already hold legal firearm-carry permits.

They will now be allowed to carry their registered firearms outside their homes for as long as their permits remain valid.

The decision has, however, attracted criticism from some political figures.

Green Alliance Party Senator Ariel Ávila described the move as a “grave error”, warning that legally owned firearms could eventually fall into the hands of criminals.

Ávila also questioned the principle of allowing civilians to carry firearms, arguing that the state should remain responsible for guaranteeing the security of citizens.

De la Espriella dismissed concerns that the policy could worsen insecurity, saying security forces were continuing their crackdown on illegal firearms.

He said authorities had seized more than 15,000 illegal firearms so far this year, many of which he said were linked to breakaway factions of the Farc rebel group and the Gulf Clan criminal organisation.

The president maintained that the new policy would preserve existing controls on legal firearm ownership while giving authorised citizens greater capacity to defend themselves.

BBC

World.title: Nollywood producers may leave YouTube if naira strengthens against dollar – Kunle Afolayan
World.content:
Kunle Afolayan

​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠

Ace filmmaker Kunle Afolayan has said Nollywood producers may leave YouTube as a distribution platform if the Naira strengthens significantly against the U.S. Dollar.

Afolayan stated this in an interview with former Minister of Finance, Kemi Adeosun, on the Nidacity Podcast, while discussing the increasing migration of Nollywood filmmakers to digital platforms.

According to him, most filmmakers who have migrated to YouTube will abandon the platform if the exchange rate were to fall significantly.

He argued that the financial incentive was a major reason filmmakers are moving their productions to the platform.

The filmmaker said although YouTube offered filmmakers greater flexibility and accessibility, platforms such as Netflix and Prime Video provided better opportunities.

“YouTube can never give you what Netflix and Prime will give you, right? Never. But it’s the most flexible. It’s for everyone. It’s like a starting point.

“If you don’t have the strength to negotiate or if you don’t have access to the big players, then you just make your film, open an account, and put it there.

“If people watch it, you make your money,” he said.

He said filmmakers currently earning substantial revenue from high viewership on YouTube could lose interest in the platform if the naira strengthened significantly against the dollar.

“But look, the reason why people now will say, ‘I’ve hit a million views, I get $10,000,’ is because of the exchange rate. If dollar drops, everybody will run away from YouTube.

“So the attraction right now is the exchange rate because that’s what’s making it more profitable than it possibly is. So, if dollar comes to, say, N200 to $1, people will leave,” he said.

Afolayan also described YouTube as a suitable starting point for filmmakers who lacked the resources or bargaining power to secure deals with major streaming platforms.

The filmmaker said such producers could independently upload their films to YouTube and earn revenue based on viewership, making the platform accessible to a wider range of filmmakers.

(NAN)

World.title: Cost of living crisis: Northwest ADC candidates demand fuel subsidy return
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA — Governorship candidates of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, in the seven Northwest states have called on President Bola Tinubu to reverse the removal of fuel subsidy, saying the policy has worsened the cost of living crisis in the region.

The candidates from Kano, Kaduna, Katsina, Kebbi, Sokoto, Zamfara and Jigawa states made the demand on Tuesday in Abuja while signing the Northwest ADC Governorship Candidates’ Compact 2027–2031.

The document was presented by former Minister of Justice and Attorney-General of the Federation and ADC governorship candidate in Kebbi State, Malam Abubakar Malami, SAN.

The candidates said they fully supported the position of the ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, on the restoration of fuel subsidy.

Malami said restoring the subsidy would be among the immediate measures required to address what he described as the worsening economic hardship confronting residents of the region.

“We, the ADC Governorship Candidates of the seven Northwest States, hereby declare our total support for the promise made by the ADC Presidential Candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, to restore the subsidy as one of the immediate steps to halt the further slide of our people into abject poverty,” he said.

The candidates alleged that the removal of the subsidy had increased hardship among households in the region, while the expected benefits of the policy had not translated into improved living conditions for ordinary Nigerians.

They also criticised APC-led administrations in the Northwest, alleging that huge allocations from the Federation Account had not resulted in commensurate improvements in infrastructure, healthcare, food security and security.

According to the candidates, the seven Northwest states and their local government areas received more than N8.33 trillion from the Federation Account Allocation Committee, FAAC, between June 2023 and August 2026.

They, however, alleged that the funds had not significantly improved the living conditions of residents.

The candidates further criticised what they described as the ostentatious lifestyles of some APC governors in the region, alleging that government officials were living in affluence while residents grappled with poverty.

On insecurity, the candidates said more than 16,000 lives had been lost to insecurity in the region between June 2023 and August 2026.

They also claimed that more than 1,583 kidnapping incidents had occurred since January 2023, affecting more than 10,000 residents.

The candidates said insecurity had also affected agricultural production, with more than 533,000 hectares of farmland in Zamfara and Katsina states allegedly abandoned.

They further claimed that the Northwest accounts for about 45 per cent of Nigeria’s out-of-school children.

“Insecurity has emptied our farms, and those empty farms have brought hunger, driven our children out of the classroom, and have denied them the education the region requires to dry up the recruitment pool for future banditry, kidnappings and all associated crimes,” they said.

To address insecurity, the candidates pledged to deploy drones across the region and establish a Northwest Regional Security Coordination Centre, alongside technology-driven surveillance and rapid-response networks in each of the region’s 21 senatorial districts.

On workers’ welfare, they promised to implement a minimum wage of N110,000 across the seven states if elected.

They also outlined five priority areas covering agriculture and food security, education, healthcare, infrastructure, and youth and enterprise development.

Their proposals include protected agricultural corridors, a regional grain reserve, improved access to Universal Basic Education Commission, UBEC, programmes, integration of Almajiri and Tsangaya children into formal education, and full access to the Basic Health Care Provision Fund, BHCPF.

They also proposed the establishment of specialist hospitals in each of the 21 senatorial districts, investment in roads, rail and independent power, as well as a Regional Youth Fund and Technical and Vocational Education and Training, TVET, programmes.

The candidates said each state would retain its constitutional authority over its budget, procurement, civil service and other internal affairs, while cooperating on issues such as security, trade and infrastructure.

“We will cooperate where cooperation works better. We will preserve the constitutional authority and priorities of our states. We will plan before we promise. We will publish what we deliver,” they declared.

They also announced the establishment of a Central Coordination Committee chaired by Hon. Abdussamad Dasuki; a Technical Committee chaired by Maj. Gen. Aminu Bande (retd.) and co-chaired by Prof. Sadiq Abubakar; and a Media and Strategic Communications Committee co-chaired by Salihu Tanko Yakasai.

The Compact was signed by Sabo Mohammed Nakudu of Jigawa, Isa Mohammed Ashiru of Kaduna, Ibrahim Ali Amin of Kano, Senator Ahmad Babba Kaita of Katsina, Abubakar Malami, SAN, of Kebbi, Manir Muhammad Dan’iya of Sokoto, and Bilyaminu Shinkafi of Zamfara.

World.title: 2027: I never threatened Northerners with suffering if Tinubu loses — Akpabio
World.content:
Senate President, Godswill Akpabio

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, has denied saying that Northerners would be made to suffer between January and May if President Bola Tinubu loses the 2027 presidential election.

Akpabio described the statement attributed to him as a “complete fabrication”, challenging those circulating the claim to produce evidence of where and when he allegedly made the statement.

In a statement issued on Wednesday by his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Hon. Eseme Eyiboh, the Senate President said there was no video, audio recording, speech, interview, press release, transcript or credible news report in which he made the alleged remark.

The statement was titled, “Desperate and Dangerous Lie: Produce the Evidence or Withdraw It.”

Akpabio said a photograph bearing the alleged quotation was not evidence of the statement, describing it as “an allegation wearing typography.”

He challenged the alleged sponsor of the material, Engr. Ibrahim Umar Ammar, whom he said was identified on his verified Facebook profile as being associated with the Atiku Abubakar Campaign Organisation and Coordinator of ADC-NYAF, Kano State, to produce the original evidence.

“Produce the original and unedited video or audio recording showing precisely where, when and before whom Senator Akpabio made the alleged statement. Name the occasion. Give the date and venue. Provide the complete recording, not a conveniently edited fragment,” he said.

The Senate President also called on anyone who claimed to have merely reposted the material to identify its original source and provide the publication from which it was obtained.

He said political opposition was legitimate but warned against what he described as the use of fabricated statements to inflame ethnic sentiments ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Akpabio said the 2027 political contest should be based on records, policies, achievements, failures and competing visions for the country rather than what he described as fabricated quotations capable of threatening national unity.

“This is not legitimate political opposition. It is calculated incitement designed to manufacture fear, resentment and hostility between Northern Nigerians and a national leader from the South,” he said.

He argued that his political relationships, appointments and legislative activities contradicted the allegation that he was hostile towards the North.

Akpabio noted that several Northerners served in his office and cited his working relationship with Deputy Senate President, Senator Barau Jibrin of Kano State, as evidence of his political cooperation across regional lines.

He also pointed to legislation establishing the North-West Development Commission and the North-Central Development Commission, as well as federal institutions in Kano and Zamfara states, as examples of initiatives he said demonstrated his commitment to development across the country.

The Senate President further recalled his visit to Borno State following devastating floods in Maiduguri and the financial intervention by the National Assembly to assist victims.

He said the Senate had also supported legislation on student loans, minimum wage, security, education and economic development, arguing that such measures benefited Nigerians irrespective of their region.

Akpabio urged Nigerians to verify the source of politically sensitive claims before sharing them on social media.

“A quotation of this gravity cannot be authenticated by repetition, likes, shares or the number of Facebook accounts carrying it,” he said.

He maintained that the burden of proof rested on those alleging that he made the statement, insisting that he could not reasonably be expected to prove that he did not make an unidentified statement at an unspecified place and time.

The Senate President urged political parties and their supporters to ensure that the 2027 contest remained “truthful, responsible and Nigerian”.

“Let the 2027 contest be vigorous. Let political parties interrogate records, challenge policies, expose failures, defend achievements and present competing visions for Nigeria,” he said.

“The North is not an electoral weapon. The South is not an enemy. Ethnicity is not campaign ammunition. And Nigeria’s unity must never become collateral damage in anybody’s campaign for power.”

World.title: NAFDAC raises alarm over local production of fake products
World.content:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, has raised the alarm over the activities of alleged Chinese counterfeit syndicates that have shifted from importing fake products into Nigeria to establishing local manufacturing and distribution networks.

The agency’s Director of Investigation and Enforcement, Martins Iluyomade, disclosed this while speaking on recent intelligence gathered by NAFDAC on the counterfeit trade.

Iluyomade said investigations showed that some foreign nationals allegedly involved in counterfeiting were now establishing manufacturing facilities and logistics networks in Nigeria to produce and distribute fake products locally.

“Before, to fake a product, you needed to go to China to bring it. Now, they are here with us,” he said.

He added: “They identify moving products, send samples to China, and distribute them locally through logistics companies they own.”

According to Iluyomade, NAFDAC has commenced the systematic closure of illegal logistics facilities allegedly operated by foreign nationals linked to the counterfeit network.

The development comes amid concerns over the circulation of dangerous and substandard consumer products, including adulterated toothpaste, contaminated bottled water, fake cosmetics and unwholesome dairy products.

The Director-General of NAFDAC, Prof. Mojisola Adeyeye, said the agency had confiscated and destroyed regulated products worth more than N1.5 trillion during coordinated enforcement operations in Lagos and the South-East.

Adeyeye also disclosed that the enforcement campaign had resulted in 64 convictions of counterfeiters between June 2025 and June 2026, describing the figure as the highest number recorded by the agency.

She said one of the convictions resulted in a five-year prison sentence for an operator of an illegal beverage laboratory in December.

NAFDAC further disclosed that legal proceedings were ongoing at federal courts against several suspects arrested in Kano, Sokoto, Delta and Anambra states over the alleged importation and distribution of fake oral-care products.

The agency said it would continue to strengthen surveillance and enforcement activities to curb the production, distribution and sale of counterfeit and unwholesome regulated products in the country.

World.title: Dangote drove my mom home from hospital after my birth – Davido
World.content:
Afrobeats star, David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, has revealed billionaire businessman Aliko Dangote’s longstanding relationship with his family.

The artiste made the revelation while speaking about his relationship with Dangote during a recent interview in Lagos.

According to him, Dangote had maintained a close relationship with his family for decades and had continued to offer him financial advice from childhood.

“Aliko Dangote drove my mom home from the hospital when she gave birth to me,” he said.

He said Dangote had remained consistent in advising him to save and manage his money whenever they met.

“Anytime I see him, he still tells me, ‘David, save your money.’ He’s been saying that since I was a baby,” he said.

Davido said Dangote’s advice had remained relevant as he navigated his career in the entertainment industry.

The “Fall” crooner also described billionaires as ordinary people despite their enormous wealth, saying their lifestyles were often different from public perception.

He also said that Dangote was a close associate of his father, businessman Adedeji Adeleke, noting that the relationship between the two families had lasted decades.

The singer said his relationship with the billionaire businessman dated back to his childhood and has continued into his adulthood.

(NAN)

World.title: FG Settles CATA Allowance for Academic Staff of Tertiary Institutions, Says Minister
World.content:
The Federal Government has settled the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance (CATA) for academic staff of universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, from January to August 2026.

The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, disclosed this to newsmen on Wednesday in Abuja.

Alausa said the affected institutions, including Federal Universities of Agriculture, had been notified to commence payment of the allowance to their academic staff.

He said the government was also working to provide funds for the payment of CATA to non-academic staff, expressing optimism that the funds would be made available within the next few weeks.

He said the development was another indication of President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to the welfare and well-being of academic and non-academic staff in the country.

The minister said the Federal Government was not only prioritising the welfare of workers in tertiary institutions, but was also investing significantly in infrastructure across tertiary, post-basic and basic education institutions.

According to him, Tinubu’s administration believes strongly in education and is committed to ensuring that every Nigerian child has access to quality education comparable to what obtains anywhere in the world.

“This is a president that believes so much in education. So far, he has delivered beyond his campaign promises by ensuring that every single child in this country gets the highest quality of education that is comparable to anywhere in the world,” he said.

Alausa thanked Tinubu for what he described as his “transformative interventions” in the education sector. (NAN)

World.title: South-west ​‌⁠⁠​‍⁠⁠‌‍‍‍‌​​‌⁠‌​Rail Network Moves Closer to Reality As SWDC Secures Provisional Licence
World.content:
The South West Development Commission (SWDC) has secured a provisional licence to establish a comprehensive regional passenger and freight rail network connecting the six states of the South-west.

The Managing Director of SWDC, Dr Charles Akinola, disclosed this during a strategic meeting with regional stakeholders held at Cocoa House in Ibadan on Monday.

Akinola said that the commission would collaborate with Odu’a Investment Company Ltd. and the Development Agenda for Western Nigeria (DAWN) Commission to develop an interconnected rail system capable of facilitating passenger movement and freight transportation across the region.

“We have secured provisional licence for rail for freight and passengers.

“We will work with Odu’a and DAWN to connect the South-west with rail,” he said in a statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) in Ibadan on Tuesday.

The SWDC boss said that the commission was also exploring other major infrastructure initiatives, including energy security and an integrated road transportation system.

“We are also planning energy security for the region.

“We are looking at constructing a road that will link Ore in Ondo State to the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway for integrated transportation to open up the region.

“We are thinking of establishment of a South-west infrastructure development fund to complement the Federal Government’s funding,” he said.

Akinola said the commission was open to partnerships that would help revive the developmental vision associated with the region’s founding leaders, including Chief Obafemi Awolowo and Alhaji Lateef Jakande.

He commended the management of Odu’a Investment Company for repositioning the organisation and delivering billions of naira in dividends to its owner states.

The SWDC boss also described the Association of Retired Heads of Service and Permanent Secretaries in the South-west as critical stakeholders whose experience could contribute to regional development.

Also, the Regional President of the association, Mr. Demola Badejo, said the meeting was aimed at exploring areas of partnership and cooperation between the association and the three institutions.

Badejo said the association presented copies of its publication on a proposed economic development plan for the South-west to Odu’a Investment Company and SWDC as its contribution to the region’s development conversation.

He said the association was particularly pleased that the DAWN Commission collaborated in producing the publication.

Badejo described Odu’a Investment Company as a symbol of the collective economic interests and aspirations of the South-west states.

According to him, ongoing efforts are on to reposition the company, unlock the value of its assets and maximise their benefits to the people.

He also acknowledged DAWN Commission’s role in promoting regional integration, collaboration and coordinated development among the six South-west states.

He described the emergence of SWDC and its mandate as providing “a new and important platform” for coordinated intervention, infrastructure development and other developmental initiatives across the region.

On his part, the Director-General of DAWN Commission, Dr Oluseye Oyeleye, said the region’s forebears demonstrated “audacity of thinking” through projects such as Cocoa House, Liberty Stadium, Odu’a Investment Company and the first television station in Africa.

Oyeleye said that the vision of the region’s founding leaders was focused on the next generation rather than the next election cycle.

“What our forebears did is audacity of thinking; they were not thinking of the next election but the next generation and taking the region to another level,” D-G said.

He identified Odu’a Investment Company, SWDC and DAWN Commission as key institutions in shaping the future of the South-west region and advocated a shift from divisive politics to “politics of development”.

Oyeleye also disclosed that DAWN Commission had collaborated with Egbe Omo Odu’a in the diaspora to establish funds for start-up capital for businesses across the region.

He said applications were being invited from interested beneficiaries.

The meeting was attended by stakeholders including the Group Managing Director of Odu’a Investment Company, Mr Yinusa Abdulraman; Badejo; Oyeleye and other regional development stakeholders. (NAN)

World.title: 2027: Katsina Assembly Endorses Radda’s Re-election
World.content:
Francis Sardauna in Katsina

The Katsina State House of Assembly has endorsed Governor Dikko Umaru Radda for a second term and pledged its support for his re-election in the 2027 governorship election.

The Speaker of the House, Hon. Nasir Yahaya Daura, revealed the Assembly’s position on Tuesday during the presentation of the N828.64 billion 2027 Appropriation Bill by Governor Radda at the Assembly Chamber in Katsina.

He also pledged the commitment of the lawmakers to give the proposed budget speedy consideration and passage to enable the government to sustain the implementation of its programmes and projects across the state.

He described the budget presentation as significant, being the final budget of Radda’s first tenure and the last budget to be presented before the expiration of the 8th Assembly.

The speaker said the executive and legislature had maintained a cordial working relationship over the past four years, which, he noted, had contributed to developments in infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture, security and human capital development.

Daura said: “On behalf of honourable members, I appreciate Your Excellency for your support to this House. We also commend you for the developmental projects and programmes across the state.”

He noted that the 8th Assembly had passed more than 50 bills, considered several motions and carried out oversight functions aimed at promoting the interests of the people.

He assured the governor that the House would carefully scrutinise the 2027 budget and pass it within the shortest possible time.

He further declared the Assembly’s support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and other candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 general election.

Daura said the occasion would be his last time receiving Governor Radda as Speaker of the 8th Assembly, expressing gratitude to God for the opportunity to serve the state.

He urged returning and newly elected lawmakers to remain united and committed to the development of Katsina State, while sustaining cooperation between the legislature and executive.

He prayed for God’s guidance, protection and success for Governor Radda in his bid for a second term.

World.title: Northwest ADC Governorship Candidates Sign Regional Compact, Pledge Joint Action on Security, Devt
World.content:
*Seven candidates unveil four-year plan targeting insecurity, food crisis, education, healthcare, jobs and regional economic integration

*Back Atiku’s promise to reverse removal of fuel subsidy

*Pledge N110k minimum wage for workers in region

The seven governorship candidates of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Nigeria’s Northwest have signed a regional development compact aimed at tackling insecurity, poverty, food insecurity, unemployment and weak human development through coordinated action across the seven states.

The Northwest ADC Governorship Candidates’ Compact 2027–2031, was adopted and signed on Wednesday by the party’s governorship candidates from Sabo Mohammed Nakudu (Jigawa), Isa Mohammed Ashiru (Kaduna), Ibrahim Ali Amin (Kano), Ahmad Babba Kaita (Katsina), Abubakar Malami SAN (Kebbi), Manir Muhammad Dan’iya (Sokoto) and Bilyaminu Shinkafi (Zamfara).

As a commitment to the pursuit of these ideals, the governorship candidates announced the establishment of a Central Coordination Committee chaired by Rt Hon Abdussamad Dasuki;

Technical Committee chaired by Maj Gen Aminu Bande (rtd) and co-chaired by Prof. Sadiq Abubakar; and Media and Strategic Communications Committee co-chaired by Salihu Tanko Yakasai.

The document sets out a common governance framework for the candidates if elected in the 2027 elections, with commitments covering security, agriculture, education, healthcare, youth employment, infrastructure, trade, industrialisation and public accountability.

The candidates said the initiative was based on the recognition that many of the region’s most serious problems do not stop at state boundaries and therefore require coordinated solutions.

“Seven states. One regional purpose. Governing together where together works better,” the candidates said in the Compact.

The proposed arrangement would not replace the constitutional responsibilities of individual states. Rather, each state would retain responsibility for its budgets, procurement, civil service, education, healthcare, agriculture, land administration, internally generated revenue and infrastructure within its boundaries, while the governors would collaborate on issues where joint action could produce better results.

The Compact comes against the backdrop of a prolonged security and humanitarian crisis affecting communities across the Northwest.

The document cites more than 16,000 fatalities recorded between June 2023 and August 2026 and 1,583 kidnapping events across the region since January 2023, involving more than 10,000 reported abductees.

It also points to widespread displacement and the abandonment of productive agricultural land in parts of the region, including about 533,000 hectares reported abandoned in Zamfara and Katsina.

The candidates argue that insecurity has become closely linked to other economic and social problems, creating a cycle in which unsafe communities lead to abandoned farms, reduced food production, higher food prices, school disruption and increased vulnerability among young people.

The Compact summarises the cycle as: insecurity, empty farms, hunger, children out of school, recruitable youth and insecurity.

“One crisis deepens every other. A regional problem demands a regional response,” the candidates said.

The document also raises questions about the relationship between public spending and citizens’ living conditions.

It estimates that the seven Northwest states and their 186 local government areas received approximately N8.33 trillion in FAAC allocations between June 2023 and August 2026, excluding other Federal Government interventions and special transfers.

The candidates sharply criticised the performance of the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led administrations currently governing the seven Northwest states.

They accused the administrations of presiding over what they described as massive and unprecedented looting of public resources, alleging that the region had little to show for the funds entrusted to its governments.

The candidates said the alleged failure was visible in the condition of public infrastructure, the security situation and the living standards of ordinary citizens.

“The level of looting witnessed across the Northwest under the current administrations is massive and unprecedented in the region,” the candidates said.

They further alleged that the APC-led governments had “little or nothing to show for their stewardship, neither in the lives of our people, physical infrastructure nor the security of lives and property.”

According to the candidates, the region’s worsening economic conditions stood in sharp contrast to what they described as the conspicuous affluence of some serving governors.

They accused current governors of spending public resources on new government houses, exotic vehicles and private-jet travel while large sections of the population struggle with poverty.

The ADC candidates said their Compact was intended to establish a different standard of public leadership.

The candidates said public resources must translate into measurable improvements in household welfare.

“The question is no longer simply what government receives. The question is what citizens can see, access and afford as a result,” they said.

Security is the first major pillar of the Compact, with the candidates proposing the establishment of 21 command-and-control centres, one in every senatorial district across the seven states, linked to state security structures and a proposed Northwest Regional Security Coordination Centre.

The proposed architecture would combine lawful aerial surveillance, drone-enabled vigilance, community intelligence, emergency reporting and geospatial information to improve early warning and response.

The candidates have also proposed a three-minute rapid-response activation standard for verified security alerts.

Under the plan, security information would move through a sequence of surveillance, early warning, verification, command and control and rapid response.

The candidates also propose protected agricultural corridors, where security arrangements would be coordinated with the return of farmers to high-risk production areas.

They said the ultimate objective was to restore normal economic activity rather than treat security as an isolated issue.

Security must mean more than military operations. It must mean that a farmer can reach his field, a trader can travel safely, a child can get to school and a family can live without fear, the candidates said.

Under its household protection, another element of the proposed programme, the candidates pledged to implement a N110,000 minimum wage for government workers across the seven states and said economic reforms would be accompanied by measures aimed at cushioning vulnerable households.

Under their five systems that guarantee prosperity, they listed Agriculture and Food, Education and Human Capital, Health Security, infrastructure and Integration, Youth, Enterprise and Jobs.

On infrastructure and integration, the candidates pledged to prioritise regional infrastructure (roads, rail network), independent power generation, solar power for public facilities, water systems, digital backbone and the border and logistics infrastructure which trade depends on. In the area of health security, they promised to ensure full access to the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF), revitalize primary health care centers, expand midwives, telemedicine and community health insurance deployment, and establish one specialist hospital in each senatorial district (21 region wide)

On Youth, Enterprise and Jobs, the candidates pledged to coordinate access to a Regional Youth Fund, prioritize Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), establish digital hubs, formalize MSME and facilitate access to development finance. The seven governorship candidates also promised to declare emergency on education, secure full UBEC access, integrate Almajiri and Tsangaya children into formal schools, support girls’ school attendance, and build a credible system for teacher recruitment, continuous training and mopping up out-of-school children.

For Agriculture and Food, they promised to ensure more land is safely farmed, strengthening of food security through protected agricultural corridors, formalised livestock production, agro-processing, a regional grain reserve and irrigation rehabilitation.

The candidates also called for the release of formernKadina State Governor, am Mallam Nasiru El Rufai.

World.title: Buses, Thrones And Talent: Inside Uba Sani’s Latest Three-Way Governance Strategy
World.content:
By Nasir Dambatta

Three announcements. One signature.

In a matter of days, Governor Uba Sani handed out CNG-powered buses, raised the pay scale for Kaduna’s traditional rulers, and put N3 million directly into the hands of the state’s top young innovators.

Taken separately, they look like familiar administrative announcements. But set against Kaduna’s N985.9 billion 2026 “Budget of Consolidation,” we see a clearer pattern: rewarding the institutions that keep public life running, supporting the traditional authority that keeps the peace at ground level, and putting money directly into the hands of the young people who will inherit the state.

Buses: Supporting THE Institutions That Hold Society Together

It started with mobility.

On September 1, Governor Sani rolled out CNG-powered transit buses for five institutions he described as indispensable: the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), Nigerian Bar Association (NBA), Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), Nigerian Correctional Service (NCS), and Kaduna State University (KASU). How many key areas? Healthcare, justice, the media, correctional centres and higher education — five pillars, one gesture.

“These institutions occupy indispensable positions in our society,” Governor Uba Sani said, describing the vehicles as a practical boost to how these bodies do their day-to-day work.

And, the response was immediate! Professional bodies welcomed the buses as a direct lift to service delivery. The message is plain: the administration is choosing to work with the professionals who keep the state running.

Thrones: Strengthening The First Line Of Defence

Effective September 1, Uba Sani approved a new salary and allowance structure for emirs, chiefs, district heads, and village heads across Kaduna’s three senatorial districts — backed by monthly security allowances for all 35 emirates and chiefdoms.

The reasoning, laid out by Commissioners Sadiq Mamman Lagos and Ahmed Maiyaki, comes down to a simple fact: traditional leaders sit closer to ordinary people than any government office ever will. That closeness makes them Kaduna’s earliest warning system against local trouble and rural disputes.

Now, combine the boost to the traditional institutions with a grassroots development push that channels N100 million into each of Kaduna’s 255 political wards, and you get a powerful outcome. Also, these allowances turn community institutions into active partners in keeping the peace. As ALGON’s Kaduna chapter put it, traditional rulers are governance anchors on the ground.

Talent: Putting Money Into The State’s Next Generation

The third latest governance strategy looks further ahead. At the 2026 International Youth Day Conference, Governor Sani handed N3 million each to a group of standout technology and science innovators.The money went to real, working breakthroughs: First,

the Ahmadu Bello University (ABU) Zaria team that built an assistive walking aid for the visually impaired.

Second, was the commercial Astronaut candidate Fauziyya Muhammad Auwal.

We also have eight state-trained microchip design specialists.

Add that to the ‘NEXTGEN Challenge’ AI winners, Malam Amin Mohammed Idris and Malam Shamsudeen Jibril.

Governor Uba Sani’s cash support is backed by structural moves too, including a new Ministry of Youth Development and three vocational skills centres across Rigachikun, Zango Kataf, and Soba.

His message was simple: build positively beyond the limits you inherited, and use technology to get around the economic friction holding young people back.Talent needs funding support, or else it will die out.

The Bigger Picture

CNG transport for professionals. Better pay and security funding for traditional rulers. Direct cash for rising technical talent.

This isn’t three unrelated actions. It’s one approach playing out in three ways: strengthen the professionals running daily operations, support the traditional structures keeping the peace, and fund the young people driving the state’s next stage of growth.

The N985.9 billion budget lays out the numbers on paper. Moves like these show what that budget looks like in practice. Heading into 2027, they offer a clearer picture of how Uba Sani intends to govern.

*Dambatta is Senior Special Assistant on Print Media to the Governor

World.title: 49.7kg Heroin: NDLEA Arrests Fugitive Drug Kingpin After Two Years on the Run
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested and repatriated Festus Ibewuike, alias Chidibest Ibewuike, a suspected drug kingpin who had been on the run for more than two years following the seizure of 49.7 kilogrammes of heroin at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Lagos.

Ibewuike, 52, was arrested at the airport in Cotonou, Benin Republic, on September 2, 2026, following actionable intelligence and coordinated efforts between the NDLEA and INTERPOL authorities in Nigeria and Benin.

He was subsequently handed over to NDLEA operatives deployed in Cotonou on September 4 and brought back to Nigeria to face prosecution over his alleged role in the trafficking syndicate behind what the agency described as the largest single heroin consignment ever intercepted at the Lagos airport.

The suspect had reportedly relocated to Mozambique, where he operated a hotel business allegedly used as a cover, while making efforts to evade Nigerian law enforcement by moving between Mozambique and Nigeria through neighbouring Benin Republic.

His arrest followed a 12-day operation by operatives of the NDLEA MMIA Strategic Command in February 2024, during which 49.70kg of heroin was intercepted at the airport’s cargo terminal.

The spokesman of the NDLEA, Femi Babafemi, in a statement on Wednesday, said the drugs were concealed in cartons containing metal-cutting machines and marked with the code ‘ND’.

Investigations subsequently linked the parcels to Ibewuike, who allegedly operated through members of a wider trafficking network.

The operation led to the arrest of several members of the syndicate, including his wife, Confidence Ndidiamaka Ibewuike, who investigators said routinely received drug-laden consignments on his behalf.

He said the agency also secured the freezing of 107 bank accounts and forfeiture of properties allegedly connected to the cartel.

He revealed that the suspects were charged before Justice Ambrose Lewis-Allagoa of the Federal High Court, Ikoyi, Lagos, in charge number FHC/L/205C/2024.

He said the suspects — Adinnu Felix Chinedu, Osita Emmanuel Obinna and Uzochukwu Frankline — have so far been convicted and sentenced by the court.

He further noted others — Chidiebere Peter, Ibewuike Ndidiamaka and Igbokwuputa Onyinye — are still standing trial, while Ibewuike Festus, Osita Chidozie Cyril and another suspect identified as Arinze were charged in absentia.

Following his repatriation, Ibewuike reportedly confirmed his identity during preliminary interviews and disclosed that he had changed his name from Chidibest Ibewuike to Festus Ibewuike.

On September 5, he was taken to the NDLEA Central Exhibit Store in Ikoyi, Lagos, where he formally identified the heroin parcels bearing the ‘ND’ code, which the agency said had been established as being linked to him.

Further investigation also uncovered his alleged connection to an earlier drug case involving the seizure of 40.255kg of methamphetamine.

The earlier case was prosecuted before the Federal High Court, Lagos, under Justice Hadiza Rabiu Shagari in charge number FHC/L/203C/2013. One Chidi Ihedioha, who was prosecuted in connection with the case, was convicted by the court in 2023.

Reacting to the latest development, the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the NDLEA, Brig. Gen. Buba Marwa (rtd), described Ibewuike’s arrest as a major breakthrough in the agency’s campaign against fleeing drug kingpins.

Marwa warned drug traffickers who flee the country to escape prosecution that international borders would not shield them from justice.

“This arrest is a major breakthrough in our resolve to track down and bring to justice every drug baron who thinks that fleeing Nigeria’s shores puts them beyond the reach of the law,” he said.

He added: “As I have always vowed, the long arm of the NDLEA will catch up with anyone involved in this illicit trade, no matter how long it takes or how far they run.”

According to him, Ibewuike’s more than two-year flight, including his alleged change of identity and relocation abroad, had not prevented the agency from tracking him down.

“This should serve as a fresh warning to fleeing suspects still at large: the Agency will not relent until everyone of you is brought to book,” Marwa said.

The NDLEA chairman commended the multinational cooperation that facilitated the arrest and transfer, particularly the Nigerian and Beninese INTERPOL National Central Bureaus, for their role in ensuring the smooth handover of the suspect.

The agency said the development further demonstrated its determination to pursue suspected drug traffickers beyond Nigeria’s borders and ensure that fleeing suspects are eventually brought before the law.

World.title: Okpella Council Canvasses Peace, Dismisses Akemokue’s Claims
World.content:
The Okpella Traditional Council in Etsako East Local Government Area of Edo State has urged residents and the general public to embrace peace and disregard what it described as recurring misleading narratives surrounding the Okuokpellagbe traditional stool, insisting that the community’s focus should remain on unity, development and stability.

Addressing journalists in a statement on Wednesday, the council’s spokesman, Chief Hanson Aimofumeh, said the statement was issued in response to a recent viral post by Lukman Akemokue, who, according to him, continued to present himself as the Okuokpellagbe of Okpella despite pending appeals over the traditional stool.

He maintained that the community deserved “peace and progress, not recurring campaigns of falsehood, self-promotion and unfounded claims”.

Aimofumeh stated that Mike Sado remained the recognised Okuokpellagbe of Okpella, adding that he continued to enjoy the support of the community as well as recognition by the relevant authorities.

“The public should ignore the misleading narratives being circulated by Lukman Akemokue. Engr. Mike Sado remains the recognised Okuokpellagbe of Okpella and will continue to work with government, stakeholders and the people to preserve the peace, unity and dignity of the kingdom,” he said.

The spokesman acknowledged that the dispute over the traditional stool remained before the courts, noting that appeals arising from the High Court judgment were yet to be determined by the Court of Appeal.

He said all parties should allow the judicial process to run its course rather than engage in public campaigns capable of heightening tension within the community.

Aimofumeh also rejected allegations reportedly made against Mike Sado concerning a recent stakeholders’ meeting convened by the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, describing the claims as unsubstantiated.

He said the council believed such issues should be addressed through the appropriate legal and administrative channels rather than in the media.

According to him, the traditional institution under Sado had continued to promote peace, security and development in Okpella, urging all stakeholders to support initiatives capable of fostering harmony instead of deepening divisions.

He said the council remained committed to working with government and other relevant institutions in the interest of the community.

The spokesman further stated that Akemokue had filed a cross-appeal in the matter pending before the Court of Appeal, arguing that the legal process should be respected by all parties until a final decision is reached.

He said the council remained confident that due process would ultimately resolve the dispute.

The palace spokeperson however appealed to residents to remain law-abiding and avoid actions or statements capable of undermining peace in Okpella.

He reiterated that the council’s priority was the unity, dignity and development of the kingdom, urging members of the public to disregard narratives which, according to him, could create unnecessary confusion while the matter remains before the courts.

World.title: PDP Inaugurates 2027 Campaign in Abia
World.content:
Boniface Okoro in Umuahia

The Abia State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) yesterday inaugurated the management team of its Campaign Council for the 2027 governorship election.

The Campaign Council Management Team, which has former Nigerian Ambassador to Argentina, Empire Kanu, as chairman and Chief Obinna Nwachukwu as director-general, was inaugurated by the team’s Secretary, Ukpai Ukairo, at the campaign office of the party’s flag bearer, Dr. Kelechi Anosike, on Aba Road, Umuahia.

The brief ceremony set the tone for what PDP leaders described as a grassroots-driven and issue-based campaign to “reclaim the soul and future of Abia State.”

The Chairman of the Campaign Council, Kanu, declared that Abia remains a PDP state and that the current Labour Party administration is holding power temporarily.

Kanu said: “PDP is not a new party. PDP is Abia State; Abia State is PDP. Labour is just holding that position temporarily.

“We knew what happened (in 2023) and that mistake will never happen again. You have a very serious candidate in the person of this young man, Dr. Anosike. He is very, very ready.”

He commended Anosike for setting up a befitting campaign structure within weeks, saying it was a sign of the seriousness and organisation he would bring to governance.

“When he takes over, Abia State will move to a different level. He has a deputy, Elder Amah Abraham, who is experienced politically, administratively, and also very, very ready to move to the State House,” he said.

The campaign council chairman charged members to focus their energy at the ward level.

“You know where we normally get our votes? It’s at the ward level. So that is where we should work. Once you deliver at the ward, we have won. You have been appointed to make sure that every ward in this state is delivered to PDP. We don’t want any excuse at all. By His grace, we are moving to Government House,” he stated.

He added that the present state government and its party “are standing on very shaky ground,” arguing that without a strong party structure, “I don’t see how you can run.”

In his address, the PDP governorship candidate, Anosike, said the inauguration marked the beginning of a movement anchored on welfare and service.

Anosike declared: “For me, we have started a journey. And the journey is to reclaim the soul and future of our state. A journey to end deceit and fraud in our state.

“This is not just the inauguration of the campaign council. This is more like commencing a movement. A movement that believes ‘People First, Abia Always’.” He charged council members to take the message of welfarism to every community.

“I’m addressing those who will translate and convey this message to every nook and cranny of the state, to every local government, every village, every community and every ward,” he stated.

Anosike said the campaign would be devoid of insults and hatred, and would instead be a “referendum of ideas.”

“We’re not giving the masses general campaign promises or rhetoric. We are going into specifics: that if before now, you don’t have food to eat, when Anosike comes, you have more than enough to eat. If our youths don’t have opportunities, when Anosike comes, there will be opportunities everywhere, because we will establish, at least, three industries in one year. It is possible,” he added.

Addressing the issue of PDP’s 24-year rule, he said: “When they tell you that PDP killed Abia State for 24 years, tell them that those actors are no longer in PDP. They are in Labour, APC, ADC, NDC. This is a new PDP. The same party, new mindset, new focus, new direction.”

The Director General of the Campaign Council, Chief Nwachukwu, pledged total commitment from the team.

“Thank you for this honour given to my team and me. I promise you, on behalf of all of us, that we are going to be committed and be intentional,” Nwachukwu said.

The Abia State PDP chairman and the deputy governorship candidate, Elder Amah, was present at the inauguration of the team, which comprises many other members. They were presented with the PDP flags.

World.title: Woolworths store under investigation after maggots discovery [video]
World.content:
Woolworths are investigating a store where maggots were found in the raw chicken section. Images via Facebook

A Woolworths store is under investigation after a video of maggots found in the fridge section containing raw chicken went viral.

The incident took place at the Bel Air shopping centre in Johannesburg.

WOOLWORTHS INVESTIGATING MAGGOTS FOUND IN FRIDGE

On Facebook, user John Mawere posted a video clip of a gruesome discovery inside his local Woolworths food store.



In it were dead maggots in the fridge section where stacks of raw chicken had been packed.

He said in the video: “I have always been a loyal Woolies customer. I buy from Woolies because I have trusted the brand to deliver quality, freshness and high standards. So imagine my shock and disgust when I found MAGGOTS in the shelves at Woolies Belair. This is more than just a disappointing shopping experience. It is a serious food-quality and customer-trust issue.

He continued: “When you pay a premium for a brand like Woolies, you are not just buying a product – you are buying the confidence that the food you take home has been handled and supplied to the standards you expect. A brand is built on trust. It only takes one experience like this to seriously damage it” 

Mawere demanded answers from the retailer on how and why the safety hazard had occurred, as well as how they planned to rectify it.

Responding to the complaints, Woolworths stated that the store was under investigation following the viral video.

It shared in a statement: “Independent hygiene experts were called to the store, all products were removed, and a deep clean was initiated.



“This is a unique and isolated incident which has triggered a full, ongoing investigation to determine the root cause. The store in question had recently been audited from a hygiene perspective, and no anomalies were detected.

Woolworths stated that it was deeply committed to the highest standards of hygiene and food safety across its entire operation.

“We recognise that we have let our customers down on this occasion and sincerely apologise. We are taking every measure to ensure this does not happen again.”



RAT ATTACK

It’s not the first time a Woolworths customer has made a disturbing discovery in a store.

In 2023, a female shopper discovered a live rat in the frozen chicken section of her local Gardens Shopping Centre store in Cape Town.

After the video found its way onto the X platform, the retailer replied to the social media backlash. In a statement issued to The South African, Woolworths profusely apologised to its shoppers.



It stated of their actions: “The store immediately underwent a forensic deep clean and was closed early to allow for a thorough investigation.”

Other shoppers have allegedly found worms, cockroaches, and even snakes in stores and in their items!

World.title: Rape in police cells and graveyards: The shocking SA crime stats
World.content:
South Africa’s most recent quarterly crime statistics contain a detail that’s easy to miss. It’s buried among the bigger headline numbers, but once you see it, it’s hard to look away.

The fourth-quarter crime statistics cover January to March 2026.

They revealed that 34 rape cases were reported nationally in police holding cells and deportation centres, with the Western Cape recording the highest number at eight.



Where these cases were reported

The statistics, released by Acting Police Minister Firoz Cachalia, break the numbers down by location in a way that’s genuinely uncomfortable to read.

Gauteng recorded five holding-cell and deportation-centre cases, while the Eastern Cape, Free State, KwaZulu-Natal and Limpopo each recorded four.

The Western Cape also topped the list for rapes reported in graveyards.

Of the 26 cases recorded nationally, six happened there, followed by the Eastern Cape with five and the Free State with four.

The province further recorded the highest number of rape cases on agricultural land, including farms, plots and smallholdings.

For context, the vast majority of cases still happen at home.



A total of 4 620 rape cases were reported in homes nationally, 547 of them in the Western Cape alone, so these unusual locations remain a small fraction of the overall picture.

But their existence at all says something troubling about just how unsafe South Africa can feel, even in spaces meant to offer some form of custody or protection.

A system already struggling to keep up

These statistics have landed alongside a separate, related concern: rape kit shortages at several police stations.

DA representative Nicholas Gotsell said an oversight visit to stations on the Cape Flats found the Nyanga Family Violence, Child Protection and Sexual Offences unit had no usable rape evidence kits in stock, with some already expired.

He described the shortages as pointing to a “deeply concerning collapse” in the police’s supply chain.

Sino Mdunjeni of Rape Crisis Cape Town Trust explained why these kits matter so much. Forensic examinations and evidence collection depend on them.

She warned that shortages can delay survivors’ access to medical care and psychosocial support.

They can also discourage people from reporting sexual violence at all, especially those who already face real barriers to coming forward.

I’ve always kept a close eye on these stats.

But a few of these locations genuinely surprised me.

Police stations, places you’d expect to feel safe, alongside a shortage of rape kits meant to secure justice for survivors.

It shows just how far South Africa has let this slip.

Nobody is reporting it with anywhere near the urgency it deserves.

As a woman living in this country, I have to ask: are we safe anywhere anymore?

Did this specific detail surprise you as much as it did us?

Let us know in the comments below…

World.title: Why emergency measures are being introduced at a popular Mossel Bay beach
World.content:
Authorities are taking urgent action as coastal erosion continues to threaten part of one of Mossel Bay's best-known beaches. Image: wikimedia commons

Authorities have agreed on emergency measures to address the serious and ongoing coastal erosion threatening Mossel Bay’s Diaz Beach, with temporary sandbags set to be installed to reduce the immediate risk of further collapse.

The Western Cape Government and Mossel Bay Municipality have reached an agreement on interim measures aimed at protecting people, properties and public infrastructure in the affected area.

The Mossel Bay Municipality has proposed installing geotextile sandbags to stabilise the dune and reduce the immediate danger posed by continued erosion.



Emergency measure to reduce the risk at Diaz Beach

According to the Western Cape Department of Environmental Affairs and Development Planning, the temporary intervention is intended to prevent further damage to properties and infrastructure.

It will also help reduce risks to members of the public accessing parts of the area, which authorities have warned remain unsafe.

However, officials have stressed that the sandbags are not a permanent solution to Diaz Beach’s erosion problems.



“The Mossel Bay Municipality and the Western Cape Government are in agreement that a permanent solution for improved coastal management at Diaz Beach needs to be implemented,” department spokesperson Rudolf van Jaarsveldt said.

A Basic Assessment process is currently underway and will help determine the most appropriate long-term solution.

Sandbags could eventually be removed

While the emergency intervention has been approved, environmental authorities have warned that coastal protection measures can affect the natural movement of sand between dunes, beaches and the nearshore environment.



If poorly designed or managed, such measures can contribute to further erosion, beach narrowing and even the loss of parts of the beach as a public amenity.

Environmental Affairs and Development Planning MEC Anton Bredell has decided to abide by a court order allowing the sandbags to be installed as an urgent temporary measure.

The longer-term solution will be determined through the environmental assessment process in the coming months.



This could ultimately include removing the sandbags, while other options, including sand replenishment, may also be considered.

Authorities say the emergency measures are aimed at managing the immediate danger, but the bigger challenge is finding a sustainable solution to protect Diaz Beach in the long term.

The Western Cape Government and Mossel Bay Municipality have committed to working together on both the immediate risks and longer-term interventions needed to improve coastal management in the area.

World.title: Apple’s first foldable iPhone coming to SA – but it won’t be cheap!
World.content:
The foldable handset, rumoured to be called the iPhone Duo, is expected to headline a major Apple launch event beginning at 19:00 (SA time). Image: Wikimedia Commons

Apple is expected to unveil its first-ever foldable iPhone later on Wednesday, with the highly anticipated device reportedly carrying a starting price of around $2 000 (R32 000).

The foldable handset, rumoured to be called the iPhone Duo, is expected to headline a major Apple launch event beginning at 19:00 (SA time).

The company is also expected to introduce the iPhone 18 Pro, updated Apple Watch models and new AirPods.



Hands-on with a foldable iPhone dummy unit 👀



I’m really liking this design! It feels compact and comfortable in the hand, especially when folded pic.twitter.com/xohvba5o5r — Apple Hub (@theapplehub) September 7, 2026

New era under John Ternus

The launch will also mark the first major Apple keynote for John Ternus, who became the company’s chief executive on 1 September, succeeding longtime CEO Tim Cook.

Cook has moved into the role of executive chairman.

Ternus has already hinted at the significance of the event, telling Apple employees in a memo that the company had a “huge launch” coming that would be “phenomenal”.

The pressure will be high as Ternus takes charge of one of the technology industry’s most closely watched product launches.

Foldable iPhone could cost up to $3 000

Reports suggest the entry-level foldable iPhone will feature 256GB of storage, with higher-capacity versions potentially costing around $3 000 (R48 000).



Apple is reportedly attempting to limit the impact of increased component costs, including those associated with a global memory shortage, in order to keep the starting price close to the $2 000 mark.

The device is expected to feature a shorter, wider design, broadly similar to Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold range.

Under the hood, reports indicate that Apple will use its new C2 modem alongside the A20 Pro chip.

The foldable is also expected to offer enhanced multitasking features, including side-by-side applications and an iPad-style approach to running multiple apps.

That could give Apple’s first foldable a stronger productivity focus, rather than relying solely on its novelty folding display.

What about South Africa?

Apple has not yet confirmed a South African launch date or local price for the foldable iPhone.

Some South African retailers have listed the device as “coming soon”, but without pricing information.

This suggests local customers may have to wait until after the international launch before the new iPhone becomes officially available in South Africa.

For Apple, however, Wednesday’s event represents more than another iPhone launch.
