It is the beginning of a new chapter under Ternus – and potentially the company’s biggest step into the foldable smartphone market yet.

What’s your price limit when it comes to buying a new phone?

Let us know by clicking on the comment banner below …

World.title: DEVELOPING | LIV Golf files for bankruptcy
World.content:
LIV Golf, the breakaway tour that spent billions of dollars luring top players away from the PGA Tour, has filed for bankruptcy protection. Image: LIV Golf website

LIV Golf, the breakaway tour that spent billions of dollars luring top players away from the PGA Tour and triggered bitter divisions within the sport, filed on Tuesday for bankruptcy protection.

The filing at a New Jersey court indicates LIV, which abruptly lost its deep-pocketed Saudi investors earlier this year, intends to restructure and return in a new form.

Owe 1 000 creditors

But documents show LIV owes between $500 million and $1 billion in estimated liabilities to at least 1 000 creditors, including star players like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm.



And the future of those popular players remains deeply unclear.

The likes of DeChambeau are now faced with deciding whether to remain with the tour in its new guise, or leave and attempt to pursue the millions of dollars they are owed in court.

READ | South African star gets captain’s pick for Presidents Cup

“This process gives us the structure and time to pursue a landmark transaction and begin the next chapter of LIV Golf,” said CEO Scott O’Neil, in a statement.

LIV still intends to return next year in a new form including “an innovative, player-first ownership model,” he said.

“No definitive decisions regarding the 2027 schedule or individual events are being announced at this time,” the LIV statement added.



Widely expected

The bankruptcy filing was widely expected, after LIV axed the majority of its staff earlier this month, and scrapped its season-ending team championship in August after losing the backing of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF).

Since LIV’s launch in 2022, the Middle Eastern fund had poured an estimated $5 billion into the tour, before abruptly pulling the plug.

The PIF will now provide a loan worth nearly $50 million for the bankruptcy and reorganization process, the LIV statement showed.

LIV’s star players Rahm, DeChambeau and Dustin Johnson hold the largest unsecured claims against the tour, totaling more than $5 million each in immediate past-due payments, per the bankruptcy filing.

But even those amounts do not reflect the future remaining contract values of some golfers, that can range into tens of millions of dollars each, the Financial Times reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.

Tuesday’s statement said “the Company remains in advanced discussions with” players, including on “creating an ownership structure aligning players’ interests with the League’s long-term success.”

“Players will have the opportunity to share directly in the value they help create,” said O’Neil, in an open letter to fans.

LIV did not immediately respond to AFP request for comment on the matter.

‘LIV 2.0’

Tour officials have previously pledged that a “2.0” version of the tour will re-emerge under new investors next season, with a shorter schedule and reduced prize money.

Further details emerged for the proposals on Tuesday.

LIV intends to host tournaments across five continents, in locations including Australia, South Africa, Mexico, England, Hong Kong and the US.

“We intend to expand our fields to 75 players, introduce a cut, and create additional pathways for players to earn their way into LIV Golf, including Monday qualifiers,” it said.

The emphasis would remain on courting young fans, with live music, and team competitions which will “embrace national identities, building on the passion and momentum of World Cup-style competition.”

But much will depend on whether top stars including DeChambeau and Rahm remain.

Return to the PGA Tour?

Widespread reports have linked several LIV stars with potential returns to the PGA Tour and other series, though the PGA said it currently has no plans to offer LIV players a pathway back.

Five-time major winner Brooks Koepka – who did return to the PGA this year – is still listed as a creditor owed $1.7 million on the LIV bankruptcy filing.

Tuesday’s filing confirmed LIV has partnered for the restructuring effort with British investment group BC Partners – long rumoured to be the tour’s mystery new “lead investor.”

LIV Golf is also seeking recognition of the US bankruptcy filing in England and Wales to cover its global assets, which total $100-$500 million.

By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: Transfer report: Sundowns beat Pirates to sign Bafana star Matuludi
World.content:
Thabang Matuludi in Bafana Bafana colours before the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Image: Bafana Bafana media

Sundowns have moved quickly to secure one of the most exciting full-backs in the Betway Premiership, with a deal now agreed with Rise and Shine.

According to iDiski Times journalist Lorenz Kohler, sources have confirmed that Sundowns have reached an agreement with Polokwane City for Thabang Matuludi.

DEAL AGREED FOR THABANG MATULUDI TO MAMELODI SUNDOWNS

Personal terms have also been agreed with the Bafana Bafana international, leaving only the routine medical before the transfer can be officially announced. The club have also reportedly signed Thabo Cele.



The move marks another major step in the impressive rise of Matuludi, who has gone from playing amateur football in Limpopo to becoming a Bafana Bafana international.

Born on January 14, 1999, in Dennilton, Limpopo, Matuludi started his football journey at Kgahlanamorulana Secondary School in the Sekhukhune District.

He initially played as a winger before eventually moving into a defensive fullback role while playing for his teacher’s club in Jane Furse.

His early senior career took place in the ABC Motsepe League, where he represented amateur clubs King Born and The Dolphins.

His big breakthrough came in 2021 when Polokwane City spotted his potential and brought him into the club.

Playing in the National First Division, Matuludi became an important part of the Polokwane City defence and helped the club earn promotion to the top flight ahead of the 2023/24 season.



Since then, he has established himself as a reliable and explosive right-back in the Betway Premiership.

Matuludi’s defensive strength, work rate and ability to attack from deep have made him one of the standout fullbacks in South African football.

His performances for Polokwane City eventually earned him international recognition.

He received his first senior Bafana Bafana call-up for the 2024 COSAFA Cup, making his debut against Mozambique and playing every minute of the tournament.

His form continued to impress national team coach Hugo Broos, who included him in the squad for the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations.

Matuludi then reached another major milestone when Broos selected him for South Africa’s squad at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Sundowns have reportedly beaten the competition for his signature, with Orlando Pirates also previously linked with the defender.

If he completes his medical without any issues, Matuludi will become the latest addition to an already star-studded Sundowns squad.

For a player who started out in grassroots football in Limpopo, his journey from the ABC Motsepe League to Bafana Bafana and now potentially Sundowns is a remarkable one.

World.title: Polokwane City make surprise stadium decision for Kaizer Chiefs clash
World.content:
Polokwane City are set to host Kaizer Chiefs at the Old Peter Mokaba Stadium despite the new stadium being available to use.

Rise and Shine are looking to get the best out of Saturday’s match and a smaller venue could suite them better than Amakhosi.

Fernando Da Cruz’s carpet football would have suited Kaizer Chiefs better at the new Peter Mokaba Stadium.



The stadium was not available to use during the opening rounds of the 2026/27 season but Polokwane municipality’s manager for Sport and Recreation, Mantlako Sebaka confimed to iDiski Times.

“The New Peter Mokaba Stadium is ready pitch wise, facility wise and amenity wise,” Sebaka told iDiski Times.

“So, we are good to go. And secondly, the Polokwane City football club match against Kaizer Chiefs football club is going to be played at the old stadium, a decision that was taken by the club together with the PSL.

“For us we had hoped that the match could be played in the new stadium but nevertheless Polokwane City is a club member of the PSL and Polokwane municipality is not a club member.

“We are just a host city discharging our responsibility of ensuring that the people of Polokwane and the surrounding they get to enjoy the sport and sport development in general.”

Kaizer Chiefs looking for another win

Amakhosi travel to Polokwane to play Rise and Shine on Saturday afternoon looking to push pressure on rivals Mamelodi Sundowns and Orlando Pirates.



Kickoff for Saturday’s match is at 15:00.

Can Amakhosi get another win or will Polokwane City contain them?

World.title: What comes next for Springboks after All Blacks series?
World.content:
There won’t be much time for rest once the Springboks wrap up their gruelling series against the All Blacks in Baltimore this Saturday.

Straight after concluding Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series, the Springboks will head to Australia to begin preparing for a one-off Test against Australia in Perth on 27 September.

A number of first-choice players who have carried a heavy workload during the series against New Zealand will be rested for the match against Australia, but it will provide an opportunity for others to bank some important game-time.



The likes of Grant Williams, Franco Mostert, Canan Moodie and Handre Pollard will all be set to return to action after missing various parts of this season due to frustrating injuries.

Others such as Aphelele Fassi, Cameron Hanekom, Paul de Villiers, Boan Venter, Jan-Hendrik Wessels and Johan Grobbelaar will all aim to get some more minutes under their belt, and to hopefully make an impression before the end-of-year tour.

That period will see the Springboks finish off the year against Italy, France, Ireland before another match during the ‘finals weekend’ of the Nations Championship.

Lots for Springboks to look forward to

Once-off Test

Sunday 27 September: Wallabies v Boks Venue: Optus Stadium, Perth Kick off: 11:30
